body.title: Wednesday Walk - Random Sightings
body.body:
Here are a few random sightings from walks this week for this #wednesdaywalk by @tattoodjay
![1000004935.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sketch.and.jam/23uQnHnoqR1XGsfX3N7eq3xYJU37dvg1EgRSc4oHvhjcu8MyVFPXeSz8cuZczVpGAChV4.jpg)
I took my daughter to a new nature center we hadn't been to yet. They had a large tank for a common snapping turtle. The reflection was quite interesting on the water's surface from underwater. Made a perfect symmetrical view of two turtles attached by the nose. 

![1000004586.jpg](2)![1000004936.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sketch.and.jam/EoeFPsabp5eMrrH11eAx6WXoyLx82Wx68RYU79ot2GTuXg5LTPM24swPS5s7LZ42zvS.jpg)
Here's what it looked like from above. Plenty of signs saying don't stick your hand in the tank lol. 

![1000004932.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sketch.and.jam/EoiUnAcpKFVthNDtBgrpb37Ef6fJJdwdRkxShaf14iMoWWPmuLMiDCJ7XXXT46RDHpC.jpg)
They also had a tortoise enclosure. More signs on not to pet the turtle. I suspect this guy isn't quite as aggressive as the snapping turtle and would do a slow motion bite if any.

![1000004942.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sketch.and.jam/23uQnVomgAEQq6WVQGUMCMe83mvWRFmUTB1nhW3JkeDQRaEVKeYT6GFTs3yJcnMmixhWB.jpg)
We got trapped here by all the books for at least an hour. I liked the interior design and halo lighting on this leaf the most lol.

![1000004740.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sketch.and.jam/EqYkW3EYi1MNXYmUMdPGjyjt4Qse2PX62r2KAkwtKG2steLSuByZoQt6zX1fd6sdwua.jpg)
I also managed to get to an aquarium and see these strange sand worm eel thingies. My daughter has a blub blub fish book with these in it so she was excited to see they really exist.

![1000004615.jpg](1)![1000004738.jpg](6)![1000004768.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sketch.and.jam/Eoprw24Uu4pVj86qWezUedo7FABAuZ5ALxG2YTKiFZ986y6VyBENHU7Ha7W7EVW27NG.jpg)
Now for a mineral display. 

![1000004550.jpg](4)![1000004771.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sketch.and.jam/EoGvTVfph8tbLYu7B3LM6dJgyrwXHvbgYAYf6oUgnGTJHaQxHXHVNXVCzKbgwJFjjAp.jpg)
Whenever I see a nice display I take lots of pictures to save it for ideas for my job. 

![1000004775.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sketch.and.jam/EoAUN4UdGLez6HjjUmb3k7HTWbQCAK2hMuFWDTQxBCdak1hpPCYoEyZRnXhRxKAP8VF.jpg)
My daughter of course mashed the red button and I had to listen to the loud speakers with music talk about minerals. Then she mashed it again... Had to do a fast exit out of there for sanity.

![1000004766.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sketch.and.jam/EoGvWRL1EEefkgY7XSXqczNkiv9a7NjHkJ7kNHS1mM23Eqmx44A3dbZ4sBFRoiX498u.jpg)
I once had a mining project and wanted to do a feature like this for the company. But it became to expensive to get real minerals to display so they ended up just being graphics. Some of these chunks of stuff are worth more than their weight in gold. I guess it pays to be a rock hound and know what you are looking at just in case you happen to find a priceless display piece.

That's all for now, thanks for looking :-)

body.body:
This year I missed an ice drift on the Vologda River. But I don't think this is a big omission, since the ice drift here are not some kind of amazing sight.

I would like, of course, to capture the views of the city with an ice drift at night on a long exposure...but in six years, I have never managed to do this yet.

body.title: Avoid Legendary Summoner If Mana Cap Is Not On Your Favor
body.body:
Good Day Fellow Summoners

Some weeks ago, I talked about my experience using one of the Legendary Summoner from Rebellion Edition. It was Elias Max Pruitt, and his combination with Commander Slade was excellent. There ware many ways to exploits other units using this outstanding summoner, I bet by seeing his stats, you have your own version of what units you want to employ in his team.

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dewabrata/23w2DJkusQeHUE2kRzAT5eEGVdqrSzwhuy7MJpaZnyquR6R86UpTPCtViXcZEypqZCCn1.png

In this post I will not talk about using this Elias Max Pruitt to win something. In fact I do not have him in my line up this season. All my legendary summoners are rented from others, I could not afford to buy them.

So the topic is not about using this legendary summoner, but it is the opposite. Something we must avoid or refrain ourselves to use them, because of mana cap of the battle. Having 2 or 3 more mana sometime because a decisive factor, because it will have you to choose, whether having a great summoner or having the right unit needed by your team.

So lets check our battle then!


#### The Battle

[![~Click The Image Above To See the Full Battle~](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dewabrata/23tGeA4eyMzQYza1yRWFuhskYQXsPUPqF7vuqHhaogJ9JseMQvwtuJ8Q6P4CKZZ7vrSAU.png)](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_401e7dd092efc31fa324a9689fcfa2cc?ref=dewabrata)

This is the battle I choose, specifically against Elias Max Pruitt. We have 34 mana cap which is a good number, not too high and not too low, but actually it is a number that often make people confuse which units they want to go with.

As you can see, both my opponent and I choose to come with 5 units. 6 Units are too much for us, but actually there are many ways to go with 6 units but always end up with weaker line up or lousy ones.

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dewabrata/23tkmzFPhi3KWy56egLRVyGcUf6tnTvCJow9KcosoNTfsHvtfAJL13pV5tNXvNqL7PKRJ.png

The reason is this Heavy Metal modifier. It makes us unable to pick units without armor. It seems simple but it is not, many of \

units for some meta become unavailable here. The result is that those line up having some holes or losing the edge.

I think this is the main reason why both of us choose 5 units team. and before I go further, let see the ambush phase first.

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dewabrata/Eo1xq6LE8Rv6BjbMbZZFpALXvBAkZDhV3NnptZSiWkLvQLkRZm7TuFDWKaUuhTQ9a3i.png


As usual, I check the power of both team during the ambush phase, after both party deploy their buff and debuff. With these line up, I could say these points:

1. Both of us in general use similar meta. We rely our meta on our tank, Silverblade Fighter. The only problem they have here is that my Silverblade fighter has higher level than theirs. However overall, our units levels do not differ a lot, almost similar.
2. They build up the team with the focus on Commander Slade. Their summoner, Elias Max Pruitt, focuses on buffing their Commander Blade. My team focuses on Warborn Shaman, and the rest of the team are meant to support him.
3. The reason why I focus on Warborn Shaman is because of the mana cap. I think most battle in 30s mana cap, populated by mid to small size units, and they are vulnerable to Warborn Shaman 3 magic damage attack.
4. If there is another different in our team, it's their line up that are fully focused on attacking. It's an all out attack, while my line up still have a couple of defensive approach. First the Nimbledook explorer protect ability, and the second one is Meriput Mossmender's repair ability. I still try to defend by enhancing my team armors.

So what happened next?

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dewabrata/23tS12kniWr4WW7gDbMTSWtza5o9tTgmoLsDxkNbwYhkyRktTTxZj8L6w7zKTXrn92PUf.png

We skip the first round because we want to talk on the main point here. The effect of extra armor and repairing armor delivers the biggest gap here. I could maintain  my tank longer, and their tank is gone in the first round.

At this point, their Commander Slade is exposed to my attacks. The sooner I could take down their core unit, the sooner they will lose. Meanwhile my Warborn Shaman still hides in the backline, unexposed!

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dewabrata/23tbMLg7THVSUejgSBWxrVrGhVzmXJQzHKkBG83EqUeDJRHLmE9ERF7qGP7mFCnCMEnPi.png

Let's skip 2 more round. On Round 4 the gap is widening. They have lost their Commander Slade and my Warborn Shaman is still safe. They have lost all their core units here and my team still has it.

https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dewabrata/Eo8L8vSj6QxnfYcqzaoJYP68npT67kr4sJSdFMUAxqAag8RVUtkc9RZz3sMf9RDVNrw.png

As the result, they all get wiped out in the fifth round. It's a good game.

Overall you can say my meta is better, I could defend better than them, although their offensive power from the Commander Slade is ridiculous. However I believe the reason they lose is not because of Warborn Shaman is better than their Commander Slade or because of my better Silverblade Fighter.

Their team fail to support their first 2 tanks, which is the core of their meta. The reason is simple, not enough Mana due to employing Elliot Max Pruitt. I do not have that issue because my summoner only cost me 3 mana. Prunda Unvervesch is not a strong summoner because of no buff she delivers, however her double element ability and 3 mana cap give me the right mana and right unit to support my Warborn Shaman. That's the decisive factor, employing summoner that allow you to get the right unit.

I think I have delivered my thought here well, so I hope you enjoy my post here. See you next time, or in Splinterlands Battlefield!

---

![https://splinterlands.com?ref=dewabrata](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dewabrata/23tbH2XfEqZJAFKMvoBTZG6B1pBkH9XJz79EpLXCGCCHvNVgeBbigFfqAtfmeowZ49T85.gif)

body.title: Holography
body.body:
# Holography

**Source:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holography

Holography is a technique that allows a wavefront to be recorded and later reconstructed. It is best known as a method of generating three-dimensional images, and has a wide range of other uses, including data storage, microscopy, and interferometry. In principle, it is possible to make a hologram for any type of wave.
A hologram is a recording of an interference pattern that can reproduce a 3D light field using diffraction. In general usage, a hologram is a recording of any type of wavefront in the form of an interference pattern. It can be created by capturing light from a real scene, or it can be generated by a computer, in which case it is known as a computer-generated hologram, which can show virtual objects or scenes. Optical holography needs a laser light to record the light field. The reproduced light field can generate an image that has the depth and parallax of the original scene.[1] A hologram is usually unintelligible when viewed under diffuse ambient light. When suitably lit, the interference pattern diffracts the light into an accurate reproduction of the original light field, and the objects that were in it exhibit visual depth cues such as parallax and perspective that change realistically with the different angles of viewing. That is, the view of the image from different angles shows the subject viewed from similar angles.
A hologram is traditionally generated by overlaying a second wavefront, known as the reference beam, onto a wavefront of interest. This generates an interference pattern, which is then captured on a physical medium. When the recorded interference pattern is later illuminated by the second wavefront, it is diffracted to recreate the original wavefront.[2] The 3D image from a hologram can often be viewed with non-laser light. However, in common practice, major image quality compromises are made to remove the need for laser illumination to view the hologram.
A computer-generated hologram is created by digitally modeling and combining two wavefronts to generate an interference pattern image. This image can then be printed onto a mask or film and illuminated with an appropriate light source to reconstruct the desired wavefront.[2] Alternatively, the interference pattern image can be directly displayed on a dynamic holographic display.[3]
Holographic portraiture often resorts to a non-holographic intermediate imaging procedure, to avoid the dangerous high-powered pulsed lasers which would be needed to optically \

moving subjects as perfectly as the extremely motion-intolerant holographic recording process requires. Early holography required high-power and expensive lasers. Currently, mass-produced low-cost laser diodes, such as those found on DVD recorders and used in other common applications, can be used to make holograms. They have made holography much more accessible to low-budget researchers, artists, and dedicated hobbyists.\nMost holograms produced are of static objects, but systems for displaying changing scenes on dynamic holographic displays are now being developed.[4][5]\nThe word holography comes from the Greek words ὅλος (holos; \

.[10]

Horizontal symmetric text, by Dieter Jung
Optical holography did not really advance until the development of the laser in 1960. The development of the laser enabled the first practical optical holograms that recorded 3D objects to be made in 1962 by Yuri Denisyuk in the Soviet Union[11] and by Emmett Leith and Juris Upatnieks at the University of Michigan, US.[12]
Early optical holograms used silver halide photographic emulsions as the recording medium. They were not very efficient as the produced diffraction grating absorbed much of the incident light. Various methods of converting the variation in transmission to a variation in refractive index (known as \

) were developed which enabled much more efficient holograms to be produced.[13][14][15]
A major advance in the field of holography was made by Stephen Benton, who invented a way to create holograms that can be viewed with natural light instead of lasers. These are called rainbow holograms.[8]

Basics of holography[edit]
Recording a hologram
Reconstructing a hologram
This is a photograph of a small part of an unbleached transmission hologram viewed through a microscope. The hologram recorded an image of a toy van and car. It is no more possible to discern the subject of the hologram from this pattern than it is to identify what music has been recorded by looking at a CD surface. The holographic information is recorded by the speckle pattern.
Holography is a technique for recording and reconstructing light fields.[16]: Section 1  
A light field is generally the result of a light source scattered off objects. Holography can be thought of as somewhat similar to sound recording, whereby a sound field created by vibrating matter like musical instruments or vocal cords, is encoded in such a way that it can be reproduced later, without the presence of the original vibrating matter.[17] However, it is even more similar to Ambisonic sound recording in which any listening angle of a sound field can be reproduced in the reproduction.

In laser holography, the hologram is recorded using a source of laser light, which is in phase. Various setups may be used, and several types of holograms can be made, but all involve the interaction of light coming from different directions and producing a microscopic interference pattern which a plate, film, or other medium photographically records.
In one common arrangement, the laser beam is split into two, one known as the object beam and the other as the reference beam. The object beam is expanded by passing it through a lens and used to illuminate the subject. The recording medium is located where this light, after being reflected or scattered by the subject, will strike it. The edges of the medium will ultimately serve as a window through which the subject is seen, so its location is chosen with that in mind. The reference beam is expanded and made to shine directly on the medium, where it interacts with the light coming from the subject to create the desired interference pattern.
Like conventional photography, holography requires an appropriate exposure time to correctly affect the recording medium. Unlike conventional photography, during the exposure the light source, the optical elements, the recording medium, and the subject must all remain  motionless relative to each other, to within about a quarter of the wavelength of the light, or the interference pattern will be blurred and the hologram spoiled. With living subjects and some unstable materials, that is only possible if a very intense and extremely brief pulse of laser light is used, a hazardous procedure which is rarely done outside of scientific and industrial laboratory settings. Exposures lasting several seconds to several minutes, using a much lower-powered continuously operating laser, are typical.

A hologram can be made by shining part of the light beam directly into the recording medium, and the other part onto the object in such a way that some of the scattered light falls onto the recording medium. A more flexible arrangement for recording a hologram requires the laser beam to be aimed through a series of elements that change it in different ways. The first element is a beam splitter that divides the beam into two identical beams, each aimed in different directions:

One beam (known as the 'illumination' or 'object beam') is spread using lenses and directed onto the scene using mirrors. Some of the light scattered (reflected) from the scene then falls onto the recording medium.
The second beam (known as the 'reference beam') is also spread through the use of lenses, but is directed so that it does not come in contact with the scene, and instead travels directly onto the recording medium.
Several different materials can be used as the recording medium. One of the most common is a film very similar to photographic film (silver halide photographic emulsion), but with much smaller light-reactive grains (preferably with diameters less than 20 nm), making it capable of the much higher resolution that holograms require. A layer of this recording medium (e.g., silver halide) is attached to a transparent substrate, which is commonly glass, but may also be plastic.

When the two laser beams reach the recording medium, their light waves intersect and interfere with each other. It is this interference pattern that is imprinted on the recording medium. The pattern itself is seemingly random, as it represents the way in which the scene's light interfered with the original light source – but not the original light source itself. The interference pattern can be considered an encoded version of the scene, requiring a particular key – the original light source – in order to view its contents.
This missing key is provided later by shining a laser, identical to the one used to record the hologram, onto the developed film. When this beam illuminates the hologram, it is diffracted by the hologram's surface pattern. This produces a light field identical to the one originally produced by the scene and scattered onto the hologram.

Comparison with photography[edit]
Holography may be better understood via an examination of its differences from ordinary photography:

![Image 1](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5f/Holomouse2.jpg/250px-Holomouse2.jpg)

A hologram represents a recording of information regarding the light that came from the original scene as scattered in a range of directions rather than from only one direction, as in a photograph. This allows the scene to be viewed from a range of different angles, as if it were still present.
A photograph can be recorded using normal light sources (sunlight or electric lighting) whereas a laser is required to record a hologram.
A lens is required in photography to record the image, whereas in holography, the light from the object is scattered directly onto the recording medium.
A holographic recording requires a second light beam (the reference beam) to be directed onto the recording medium.
A photograph can be viewed in a wide range of lighting conditions, whereas holograms can only be viewed with very specific forms of illumination.
When a photograph is cut in half, each piece shows half of the scene. When a hologram is cut in half, the whole scene can still be seen in each piece. This is because, whereas each point in a photograph only represents light scattered from a single point in the scene, each point on a holographic recording includes information about light scattered from every point in the scene. It can be thought of as viewing a street outside a house through a large window, then through a smaller window. One can see all of the same things through the smaller window (by moving the head to change the viewing angle), but the viewer can see more at once through the large window.
A photographic stereogram is a two-dimensional representation that can produce a three-dimensional effect but only from one point of view, whereas the reproduced viewing range of a hologram adds many more depth perception cues that were present in the original scene. These cues are recognized by the human brain and translated into the same perception of a three-dimensional image as when the original scene might have been viewed.
A photograph clearly maps out the light field of the original scene. The developed hologram's surface consists of a very fine, seemingly random pattern, which appears to bear no relationship to the scene it recorded.
Physics of holography[edit]

For a better understanding of the process, it is necessary to understand interference and diffraction. Interference occurs when one or more wavefronts are superimposed. Diffraction occurs when a wavefront encounters an object. The process of producing a holographic reconstruction is explained below purely in terms of interference and diffraction. It is somewhat simplified but is accurate enough to give an understanding of how the holographic process works.
For those unfamiliar with these concepts, it is worthwhile to read those articles before reading further in this article.

A diffraction grating is a structure with a repeating pattern. A simple example is a metal plate with slits cut at regular intervals. A light wave that is incident on a grating is split into several waves; the direction of these diffracted waves is determined by the grating spacing and the wavelength of the light.
A simple hologram can be made by superimposing two plane waves from the same light source on a holographic recording medium. The two waves interfere, giving a straight-line fringe pattern whose intensity varies sinusoidally across the medium. The spacing of the fringe pattern is determined by the angle between the two waves, and by the wavelength of the light.
The recorded light pattern is a diffraction grating. When it is illuminated by only one of the waves used to create it, it can be shown that one of the diffracted waves emerges at the same angle at which the second wave was originally incident, so that the second wave has been 'reconstructed'. Thus, the recorded light pattern is a holographic recording as defined above.

Sinusoidal zone plate
If the recording medium is illuminated with a point source and a normally incident plane wave, the resulting pattern is a sinusoidal zone plate, which acts as a negative Fresnel lens whose focal length is equal to the separation of the point source and the recording plane.
When a plane wave-front illuminates a negative lens, it is expanded into a wave that appears to diverge from the focal point of the lens. Thus, when the recorded pattern is illuminated with the original plane wave, some of the light is diffracted into a diverging beam equivalent to the original spherical wave; a holographic recording of the point source has been created.
When the plane wave is incident at a non-normal angle at the time of recording, the pattern formed is more complex, but still acts as a negative lens if it is illuminated at the original angle.

To record a hologram of a complex object, a laser beam is first split into two beams of light. One beam illuminates the object, which then scatters light onto the recording medium. According to diffraction theory, each point in the object acts as a point source of light so the recording medium can be considered to be illuminated by a set of point sources located at varying distances from the medium.
The second (reference) beam illuminates the recording medium directly. Each point source wave interferes with the reference beam, giving rise to its own sinusoidal zone plate in the recording medium. The resulting pattern is the sum of all these 'zone plates', which combine to produce a random (speckle) pattern as in the photograph above.
When the hologram is illuminated by the original reference beam, each of the individual zone plates reconstructs the object wave that produced it, and these individual wavefronts are combined to reconstruct the whole of the object beam. The viewer perceives a wavefront that is identical with the wavefront scattered from the object onto the recording medium, so that it appears that the object is still in place even if it has been removed.

Early on, artists saw the potential of holography as a medium and gained access to science laboratories to create their work. Holographic art is often the result of collaborations between scientists and artists, although some holographers would regard themselves as both an artist and a scientist.
Salvador Dalí claimed to have been the first to employ holography artistically. He was certainly the first and best-known surrealist to do so, but the 1972 New York exhibit of Dalí holograms had been preceded by the holographic art exhibition that was held at the Cranbrook Academy of Art in Michigan in 1968 and by the one at the Finch College gallery in New York in 1970, which attracted national media attention.[18] In Great Britain, Margaret Benyon began using holography as an artistic medium in the late 1960s and had a solo exhibition at the University of Nottingham art gallery in 1969.[19] This was followed in 1970 by a solo show at the Lisson Gallery in London, which was billed as the \

.[20]\nDuring the 1970s, a number of art studios and schools were established, each with their particular approach to holography. Notably, there was the San Francisco School of Holography established by Lloyd Cross, The Museum of Holography in New York founded by Rosemary (Posy) H. Jackson, the Royal College of Art in London and the Lake Forest College Symposiums organised by Tung Jeong.[21] None of these studios still exist; however, there is the Center for the Holographic Arts in New York[22] and the HOLOcenter in Seoul, which offers artists a place to create and exhibit work.\nDuring the 1980s, many artists who worked with holography helped the diffusion of this so-called \
in the art world, such as Harriet Casdin-Silver of the United States, Dieter Jung of Germany, and Moysés Baumstein of Brazil, each one searching for a proper \

to use with the three-dimensional work, avoiding the simple holographic reproduction of a sculpture or object. For instance, in Brazil, many concrete poets (Augusto de Campos, Décio Pignatari, Julio Plaza and José Wagner Garcia, associated with Moysés Baumstein) found in holography a way to express themselves and to renew concrete poetry.
A small but active group of artists still integrate holographic elements into their work.[23] Some are associated with novel holographic techniques; for example, artist Matt Brand[24] employed computational mirror design to eliminate image distortion from specular holography.
The MIT Museum[25] and Jonathan Ross[26] both have extensive collections of holography and on-line catalogues of art holograms.

Holographic data storage is a technique that can store information at high density inside crystals or photopolymers. The ability to store large amounts of information in some kind of medium is of great importance, as many electronic products incorporate storage devices. As current storage techniques such as Blu-ray Disc reach the limit of possible data density (due to the diffraction-limited size of the writing beams), holographic storage has the potential to become the next generation of popular storage media. The advantage of this type of data storage is that the volume of the recording media is used instead of just the surface.
Currently available SLMs can produce about 1000 different images a second at 1024×1024-bit resolution which would result in about one-gigabit-per-second writing speed.[27]
In 2005, companies such as Optware and Maxell produced a 120 mm disc that uses a holographic layer to store data to a potential 3.9 TB, a format called Holographic Versatile Disc. As of September 2014, no commercial product has been released.
Another company, InPhase Technologies, was developing a competing format, but went bankrupt in 2011 and all its assets were sold to Akonia Holographics, LLC.
While many holographic data storage models have used \
storage, where each recorded hologram holds a large amount of data, more recent research into using submicrometre-sized \

has resulted in several potential 3D optical data storage solutions. While this approach to data storage can not attain the high data rates of page-based storage, the tolerances, technological hurdles, and cost of producing a commercial product are significantly lower.

In static holography, recording, developing and reconstructing occur sequentially, and a permanent hologram is produced.
There also exist holographic materials that do not need the developing process and can record a hologram in a very short time. This allows one to use holography to perform some simple operations in an all-optical way. Examples of applications of such real-time holograms include phase-conjugate mirrors (\

of light), optical cache memories, image processing (pattern recognition of time-varying images), and optical computing.
The amount of processed information can be very high (terabits/s), since the operation is performed in parallel on a whole image. This compensates for the fact that the recording time, which is in the order of a microsecond, is still very long compared to the processing time of an electronic computer. The optical processing performed by a dynamic hologram is also much less flexible than electronic processing. On one side, one has to perform the operation always on the whole image, and on the other side, the operation a hologram can perform is basically either a multiplication or a phase conjugation. In optics, addition and Fourier transform are already easily performed in linear materials, the latter simply by a lens. This enables some applications, such as a device that compares images in an optical way.[28]
The search for novel nonlinear optical materials for dynamic holography is an active area of research. The most common materials are photorefractive crystals, but in semiconductors or semiconductor heterostructures (such as quantum wells), atomic vapors and gases, plasmas and even liquids, it was possible to generate holograms.
A particularly promising application is optical phase conjugation. It allows the removal of the wavefront distortions a light beam receives when passing through an aberrating medium, by sending it back through the same aberrating medium with a conjugated phase. This is useful, for example, in free-space optical communications to compensate for atmospheric turbulence (the phenomenon that gives rise to the twinkling of starlight).

Peace Within Reach, a Denisyuk DCG hologram by amateur Dave Battin
Since the beginning of holography, many holographers have explored its uses and displayed them to the public.
In 1971, Lloyd Cross opened the San Francisco School of Holography and taught amateurs how to make holograms using only a small (typically 5 mW) helium-neon laser and inexpensive home-made equipment. Holography had been supposed to require a very expensive metal optical table set-up to lock all the involved elements down in place and damp any vibrations that could blur the interference fringes and ruin the hologram. Cross's home-brew alternative was a sandbox made of a cinder block retaining wall on a plywood base, supported on stacks of old tires to isolate it from ground vibrations, and filled with sand that had been washed to remove dust. The laser was securely mounted atop the cinder block wall. The mirrors and simple lenses needed for directing, splitting and expanding the laser beam were affixed to short lengths of PVC pipe, which were stuck into the sand at the desired locations. The subject and the photographic plate holder were similarly supported within the sandbox. The holographer turned off the room light, blocked the laser beam near its source using a small relay-controlled shutter, loaded a plate into the holder in the dark, left the room, waited a few minutes to let everything settle, then made the exposure by remotely operating the laser shutter.
In 1979, Jason Sapan opened the Holographic Studios in New York City. Since then, they have been involved in the production of many holographs for many artists as well as companies.[29] Sapan has been described as the \

.
Many of these holographers would go on to produce art holograms. In 1983, Fred Unterseher, a co-founder of the San Francisco School of Holography and a well-known holographic artist, published the Holography Handbook, an easy-to-read guide to making holograms at home. This brought in a new wave of holographers and provided simple methods for using the then-available AGFA silver halide recording materials.
In 2000, Frank DeFreitas published the Shoebox Holography Book and introduced the use of inexpensive laser pointers to countless hobbyists. For many years, it had been assumed that certain characteristics of semiconductor laser diodes made them virtually useless for creating holograms, but when they were eventually put to the test of practical experiment, it was found that not only was this untrue, but that some actually provided a coherence length much greater than that of traditional helium-neon gas lasers. This was a very important development for amateurs, as the price of red laser diodes had dropped from hundreds of dollars in the early 1980s to about $5 after they entered the mass market as a component pulled from CD, or later, DVD players from the mid-1980s onwards. Now, there are thousands of amateur holographers worldwide.
By late 2000, holography kits with inexpensive laser pointer diodes entered the mainstream consumer market. These kits enabled students, teachers, and hobbyists to make several kinds of holograms without specialized equipment, and became popular gift items by 2005.[30] The introduction of holography kits with self-developing plates in 2003 made it possible for hobbyists to create holograms without the bother of wet chemical processing.[31]
In 2006, a large number of surplus holography-quality green lasers (Coherent C315) became available and put dichromated gelatin (DCG) holography within the reach of the amateur holographer. The holography community was surprised at the amazing sensitivity of DCG to green light. It had been assumed that this sensitivity would be uselessly slight or non-existent. Jeff Blyth responded with the G307 formulation of DCG to increase the speed and sensitivity to these new lasers.[32]
Kodak and Agfa, the former major suppliers of holography-quality silver halide plates and films, are no longer in the market. While other manufacturers have helped fill the void, many amateurs are now making their own materials. The favorite formulations are dichromated gelatin, Methylene-Blue-sensitised dichromated gelatin, and diffusion method silver halide preparations. Jeff Blyth has published very accurate methods for making these in a small lab or garage.[33]
A small group of amateurs are even constructing their own pulsed lasers to make holograms of living subjects and other unsteady or moving objects.[34]

Holographic interferometry[edit]

Holographic interferometry (HI) is a technique that enables static and dynamic displacements of objects with optically rough surfaces to be measured to optical interferometric precision (i.e. to fractions of a wavelength of light).[35][36] It can also be used to detect optical-path-length variations in transparent media, which enables, for example, fluid flow to be visualized and analyzed. It can also be used to generate contours representing the form of the surface or the isodose regions in radiation dosimetry.[37]
It has been widely used to measure stress, strain, and vibration in engineering structures.

Interferometric microscopy[edit]

The hologram keeps the information on the amplitude and phase of the field. Several holograms may keep information about the same distribution of light, emitted to various directions. The numerical analysis of such holograms allows one to emulate large numerical aperture, which, in turn, enables enhancement of the resolution of optical microscopy. The corresponding technique is called interferometric microscopy. Recent achievements of interferometric microscopy allow one to approach the quarter-wavelength limit of resolution.[38]

Sensors or biosensors[edit]

The hologram is made with a modified material that interacts with certain molecules generating a change in the fringe periodicity or refractive index, therefore, the color of the holographic reflection.[39][40]

Identigram as a security element in a German identity card
Dove hologram used on some credit cards
Holograms are commonly used for security, as they are replicated from a master hologram that requires expensive, specialized and technologically advanced equipment, and are thus difficult to forge. They are used widely in many currencies, such as the Brazilian 20, 50, and 100-reais notes; British 5, 10, 20 and 50-pound notes; South Korean 5000, 10,000, and 50,000-won notes; Japanese 5000 and 10,000 yen notes, Indian 50, 100, 500 rupee notes; and all the currently-circulating banknotes of the Canadian dollar, Croatian kuna, Danish krone, and Euro. They can also be found in credit and bank cards as well as passports, ID cards, books, food packaging, DVDs, and sports equipment. Such holograms come in a variety of forms, from adhesive strips that are laminated on packaging for fast-moving consumer goods to holographic tags on electronic products. They often contain textual or pictorial elements to protect identities and separate genuine articles from counterfeits.
Holographic scanners are in use in post offices, larger shipping firms, and automated conveyor systems to determine the three-dimensional size of a package. They are often used in tandem with checkweighers to allow automated pre-packing of given volumes, such as a truck or pallet for bulk shipment of goods.
Holograms produced in elastomers can be used as stress-strain reporters due to its elasticity and compressibility, the pressure and force applied are correlated to the reflected wavelength, therefore its color.[41] Holography technique can also be effectively used for radiation dosimetry.[42][43]

High-security registration plates[edit]
High-security holograms can be used on license plates for vehicles such as cars and motorcycles. As of April 2019, holographic license plates are required on vehicles in parts of India to aid in identification and security, especially in cases of car theft. Such number plates hold electronic data of vehicles, and they have a unique ID number and a sticker to indicate authenticity.[44]

Holography using other types of waves[edit]
In principle, it is possible to make a hologram for any wave.
Electron holography is the application of holography techniques to electron waves rather than light waves. Electron holography was invented by Dennis Gabor to improve the resolution and avoid the aberrations of the transmission electron microscope. Today it is commonly used to study electric and magnetic fields in thin films, as magnetic and electric fields can shift the phase of the interfering wave passing through the sample.[45] The principle of electron holography can also be applied to interference lithography.[46]
Acoustic holography enables sound maps of an object to be generated.  Measurements of the acoustic field are made at many points close to the object.  These measurements are digitally processed to produce the \

of the object.[47]
Atomic holography has evolved out of the development of the basic elements of atom optics. With the Fresnel diffraction lens and atomic mirrors atomic holography follows a natural step in the development of the physics (and applications) of atomic beams. Recent developments including atomic mirrors and especially ridged mirrors have provided the tools necessary for the creation of atomic holograms,[48] although such holograms have not yet been commercialized.
Neutron beam holography has been used to see the inside of solid objects.[49]
Holograms with x-rays are generated by using synchrotrons or x-ray free-electron lasers as radiation sources and pixelated detectors such as CCDs as recording medium.[50] The reconstruction is then retrieved via computation. Due to the shorter wavelength of x-rays compared to visible light, this approach allows imaging objects with higher spatial resolution.[51] As free-electron lasers can provide ultrashort and x-ray pulses in the range of femtoseconds which are intense and coherent, x-ray holography has been used to capture ultrafast dynamic processes.[52][53][54]

Virtually every illusion of an image that looks three-dimensional, seems to be floating in space, or features other vague resemblances, has erroneously been labelled a hologram, including effects produced by lenticular printing, iridescent foil printing, bubblegrams, the Pepper's ghost illusion (or modern variants such as the Musion Eyeliner), tomography and volumetric displays.[55][56] Such illusions have been called \
.[57][58]\nThe Pepper's ghost technique is most prevalent in 3D displays that claim to be (or are referred to as) \

. While the original illusion, used in theater, involved actual physical objects and persons, located offstage, modern variants replace the source object with a digital screen, which displays imagery generated with 3D computer graphics to provide the necessary depth cues. The reflection of flat imagery can look less realistic than that of an actual 3D object. Alternatively, rear projection of realistic images on semi-transparent screens can create the same illusion. Notable examples of digital Pepper's ghost illusions include virtual \

performances by the Gorillaz (in the 2005 MTV Europe Music Awards and the 48th Grammy Awards), Tupac Shakur's at Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival in 2012,[59] Swedish supergroup ABBA,[60] American rock group Kiss,[61] and Hatsune Miku and other Vocaloid singing synthesizer applications.[62][63][64][65][66]
Holography is distinct from specular holography, which is a technique for making three-dimensional images by controlling the motion of specularities on a two-dimensional surface.[67] It works by reflectively or refractively manipulating bundles of light rays, not by using interference and diffraction.

Holography has been widely referred to in movies, novels, and TV, usually in science fiction, starting in the late 1970s.[68] Science fiction writers absorbed the urban legends surrounding holography that had been spread by overly-enthusiastic scientists and entrepreneurs trying to market the idea.[68] This had the effect of giving the public overly high expectations of the capability of holography, due to the unrealistic depictions of it in most fiction, where they are fully three-dimensional computer projections that are sometimes tactile through the use of force fields.[68] Examples of this type of depiction include the hologram of Princess Leia in Star Wars, Arnold Rimmer from Red Dwarf, who was later converted to \

to make him solid, and the Holodeck and Emergency Medical Hologram from Star Trek.[68]\nHolography has served as an inspiration for many video games with science fiction elements. In many titles, fictional holographic technology has been used to reflect real-life misrepresentations of potential military use of holograms, such as the \

in Command & Conquer: Red Alert 2 that can disguise themselves as trees.[69] Player characters are able to use holographic decoys in games such as Halo: Reach and Crysis 2 to confuse and distract the enemy.[69] Starcraft ghost agent Nova has access to \

as one of her three primary abilities in Heroes of the Storm.[70]
Fictional depictions of holograms have, however, inspired technological advances in other fields, such as augmented reality, that promise to fulfill the fictional depictions of holograms by other means.[71]

body.title: Looking Up On Wednesday
body.body:
> #
Looking Up On Wednesday
**FLOWERS IN THE SKY**

![1.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/adetorrent/EpnAvgDcNFBqhaj9q1ziSxnHuvxqQQmk2W432XGwrGSx2gRRRqSbB4JUeR1ULQQrrGw.jpeg) We've been having blue skies lately, even if a little windy, so I've been walking a lot. I found some beautiful contrasts between the very colourful flowers on tall trees up against the blue skies. I tried making some *negative space* type photos but I didn't quite achieve that.
![2.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/adetorrent/Ep5jEzKZTqkSQMCQNEzJDTcXVwKwv9cRvJGSzht9Wh8g4mNeG92GLzHPQJymGPozdcW.jpeg) I tried mirroring the few clouds visible with the white flowers but they were moving too quickly and didn't quite work :)
![3.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/adetorrent/EqL15ENwHD9FZVkgSfjAPiqFTii37pybW6MBWLTrqPF31xiqkomtShK99BEPvXWEcsV.jpeg) ![4.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/adetorrent/EpEFL2waKByCpu1D7hcMdGPVrvsMWbmcBZa677nxzkCWyDPNtu7qTwonRjtXBPAEJcA.jpeg) These two reminded me of the last time I was on the Canary Islands with epic blue skies and high contrast palm trees, mostly deep green, against blue. There were also, at times, some white fruit looking things on trees there that till this day I haven't figured out what they were. Anyway, I'll try again next wednesday 📷 Peace & Love, *Adé*

Thats because the team tested the BTC pool with a higher % of the pool reserve to test the CLP fee. That was a few early Txs. 
CLP fee is derived from swap size vs pool reserve. 

The actual Fees are this: 

**0.08% + 0.25% service fee for HBD->BTC** 
**0.16% + 0.25% service fee for HIVE->HBD->BTC** 
**0.08% + 0% service fee for BTC->HBD**
**0.16% + 0% service fee for BTC->HBD->HIVE**

body.title: Wednesday Walk: Nature Never Hides Itself Under A Mask
body.body:
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUKy2F3SRe34oaBWqAt2aFzPCqHAxB9P7MeuBGWeZzuTR/001240.jpg)

Translated from Lithuanian with Google.com

Wednesday coffee. I'm sitting on the terrace because the sun is warming me up quite well. I'm sitting with a cup in my hand after work, and my head is still a bit chaotic. It's so hard to organize my thoughts. After chatting with quite a few people online about work, I'm starting to think that many people want to be someone because they're afraid to show their true selves, to put on a thousand masks, and to put on some armour so as not to be hurt. And besides, a beautiful, improved image is much easier to sell. You can even pretend to be confident when you have zero confidence, but when you're talking online, no one sees you for who you really are.

>Trečiadienio kava. Sėdžiu terasoje, nes saulė jau gana gerai šildo. Sėdžiu su puodeliu rankoje po darbo, o mano galva vis dar šiek tiek chaotiška. Taip sunku susidėlioti mintis. Po pokalbių su nemažai žmonių internete  darbo reikalais pradedu galvoti, kad daugelis žmonių nori būti kuo nors kitu, nes bijo parodyti tikrąjį save, užsideda tūkstantį kaukių ir apsivilka šarvus, kad tik nebūtų sužeisti. Be to, gražų, patobulintą įvaizdį daug lengviau parduoti. Galima net apsimesti pasitikinčiu savimi, kai to pasitikėjimo nulis, bet kai kalbi internetu, niekas nemato tavęs tokio, koks esi iš tikrųjų.>

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmP744kD6KEhDhmgaRUGTqHthFEdML8QQByrwhYz9czrW6/001520.jpg)

So I'm starting to think maybe it's enough to pretend to be someone else and beat smarter people. Maybe you can play without rules and reach the top easier that way?

>Tad pradedu galvoti, kad galbūt užtenka apsimesti kuo nors kitu ir laimėsi prieš protingesnius žmones. Galbūt galima žaisti be taisyklių ir taip lengviau pasiekti viršūnę?>

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmamQo9ZLrm8JvLENc1FidxZ7yyZbth1FyJMthjPprivAt/001004.jpg)

I finish my coffee and lazily stand up from my chair. I know I'll force myself to go to the park and take some photos, because my beloved sakuras are already starting to bloom. And when I get back, I'll write about my Wednesday walk. And only after leaving the house do I feel that the walk is beneficial for me. I've been spending a lot of time on the Internet lately. All my work is there. So it's time for me to clear my mind.

>Baigiu gerti kavą ir tingiai atsistoju nuo kėdės. Žinau, kad priversiu save nuslinkti į parką ir padaryti keletą nuotraukų, nes mano mylimos sakuros jau pradeda žydėti. O grįžusi parašysiu apie savo trečiadienio pasivaikščiojimą. Ir tik išėjusi iš namų pajuntu, kad pasivaikščiojimas man naudingas. Pastaruoju metu daug laiko praleidžiu internete. Visi mano darbai ten. Todėl pats laikas man prasivalyti mintis.>

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmXjSyvpYKbP22bwYEbne5B9bLuRtNL5yrFeKZf9j3VMaT/0255200.jpg)

Continuing my thoughts, I still believe that there are things that you will never achieve with cunning alone. And the most important of them is peace. This is peace, when you can calmly look at yourself in the mirror, without reproaching yourself and without a guilty conscience. After all, life will test us all someday. And then neither our beautiful speech nor our perfect image will help. Only our wisdom will help. Are we ready to face difficulties, or will we hide in the bushes? Will we be able to remain good people when no one sees us and does not discuss us? Will we have not only a backbone - stubbornness, but also a heart - sincerity, compassion? Will the struggle with difficulties make us insensitive?

>Tęsiant savo mintis, vis dar tikiu, kad yra dalykų, kurių vien gudrumu niekada nepasieksi. O svarbiausia iš jų – ramybė. Tai ramybė, kai gali ramiai pažvelgti į save veidrodyje, nepriekaištaudamas sau ir be sąžinės graužaties. Juk gyvenimas kada nors mus visus išbandys. Ir tada nepadės nei mūsų graži kalba, nei tobulas įvaizdis. Padės tik mūsų išmintis. Ar esame pasiruošę susidurti su sunkumais, ar tiesiog pasislėpsime krūmuose? Ar sugebėsime išlikti gerais žmonėmis, kai niekas mūsų nematys ir neaptarinės? Ar turėsime ne tik stuburą – užsispyrimą, bet ir širdį – nuoširdumą, atjautą? Ar kova su sunkumais nepadarys mūsų nejautriais?>

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQ8KaqhLDJerbh6GVqCNrsZeDT5u3dnY5C6gUrC1rBsf1/img_20260422_103920.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmT6Zu6J7W6pdKJQjp4yggkWaS4W12ifjjfPmj2u89CBdy/img_20260422_103939.jpg)

In a world full of people wearing masks, our greatest weapon, our strength, is to remain a real person. How good it is that even nature has no masks. If it is grey and angry, that is how it appears. If it smiles, if love for the world burns in its heart, it generously shares everything with us. That is why I love nature so much. It is my refreshment, and even when I am most tired, I want to connect with it for at least a short while, to touch its wisdom and essence.

>Pasaulyje, pilname žmonių su kaukėmis, didžiausias mūsų ginklas, mūsų stiprybė – išlikti tikru žmogumi. Kaip gera, kad nors gamta neturi kaukių. Jei ji pilka ir pikta, ji tokia ir pasirodo. Jei ji šypsosi, jei jos širdyje dega meilė pasauliui, ji dosniai ja dalijasi  viskuo su mumis. Štai kodėl aš taip myliu gamtą. Ji – mano atgaiva, ir net tada, kai esu labiausiai pavargęs, noriu bent trumpam su ja susilieti, prisiliesti prie jos išminties ir esmės.>

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRB2zmP975bHTzxBB6NBmnZyo7FbZHUbMxRU15S1Z9vCt/010101.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdnNyqPz6oQjPMsqrRPG9SdtL4Wkc7XzUAhRMt2EqCMyA/0010104.jpg)

The world may punish us for our openness, but nature never will. We may lose the battles of our lives for a while, but nature will always give us its shelter and heal us. We don’t need to chase the world; we just need to each go our own way, take small steps forward, calmly go step by step, and then the world itself will start chasing us. Therefore, after work, we can calmly drink coffee, we can go out into nature, calmly breathe in fresh air, calm our restlessly beating hearts, because we are doing what we must. We just live our lives. Slowly, calmly, because no matter how much we would like to live someone else’s life, we will only waste our strength on meaningless struggles.

>Pasaulis gali mus nubausti už mūsų atvirumą, bet gamta niekada to nepadarys. Galbūt kurį laiką pralaimėsime savo gyvenimo kovas, bet gamta visada suteiks mums savo prieglobstį ir išgydys mus. Mums nereikia vytis pasaulio; tereikia eiti savo keliu, žengti mažais žingsneliais į priekį, ramiai eiti žingsnis po žingsnio, o tada pats pasaulis pradės mus vytis. Todėl po darbo galime ramiai išgerti kavos, išeiti į gamtą, ramiai įkvėpti gryno oro, nuraminti neramiai plakančias širdis, nes darome tai, ką privalome. Mes gyvename savo gyvenimą. Lėtai, ramiai, nes kad ir kaip norėtume gyventi kažkieno kito gyvenimą, tik švaistysime savo jėgas beprasmėms kovoms.>

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQWUMiFgrUVW1Z57bHUdHBxi1dvfJFkeiGTykAFmZAc4r/img_20260422_103752.jpg)

And nature will not wait for anyone, it will go its own way, it will move forward into the summer, so let’s better watch it and not become like those who are afraid to take off their masks in front of us.

>Ir gamta niekieno nelauks, ji eis savo keliu, žengs pirmyn į vasarą, tad geriau stebėkime ją ir netapkime tokiais, kaip tie, kurie bijo nusiimti kaukes prieš mus.>

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNrsTQ7oD1WtuMCmkwopamTFb1eGEyZgX5htAVDFAg7ho/0104102145.jpg)


💝💝💝💝💝💝💝💝💝💝

With love, @madeirane  
Photos are taken by me.  
© 2026

Hey everyone!

My name is ikedichukwu, and I am very happy to finally join the amazing community here on Hive. I feel honored to be part of this platform where people share ideas, stories, cultures/traditions, learn from each other, and grow together.

I am from Nigeria, a country rich in diversity, culture/traditions, resilience, and creativity. I have always looked up to learning new things and sharing knowledge with others. Writing and teachings has been one of my dreams, especially when it comes to real-life matters, traditions/cultures, African foods, African herbs and usages, and personal development.

- culture and traditions.
- African foods.
- African herbs and usages.
- teach the public how to enlarge their penises, enlarge their boobs(naturally)train and become the best for your partner.
- personal development.

- business.

Apart from herbs and cultures, I am also passionate about logical stories and travels. Learning about different cultures and communities is very important to me, and I enjoy maintaining a healthy lifestyle. I plan to share my travel experiences , cultural  experiences, and cultural shocks, which I believe will motivate others who are also interested in learning about other cultures around the world.

Another lovely thing I truly enjoy is cooking. I cook native foods that are salivating and I'll be teaching on how to cook proper Igbo foods. I will be  sharing African(IGBO) food preparation posts, recipes, and cooking experiences that others can learn from or enjoy.

Here on Hive, my main goal is to:

I joined Hive because I believe it is a platform that rewards creativity and effort. I am grateful to the food community for supporting new users and helping newcomers feel welcomed.

Thank you all for welcoming me to this wonderful platform. I truly look forward to meeting new friends, sharing my experiences, and contributing valuable content to this amazing community.

Follow for more updates, you can message me if you'd like to learn anything privately, about cultures in Africa and Africa herbs on sexualities. 

Thanks for reading,
Ikedichukwu

body.title: I'm just drifting -5minutefreewrite
body.body:
For https://peakd.com/hive-161155/@daily.prompt/22-april-2026-freewriters-community-daily-writing-prompt-day-3081-im-just-drifting

I'm just drifting. I drift from thing to do to the next, never fully knowing why... I just realized that not only is today an unexpected day off, tomorrow is an expected day off. That feels freeing. I want my kid and wife to come see the show on Friday. The whole show.

Let's drift back to what I can do. I can write Gentle Werewolf. I can look at it and dive in deep. I sure can. I have most of tomorrow to do it, still. That will be excellent. I'm excited. Maybe I make a list of what I need to do. I'll open the document. I'll re-read what I've written so far. I'll ask myself what I want to do with these characters. What do I like about it already? Let's answer that.

I like that I'm imagining a world where the mess-up is someone other people love and take care of. I like that it's a world where people in general take care of each other. I like the idea that there's some forces that are trying to keep them from being weird...ooo. Maybe that's it. Maybe I need all the characters to embrace a bit of weird that there's some pressure externally to not be... maybe it needs to be more of a discovery of how to be themselves in the face of repressive forces?

Let's examine that. We've got Tom, centrally. I think...hmmm I think I do like that he has been self-medicating, and it's been hurting him and his friends. And that finding joy in being a werewolf is a change that's going to make him behave in a healthier way.

body.title: Ourpick Reading Suggestions for April 22nd
body.body:
OurPick encouragement program is part of the @Liotes ecosystem, where quality posts are curated. Authors are encouraged to continue creating content, adding value to various communities, and contributing to Hive in general.

<center>
![Our Pick.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ourpick/23xKvmLuUXLGUefmnwhW6ThR931bbPk67mbW7xftvt6mXpisA5BMC24gczdnAfiep8WgL.jpg)
*Created in Canva.com*
</center>

Occasionally, we will select a couple of outstanding posts that we find particularly interesting and suggest them for your further reading... We hope it will help authors as an additional promotional tool... We support creators with our upvotes in Hive, but also in other tribe tokens! These Hive-Engine tribes add extra value to the entire ecosystem, helping authors and curators follow their niches and dreams...

<center>
![LEN Divider - Pick1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cryptofiloz/23vhKVQg9XEpsfMHC2AJpbhYf825iQWRaAN6vRK63ZuQzGgXTogcbmc7HFeDWaUyrrhyW.png)
</center>

#### [Sporting memories: The day I finally learned now to hit a baseball](https://ecency.com/hive-101690/@sports.guy55/sporting-memories-the-day-i-finally-learned-now-to-hit-a-baseball) by @sports.guy55

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ourpick/23wg8wKi9cnUWkmxbnpKkyi4G4cHX6oStDG7i45TKAy7Jna9E9KZyTLjDSW6daGQAyNGT.png)

> *Sounds like a lot of fun, and well-deserved if the ball hits a drunk guy who entered the cage... 😂
Jokes aside, nice story! Who would tell that $2 worth of credits can teach you baseball, while dozens of coaches couldn't do it... 😃 I remember the time when I was working in the PC gaming club, wondering what those kids could learn from games that could help them out in life... Who knows, even PC games could develop skills... 🙂*

<center>
![LEN Divider - Pick2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cryptofiloz/23vhKckUthotT4G75iuSazJXjJYtZZpUqAkYAj8TuSYAwpQcsTBJZxGeMRLm3XYNiVnZ2.png)
</center>

#### [The riverbank is always attractive for a photographic stroll (Es-Eng)](https://ecency.com/hive-155530/@jlufer/the-riverbank-is-always-attractive-for-a-photographic-stroll-es-eng) by @jlufer

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ourpick/23tmFiFGoP8EG4zLsgHt9PteXXL6z5RxEB637C8SaFLJZ6RKNWkRUvu1JSWJ33t3qAQSQ.png)

> *What I liked most was the pergola, as it reminded me of one just like it in my hometown. The entire place is truly beautiful; you mention that it is especially for children, but I believe that we adults—who know how to appreciate the beauty of every little nook—find it absolutely delightful as well. I am glad you are writing about this other area of ​​the city situated right by the river; I have always thoroughly enjoyed what you share with us, and your photos just keep getting better.*

<center>
![LEN Divider - Pick3.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cryptofiloz/23vhKckUthotT4G74RAZkFg39g7xkai4vXWirc1vVhf9g3ZRSkqbWVSKhQBGyAJ1dH7PJ.png)
</center>

#### [You’re not going to believe it! 😄](https://ecency.com/hive-177745/@nanixxx/youre-not-going-to-believe-it) by @nanixxx

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ourpick/23u5xjL4dcmSnEFJg46S5M1TDxhRkymAfZpVELt4CdDkijBDKJFj46qAjUudwmDPxmyx1.png)

> *Of course I understand what you’ve achieved; just as in every aspect of life and in whatever each of us enjoys, achievements are a source of immense joy, and that’s something to celebrate! And I’m not just highlighting the achievement of coming second, I’m sure you’ll soon be first, but there’s more to it than that: bringing a smile to people’s faces, taking in beautiful views, photographing churches, exploring new places and finding happiness in the little things, like having a beer.
Congratulations!!! I know it’s taken a lot of effort and many attempts, but those with discipline and perseverance succeed! This can serve as inspiration to others, too.*

<center>
![LEN Divider - Pick4.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cryptofiloz/23vhKckUtj698ykr5smUgcBQPWBDGx8sENEZeZ6bU4CgJfJxaVW2BNZyHiMHGFYgmnsGG.png)
</center>

#### [Going to the Shrine with My Favorite People... <3](https://ecency.com/hive-108045/@tegoshei/going-to-the-shrine-with-my-favorite-people-3) by @tegoshei

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ourpick/23yTWX5eabBSrbLyo4ZLdNcynm4XRH5BjD3Srcru5cxuKFh2iC9NFUvYyxHcisphF96ja.png)

> *Sometimes, our parents got in a bad relationship with the rest of their families, and we, children, can still have good relations with our cousins... Why not? It's great to see that you are keeping good connections with half of your family, and that the generation gap isn't an issue... That doesn't happen too often...
Take care of each other and always remember these good days... 😉*

<center>
![LEN Divider - Bonus Pick.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ourpick/23uEoCNzr6v6M7yEro1pRUrWBHfDrgCbcEAXUbxkgKqhS92hHUPEhGP2gH5mqSiA9v5sn.png)
</center>

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ourpick/23u5Wugxjdvtg4W7syWYc9peZmdPJrM3LZcEiouQcgTGhJB1sWgKQ3SLeyuBs7tEHKFsw.png)

> *What a terrifying story, but who knows if it could ever be real, perhaps one day. It’s one of the possible endings that films occasionally mention: being invaded by aliens and the end of our world. But you’ve added the twist of human experimentation and another aspect that’s often discussed: the implantation of memories. Could this world be real, or are we living in a matrix? Anything is possible; who’s to say what’s real and what isn’t?
You handle the dialogue very well, leading the reader to consider different hypotheses throughout the story. I loved it! Thank you so much for always being part of the community and, as I always say, for interacting with other members, I really appreciate it*

body.title: Above the Vydra River (for #wednesdaywalk)
body.body:
> Na jednom úseku řeky Vydry bývám častým „hostem“ :-).
Řeka protéká malebným a zároveň drsným šumavským údolím. Mohutné balvany „zdobí“ jak koryto řeky, tak i okolní stráně.
Bohužel i tady, uprostřed divoké krásy Šumavského národního parku, dnes uvidíte spoustu mrtvých stromů, které má na svědomí kůrovec.

Asi uprostřed naučné stezky kolem řeky, z Čeňkovy pily do Antýglu, se nachází Turnerova chata. Právě tuto chatu zásobuje naše firma a proto jsem zde častým hostem. Provozují zde restauraci s velmi ochotnou obsluhou, Výborné místo pro doplnění tekutin a utišení žaludku při procházce kolem řeky :-)

> I am a frequent “guest” on one section of the Vydra River :-).
The river flows through a picturesque and at the same time rugged Šumava valley. Massive boulders “decorate” both the riverbed and the surrounding slopes.
Unfortunately, even here, in the midst of the wild beauty of the Šumava National Park, today you will see a lot of dead trees, which are the work of the bark beetle.

About in the middle of the nature trail around the river, from Čeňkova pila to Antýgl, is Turnerova chata (cottage). This is the cottage that our company supplies and that is why I am a frequent guest here.
They run a restaurant with very helpful staff, a great place to replenish fluids and calm your stomach while walking around the river :-)
![vlcsnap-2026-04-18-18h52m17s707.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bucipuci/23vhwMWMYmP36J3rpq4hn5wcRU7M9Vq9DGxTGjoTxYgUCjkPuCpPscz3sELoL3vTpgpTq.png)

![vlcsnap-2026-04-20-20h49m49s942.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bucipuci/23yd5eJUSVpQvtvnUwCcnxYWXeR99v59w6f2jPv39KK632Jc2iJsXPrK8g6D4gRPLeU1t.png) ![linka1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bucipuci/23swXQgUNzHCUaoqVQ7xJsMWUUjSApjCzgkGyzcvzGpiGuHbnAkuDqrzatb2oYeGtHJ15.png)
>\nMinulý týden to byla poslední zastávka na mé zásobovací trase. Zboží bylo složeno a Tom (dron Potensic Atom) netrpělivě čekal až ho vypustím nad řeku :-)\n

> Last week it was the last stop on my supply route. The goods were packed and Tom (Potensic Atom drone) was impatiently waiting for me to release it over the river :-)
![IMG_20260417_123103.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bucipuci/23tSKhtpBss1e6wLELNVrsCf5EUpW83vNya7PEosZf1xJXgrTJQ3XaFBPmtBuoVUCTm3W.jpg)

>\nPořídili jsme spolu krátké video (naleznete jako vždy na konci článku) a z videa nějaké fotografie. Pokud vás zaujme stříbrná až šedá barva některých stromů, tak vězte, že to je barva „smrti“. Tyto stromy byly napadeny kůrovcem. Protože se místo nachází v prvním ochranném pásmu národního parku, zůstávají stromy na svém místě. Pokáceny jsou jen v místech, kde by mohly ohrožovat bezpečnost návštěvníků nebo svým pádem zatarasit řeku.\n

>\nWe made a short video together (you can find it at the end of the article as always) and some photos from the video. If you are interested in the silver to gray color of some trees, know that it is the color of \

. These trees were attacked by bark beetles. Since the place is located in the first protection zone of the national park, the trees remain in place. They are cut down only in places where they could threaten the safety of visitors or block the river by falling.

>\nSlibovaný přelet nad krátkým úsekem řeky si můžete prohlédnout na přiloženém videu.\n

![linkacz.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bucipuci/23tRtHQSTtpEUt2Kryo83QGdKRJZ7m2uzkufoxs72uiabH7ibsLUo2DzFHLmVdmtsKBF1.png)

> Procházka kolem řeky z Antýglu na Čeňkovu pilu (nebo obráceně) vám nabídne mnohem více atraktivních pohledů na řeku a okolí. Cestu kolem řeky zvládnete i s kočárky. Jen kola a vaše automobily budete muset zanechat na vyhrazených parkovištích. Tyto dopravní prostředky na naučnou stezku nesmí.
A pokud vás přepadne hlad nebo žízeň, nezapomeňte se zastavit v restauraci na Turnerově chatě :-)

> A walk around the river from Antýgl to Čeňkova pila (or vice versa) will offer you many more attractive views of the river and the surrounding area. You can also manage the journey around the river with strollers. You will only have to leave your bicycles and cars in the designated parking lots. These means of transport are not allowed on the nature trail.
And if you get hungry or thirsty, don't forget to stop at the restaurant at Turnerova cottage :-) ---

body.title: Book review of “Steps to strategic management: A guide for entrepreneurs” by Rick Molz
body.body:
/>

When it comes to reading business management books, most people believe that these books only appeal to a specific niche of readers, such as scholars and students who are involved in the study and promotion of the science of management.

However, the book titled “Steps to strategic management: A guide for entrepreneurs”, written by Dr. Rick Molz, Professor of International Business and Strategic Management at Concordia University in Canada, could be one of those cases that the above statement simply does not apply.

**What you can find in the book**

It wouldn’t be far from the truth to say that this book on strategic management is a real hidden gem in the ocean of books on the same subject.

Rick Molz manages to kill two birds with one stone.

On the one hand, he manages to capture the reader’s interest right from the beginning, through a basic plot that is based on two characters; himself teaching management at a local college, and a local entrepreneur who wants to grow his business, and asks Molz’s help to achieve that.

On the other hand, he explains complex strategic management concepts and theories, such as SWOT analysis and Porter’s 5 forces model, in a simple, straightforward, and practical way that enables the easy adoption and implementation of those ideas in practice by a business owner with no academic qualifications or background.

**What I think of the book**

I read the book in 2005, after 17 years had passed from its publication date.

The fact that it was published back in 1988, could cause people to think that it was outdated at the time, which would make it even more irrelevant and unsuitable for use in the modern business environment.

Far from it, I would say.

The book is as fresh and current today, as it was at the time that it was published.

This itself proves that the book has maintained its value through the years.

What is more, since the book has stood the test of time, the author’s approach to strategic management could offer a golden opportunity to today’s business owners and managers, if they decided to follow this approach.

**How this book has helped me**

Through this book, I have become familiar with a strategic approach that I didn’t know before, in terms of identifying, setting, achieving, and revising goals in both my personal and professional life.

It has fit perfectly and supplemented my traditional textbook approach to reaching goals.

I was pleasantly surprised to discover it back in 2005, and it hasn’t stopped amazing me with those little secrets that I manage to reveal every time that I find the opportunity to read it again.

**What I don’t like about the book**

There is one thing that I don’t like about this book, and this is the fact that it has not been promoted as much as it should have been.

If it was, more people would be able to discover it and benefit from the ideas presented in it.

In the Internet-era that we live in, it would be a great idea to offer readers a pre-taste of what’s included in the book.

For example, it would be a great idea to upload a preview of it to Google books.

I strongly believe that this would have a positive effect on the book’s sales, and further increase its reach to new readers.

**Where you can find the book**

You can find the book on Amazon.

Unfortunately, it is not available on Google books or Google Play.

_Sources and further reading:_

[Rick Molz – LinkedIn profile](https://ca.linkedin.com/in/rick-molz-b190394)

[Rick Molz – Biography](https://biography.omicsonline.org/canada/concordia-university/rick-molz-679164)

[Steps to strategic management – Goodreads](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/4341353-steps-strategic-mang)

[I read the 8 best business books of all time (so you don’t have to)—here are the only lessons you need to know](https://www.cnbc.com/2019/03/06/i-read-the-8-best-business-books-of-all-time-here-are-the-most-brilliant-lessons-from-each.html)

[An unorthodox reading list for readers](https://scottamartin.org/2015/11/25/an-unorthodox-reading-list-for-leaders/)

[The Five Stages of the Strategic Management Process](https://smallbusiness.chron.com/five-stages-strategic-management-process-18785.html)

* * *

body.body:
![The Theft of Privacy Header.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amaterasusolar/2458SZy3s5vRzF7mdWAL49Xd8VxuidkpcJtZ4MX25jc7UDj1yukurHPoKgqmbAZg6FcEg.png)
Who are They, who hide behind “The Government™,” using legalates (that They call “laws” but which are not Laws) to pretend Their theft of privacy is to “protect the children” – the duty of the parent(s) and ***not*** any construct that usurps power. Who are They – are They old enough?  Do We need to protect Them?  LOL! Seriously, the moneyed psychopaths in control on Our planet (by virtue of money) are going to extort Us of Our privacy while They hide and use Their money to push Their lies about why They are doing it.  Use that power that Their money gives Them to convince Us We need to give up Our privacy (like They work to get Us to give up Our guns). People like Me, who speak against Their machinations, will be silenced, and 1984 will bloom.  They can change the “facts” to suit Their aims and keep Us who know the truth quiet.  They will know who We are if We submit to Their unEthical extortion, and keep those of Us who refuse Their extortion (“dissidents,” don’t You know?) from speaking in the public forum at all. And why do They get a pass, why are They not required to meet the same standards as We are?  There is no One on this planet – or anywhere else – that stands above Me.  Do They stand above You? Yet They can hide and We cannot…
![Create.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amaterasusolar/23xepBpprep9yTAksh7f61StBvZymitWDervPRNP1EevovBuQGm2JuNv4yorqjaYxfjBE.png)
We need to do what We can to circumvent this mess, and I suggest We start a new connected community – not a “net” or a “web” to capture People with, but an electronic freedom fellowship, where joining is optional, no One is in charge, the source is open, and parents are expected to protect Their own children, not some artificial construct aiming to control Us 100%. Where People who break the Laws of Ethics (the only Laws) are the Ones We aim to solve for, not precriming the lot of Us. Where We have the freedom that is Ours. This is not about “protecting the children” with a psychopathic legal/governmafia mess.  “Age verification” is to thieve away web anonymity, to steal privacy. If anyOne is in doubt of My age here on this mess of a net, They might ponder the fact that I have been present here for 30 years.  And each year have claimed My age one year older than the year before.  I am approaching 70, and if My words, My descriptions of My past, are not enough to convince You that I am over 18, that’s Your problem.
![Bowing.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amaterasusolar/245n3aLBHptw6JCefhrFyFuqsHBbBVqqS98f8LkzLZSjQiZqoqnVEx5RR1KtAnxKM991K.png)
Why would You choose to kowtow to the hidden Ones who shield Themselves with an illegitimate construct?  Why would You consent to that construct ruling You?  Do You really believe that the governmafias of the world are there to care about ***You***? Please do not be that naïve. The Ones who own those for-profit corp(se)orations (all “governments” on Our planet these days are for-profit corp(se)orations owned by the same Ones) are aiming to get Us to consent to Their rule and rules, Their mandates, Their decrees, Their statutes, bills, codes, ordinances, and all. They have convinced Us that the pirate system, the “law of the sea,” the admiralty mess, is “law” and We must obey.  But none of that is Law.  It’s all legalates.  And We only must obey if We consent to that mess.
![_Three Laws (1).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amaterasusolar/243zfWVU3GocpqWs9QYq1zXf5RwgxzPVGZbDER3FkJupagr7jTxSGtt4pJV7zJGD2SZJd.png)
If We do not consent, We are not in Their jurisdiction.  We are under the only true Laws: **The three Laws of Ethics** (Natural Law expressed as the three things not to do): 1.  Do not willfully and without fully informed consent hurt or kill the flesh of anOther 2.  Do not willfully and without fully informed consent take or damage anything that does not belong to You alone 3.  Do not willfully defraud anOther (which can only happen without fully informed consent)
![Crown.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amaterasusolar/23r1kgoaa9RGKGC8FN7kcL466DsVACzKJmq9qrDQPJ7YeksxBJy7vRYfGxh31gYVCtczd.png)
So I hereby state, as one sovereign, that I expect and demand to be left alone, allowed My freedom of speech (which includes but is not limited to freedom of reach – limiting reach is censorship, and no One has the right to censor anOther), and the ability to continue My work for Humanity on Our planet, to return to Us all the rest that has been stolen from Us:  Our interest in the wealth of Our planet. Please see My articles linked below about legalates, about the heist of Humanity’s wealth, and more aimed to solve for the moneyed psychopaths in control on Our planet (by virtue of money). And if You can, get a new connection for Humanity build a freedom fellowship up and running, and free energy tech out in the open. And make Your stand, withdrawing consent from the psychopathic legal/governmafia mess, as a sovereign on Ethical ground (under the three Laws of Ethics ***only***.

body.body: Math Easy Solutions, **deuterium** is the neutral hydrogen isotope atom, written **²H or D**: 1 proton + 1 neutron, with 1 electron if it’s an atom. A **deuteron** is just the **nucleus of deuterium**, so it’s **D⁺**: 1 proton + 1 neutron, but **no electron**; that’s the positively charged ion that moves in electrolysis toward the cathode and can pick up an electron there to become neutral deuterium again [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deuterium) [LibreTexts](https://chem.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/General_Chemistry/Map%3A_Chemistry_(Zumdahl_and_Decoste)/18%3A_The_Representative_Elements/18.03%3A_The_Chemistry_of_Hydrogen). Your image has the core cell logic right: in an electrolytic cell, cations head to the cathode, so deuterons move there; “deuterium” is the broader neutral species, while “deuteron” is the stripped, charged version doing the ion-migration work Britannica Wikipedia. I’m not seeing a useful InLeo post on this exact chemistry distinction, so the clean distinction is: **deuterium = atom/isotope; deuteron = its bare nucleus/ion**.

body.title: THE DELMAR METHOD | @mariannewest's Freewrite Writing Prompt Day 3081: I’m just drifting | 🇬🇧 | 🇪🇸
body.body:
> Many of those who claim it’s impossible to separate the physical body and travel between planes likely do so because they’ve never attended a class with Professor Delmar. An hour in that classroom was like being adrift. At first, I’d try to stay afloat, following the monotonous drone of his voice, but soon the words would lose their meaning. My mind would eventually give up the struggle, and I was just drifting, moving away from the material world, until only the sharp ring of the bell managed to drag me back and anchor me to reality. ---

**“EL MÉTODO DELMAR”**
####
***

> Muchos de los que afirman que es imposible separarse del cuerpo físico y viajar entre planos probablemente lo hacen porque nunca han asistido a una clase del profesor Delmar. Una hora en aquel aula era como estar a la deriva. Al principio, intentaba mantenerme a flote, siguiendo el monótono murmullo de su voz, pero pronto las palabras perdían su significado. Mi mente acababa por rendirse y yo me dejaba llevar, alejándome del mundo material, hasta que solo el agudo sonido de la campana lograba arrastrarme de vuelta y anclarme a la realidad. ---
