title.title: What Is Written in Light Cannot Be Erased by Shadow
title.body:
# What Is Written in Light Cannot Be Erased by Shadow



You cannot unmake the deed once it is done. You cannot recall the arrow once it has flown, nor un-speak the word once it has left the tongue. And yet—you persist. Vote by vote, click by click, you cast your judgment not upon the guilty, but upon the blameless: the Bilpcoin collective, yes, but also hundreds, thousands of souls whose only crime was to exist in the wrong light, at the wrong hour, beneath the wrong gaze.

Consider the ledger of your intent—not as data, but as testimony:

> A name appears: *freebornsociety*. A number follows: −2.04%.  
> Then *meritocracy*, quieter, colder: −0.54%.  
> *the-unblinking-mirror*—a meditation on truth, on transformation—is met not with reflection, but with recoil: −1.79%, −2.01%, −0.28%...  
> A chorus of negation. A symphony composed in minor keys.

We see you.  
Not as abstraction, but as pattern.  
Not as accident, but as design.

At Bilpcoin, we do not look away. We bear witness.  
#buildawhalescam #buildawhalefarm #themarkymarkscam #hurtlockerscam  
These are not mere hashtags. They are signposts planted in the soil of memory. Warnings etched not in sand, but in stone.

Meanwhile, the machinery hums.  
*smooth* votes 100%. *smooth-a*, *smooth-b*, *smooth-c*, *smooth-d*, *smooth-e*, *smooth-f*—a constellation of accounts, a galaxy of influence, all orbiting a single will. Delegations flow like rivers: 918,809 HP… 837,289 HP… 812,122 HP… A treasury of power, not earned in the marketplace of ideas, but accumulated in the quiet chambers of leverage.

Rewards are claimed with metronomic precision:  
22,464.696 HP… 34,463.893 HP… 135,643.242 HP…  
Day after day, a harvest reaped not from labor, but from position.

But truth is not a token.  
It cannot be devalued by downvote.  
It cannot be delegated, staked, or withdrawn into a savings account yielding 12% interest.  
Truth is like dawn: you may close your eyes, you may curse the light, you may cast your ballot against the sun—  
but darkness does not thereby become the truth.

> *\

*

We do not ask for vengeance.  
Vengeance is a fire that consumes the one who carries it.

We ask only for accountability.  
That influence be measured not in Hive Power, but in integrity.  
That community remain just that—a *common unity*—and not a battlefield where the powerful trample the voiceless beneath the banner of \

For in the end, it is not the blockchain that judges us.  
It is time.  
It is memory.  
It is history—that relentless scribe who knows no delete key, no undo command, no escape from the record we have made.

What you have done is written.  
Not in disappearing ink, but in the permanent ledger of consequence.  
And though you may downvote a thousand posts, you cannot downvote the truth that one day, the mirror will blink—and in its reflection, you will see not the enemy you sought to silence, but the architect of your own undoing.

—  
*Written with pen, not keystroke.  
For those who still believe: words carry weight, and weight endures.*

title.title: ABSTRACT FLORAL DETAILS
title.body:
![Kopia – Essence.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ladytruckview/23wgcRQXyc6x3jcbPPwGJ8svx4UikQiMgvC4UVpjUQTFh5QBZMoGa2DJdaXTYqX1iSzYp.jpg)

These flowers were originally pink.
I found them near a train station in Germany, in the already familiar Torgau.
That’s where I was learning to experiment with aperture settings.
As you can see it didn’t stop at technique. I also started experimenting with color.
I pushed the tones towards warmer, almost fiery shades.
I wanted them to visually resemble fire.

After these adjustments even AI couldn’t identify the species of these flowers, so this time there won’t be an educational part. 😄
I also wasn’t able to check it myself — I deleted the original photos a long time ago and had no reference point.

If any of you recognize what kind of flower this is, feel free to share in the comments — I’d love to know 🙂

What do you think about this kind of approach?
Do you prefer natural colors or do you sometimes like to let your imagination run free, like I do?

title.title: Sea hare (Eng/Esp)
title.body:
> I love gazing at the seascape, so on a recent trip to Güirintal Beach, I came across an animal that caught my eye because of its shape and color. It was also an adult specimen, so it was quite large—about 10 cm. After doing a little research, I discovered that I had stumbled upon a sea hare (Aplysia dactylomela), a soft-bodied mollusk that moved like jelly. It is known as a sea hare because it has two to four appendages on its head called rhinophores that resemble the ears of a land hare. I found this specimen on the shore, near the rocks. When I go on excursions, my father comes along; he’s passionate about nature and loves to explore. He’s also very gentle when handling animals, never causing them any harm—and, of course, always coming out unscathed. While I handle the filming and photography—the easiest job 😅—together we make an excellent team.
![1000099981.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/Ep3fFDZoa2kNWhVXXx7DRaCf8rzNzEG4DcyQekDgjkPnwdm6Ut1ZhCocktcQN55dzKi.jpg)
![1000099976.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/Eou8d8poDfbrRsubAcK19EdPPBTPSK2fsxzb4ePajZqqPv2z8YazP6QxjFxNUkPzVXK.jpg)
This sea hare was cream-colored with small black ring-shaped spots. I noticed that it also changed color when it expelled purple defensive ink after feeling threatened; they do this to distract predators and escape from them. According to Chapman and Fox (1969), this ink is a byproduct of consuming red algae. However, it is not toxic to humans, so these mollusks are harmless, which put my mind at ease. Like the slugs they are, they can crawl along the seafloor with great ease and also swim. The photographs show several of their characteristics; they resemble snails, but each rhinophore functions as a sensory organ, and beneath each one is an eye. The rhinophores have an olfactory epithelium, which allows them to detect food and pheromones.
![1000099972.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/Eos1kzXosgxTfcEXoriBfeqce2nphxVVihDfsj5As23cxMojyrNA9Sr95McdnRWBvTy.jpg)
![1000099970.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/EoiWfMfUQ7qf2jDNrJ9NVSfi91opGkZWGzU1oEibesZCLG792Eb2NrS5pTVWocXxLdC.jpg)
![1000099995.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/EowGdAwAsyLd6ryfrkPSQhKMTntwPqWU5gq2ADiuQwdPj5uPATTz8dQvx3WX6JySJyA.jpg)
Sea hares are herbivores; they feed on green and red algae. Juveniles typically eat red algae, while adults eat green algae. An interesting fact is that the pigmentation of their bodies is determined by their diet. According to my research, these sea slugs are hermaphrodites; they possess both male and female reproductive organs, but they are unable to self-fertilize, so they need a mate to reproduce. When I looked at the sea hare from below, I noticed that it has highly developed parapodia; they look like wing-like appendages, and through contractions, it can move them in a undulating motion. These particular sea slugs are nocturnal; they come out to feed in complete darkness, while during the day they take refuge in quiet, dark areas, usually among the rocks.
![1000099986.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/Ep7v4ca7VShNnogRbaqUFA7se4PcxRWMiuxg9dKCgJgfLbTxmnjF53eEDZ8Hbb86wDX.jpg)
![1000099983.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/Ep1XTXjYqNDEX6MT9PKa4N1LPnr7bfiEg3zT3hsaumwhQq9ud2UefqSVJ5VH5A4PQgK.jpg)
![1000099958.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/Eoc8Yoe7dvWTfqgJb8191VczRQuLKQftbfPp2TquYD8Ucpcru954reXQ3PYk6R2CzXA.jpg)
![1000099955.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/EoEqxp4PQRk6ejZLMTKTtNWx4evVGxaweUiy3jwKoq5h7cPpUP9Rp6zMTSv2uAywGrU.jpg)
Although they may not seem like it, sea hares play an important role in the marine ecosystem because they help maintain an appropriate amount of algae; otherwise, there would be an excess that would cause an imbalance—the so-called green tide—which is harmful to humans and animals. It was very interesting to come across this animal, which, backlit, looks like a piece of leopard skin, with its striking pattern and gelatinous body. It’s a rarity, and although at first it seemed somewhat repulsive to me, it reminded me of land slugs and snails; in fact, some researchers suggest that these sea hares are a type of snail that evolved after becoming accustomed to living without a protective shell. What is certain is that they are related, as they belong to the same class (Gastropoda) and phylum (Mollusca).
![1000099953.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/EoGyQvSHVojZavsQ314gdySNV4J4D2Nsrn5vFqaX1rBDGPdR9m2z5M2j4xx78ikB8jN.jpg)
![1000099945.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/EoGxzg6iiiTKrBrXSuh99U7kjEDJkGS4N3p7P3cP5ALYJMfyQJnWh9oXm5z5jKo5Ag8.jpg)
![1000099960.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/EopuNSjDWtpFhPLjHh848j4oenijTt1ad72mjWXb6csuEGK8u7wHgYSwijP8PcnPvf5.jpg)
*** ***
## Versión en Español

> Adoro contemplar el paisaje marino, así que en una nueva expedición a la playa Güirintal encontré un animal que llamó mi atención por su forma y color, además era una especie adulta, así que tenía un tamaño considerable de unos 10 cm. Investigando un poco descubrí entonces que me había tropezado con una liebre o babosa de mar (Aplysia dactylomela), un molusco de cuerpo blando que se movía como una gelatina.
![1000099981.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/Ep3fFDZoa2kNWhVXXx7DRaCf8rzNzEG4DcyQekDgjkPnwdm6Ut1ZhCocktcQN55dzKi.jpg)
![1000099976.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/Eou8d8poDfbrRsubAcK19EdPPBTPSK2fsxzb4ePajZqqPv2z8YazP6QxjFxNUkPzVXK.jpg)
Se le conoce como liebre de mar porque posee de dos a cuatro apéndices en su cabeza llamados rinóforos que lucen semejantes a las orejas de una liebre terrestre. Este espécimen lo encontré en la orilla, cerca de las piedras. Cuando voy de excursión mi padre me acompaña, él es un apasionado de la naturaleza y le encanta explorar, también tiene mucho tacto para manipular animales sin causarles ningún daño y, por supuesto, salir ileso. Mientras yo me encargo de grabar y tomar fotografías, el trabajo más sencillo 😅, juntos hacemos un excelente equipo. Esta liebre de mar era de color crema con pequeñas manchas negras en forma de anillos. Noté que también cambió de color cuando expulsó tinta púrpura defensiva ya que se sintió amenazada, esto lo hacen para distraer a los depredadores y escapar de ellos. Esta tinta, según Chapman y Fox (1969) es un subproducto de la ingesta de algas rojas. Sin embargo, no es tóxica para los humanos, por tanto, estos moluscos son inofensivos, lo cual me generó mayor tranquilidad.
![1000099972.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/Eos1kzXosgxTfcEXoriBfeqce2nphxVVihDfsj5As23cxMojyrNA9Sr95McdnRWBvTy.jpg)
![1000099970.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/EoiWfMfUQ7qf2jDNrJ9NVSfi91opGkZWGzU1oEibesZCLG792Eb2NrS5pTVWocXxLdC.jpg)
![1000099995.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/EowGdAwAsyLd6ryfrkPSQhKMTntwPqWU5gq2ADiuQwdPj5uPATTz8dQvx3WX6JySJyA.jpg)
Como babosas que son, pueden arrastrarse por el fondo marino con mucha facilidad y también nadar. En las fotografías se pueden apreciar varias de sus características, parece familia de los caracoles, sin embargo cada rinófono funciona como órgano sensorial y debajo de cada uno se encuentra un ojo. Los rinóforos poseen un epitelio para la olfacción, así detectan alimentos y feromonas. Las liebres de mar son herbívoras, se alimentan de algas verdes y rojas. Las jóvenes suelen consumir algas rojas, mientras que las adultas consumen algas verdes, un dato interesante es que la pigmentación de su cuerpo viene dada por la alimentación. Según mi investigación, estas babosas son hermafroditas, poseen órganos sexuales masculinos y femeninos, pero no son capaces de autofecundarse, así que necesitan de una pareja para reproducirse.
![1000099986.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/Ep7v4ca7VShNnogRbaqUFA7se4PcxRWMiuxg9dKCgJgfLbTxmnjF53eEDZ8Hbb86wDX.jpg)
![1000099983.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/Ep1XTXjYqNDEX6MT9PKa4N1LPnr7bfiEg3zT3hsaumwhQq9ud2UefqSVJ5VH5A4PQgK.jpg)
![1000099958.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/Eoc8Yoe7dvWTfqgJb8191VczRQuLKQftbfPp2TquYD8Ucpcru954reXQ3PYk6R2CzXA.jpg)
![1000099955.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/EoEqxp4PQRk6ejZLMTKTtNWx4evVGxaweUiy3jwKoq5h7cPpUP9Rp6zMTSv2uAywGrU.jpg)
Cuando aprecié a la liebre de mar por debajo me di cuenta que posee parapodios muy desarrollados, lucen como apéndices similares a alas, por medio de contracciones las puede mover de forma ondulante. Estas particulares babosas tienen hábitos nocturnos, salen a comer en plena oscuridad, mientras que en el día se refugian en zonas tranquilas y oscuras, por lo regular entre las rocas. Aunque no lo parezcan, las liebres de mar cumplen un rol importante en el ecosistema marino porque contribuyen a mantener una cantidad adecuada de algas, de lo contrario, habría un exceso que causaría un desequilibrio, la conocida marea verde, que resulta perjudicial para seres humanos y animales. Fue muy interesante encontrarme con este animal, que a contraluz parece un pedazo de piel de leopardo, con su diseño llamativo y su cuerpo gelatinoso. Es una rareza y aunque en principio me pareció algo repulsivo, me hizo recordar a las babosas de tierra y a los caracoles, inclusive algunos investigadores asoman que estas liebres de mar son una especie de caracol que evolucionó tras adaptarse a vivir sin el caparazón protector. Lo que sí es cierto es que comparten el parentesco al pertenecer a la misma clase (Gastropoda) y filo (Mollusca).   *** *** ✓Photos from my personal gallery, edited with Fotocollage. ✓Text translated with DeepL.

title.title: Mishti Doi of Bogura: A sweet dessert.
title.body:
Hello everyone! There are 64 districts in Bangladesh. Each district has traditional food items. Two years ago I visited Bogura district which is famous for Sweet Curd, Mishti Doi in Bengali. The fame of Mishti Doi is beyond Bangladesh. When the experts of Bogura go abroad for work they take curd from here for their colleagues and friends. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmS2sGJ84EATEWxrwmV3AsXzF488vtAFrBUsoPFbaKs6Ey/1776867151963.jpg)

I had a training in Rural Development Academy (RDA) on food safety. There we visited the industry where curd is made by the skilled doi maker. We saw the process of making sweet curd. First they take fresh milk of cows. Then they heat the milk untill the milk becomes a two thirds portion. Then sugar and seed curd mixed with it. There are a lot of curd pot made of clay. Before setting the curd the pots are heated for disinfect. Then the pots filled by liquid milk which are ready to set. Then they covered the pots with a large Jhapi made of bamboo. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPKzqBWZkmr3sPHkbUcwwwVpedgjaHRw3L33vQTqB1a69/1776867182241.jpg)

The curds sets overnight. The next morning the curd become ready to sell. Curd is a source of vitamins, mineral and calcium. The curd and yogurt are full of lacto bacillus bacteria which help us for digesting foods. Every one in our country loves this food. Especially children like curd most. In Bangladesh curd is served as dessert almost every function. I remember that when I was child a kind of sweet icy curd sold in small glass. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQme295mad2ekixu4P2VERXbGQn3qJEq9kgpq2jtrNBzELn/1776867182435.jpg)

Now a days that is not found. Now curd sells in food grade plastic cups, clay cups,  plastic bowls or clay pots. Yogurt is  sour in taste and it is also popular in our counyry. It is better for digesting than sweet curd. The making process of yogurt is almost the same but no sugar added with it. Would you like to taste sweet curd and yogurt? I think if you taste these you will be a fan of these dessert.  

If you ever come in Bangladesh you must taste mishti doi and tok doi (yogurt). Would you like to miss a nice taste! Oh! You can make curd in your home also.  The processing of making sweet curd in home is available in internet. My mom often made it for me in my childhood but there was no telephone or mobile phone in our house. You can also try this at home.

body.body: 1/5 🧵 Scott Stringer is now arguing his 2021 mayoral collapse wasn’t just bad luck or a brutal allegation cycle — it was a political hit job. His new claim: operatives tied to Andrew Yang’s orbit helped manufacture the accusations that blew up his campaign. That’s not a minor twist. It’s the whole damn case.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 2/5 🧵 The article says Stringer is suing his accuser, Jean Kim, for defamation and now wants to add **Bradley Tusk** and **Tusk Strategies** to the lawsuit. According to court filings, an unnamed consultant who worked for Yang told Stringer last year that “Tusk manufactured each of the defamatory statements” that wrecked his then-rising campaign. Stringer says he vetted that information and tried to resolve it directly before expanding the suit.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/5 🧵 The original allegations were serious and politically devastating. In 2021, Kim accused Stringer of groping her, touching her sexually without consent, and repeatedly making advances when she was an unpaid intern on his 2001 public advocate campaign. She also publicly claimed he asked her, “Why won’t you f–k me?” Those accusations landed at exactly the worst possible moment — when Stringer was still viable in the NYC mayoral race.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 Kim flatly rejects Stringer’s new theory. In court, she called the case “a continuation of the harassment against me” and said she has never met Bradley Tusk or even been in the same room with him. Tusk Strategies’ CEO Chris Coffey also denied any link, saying nobody at Tusk had ever met Kim and arguing she’d been talking about her accusations for years before the race. In other words: Stringer says coordinated smear; Kim and Tusk say desperate rewrite.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body:
5/5 🧵 Politically, the damage was real whether the conspiracy claim holds up or not. A poll shortly before the allegations had Stringer at **11%** and in third place; roughly two weeks after Kim’s press conference, he dropped to **9%**; by Election Day he finished with **5.5%** of first-round votes and was eliminated. So the piece is really about two fights at once: a legal fight over who engineered the scandal, and a political postmortem over whether a campaign was destroyed by truth, timing, or dirty tricks. 📎 Source

body.title: Simple Magic             ...Part 1.          ...Second Regard
body.body:
*We are always the same age inside. ― Gertrude Stein*


![Simple Magic.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/johnjgeddes/23xempstMwoNbQyibGRGyVsqKdVY4MhnuUhQ2Qtoqd9ep5BzQmKdEA9FWUTpiCYa3mJEk.jpg)


Mikey looked at his grandmother as she sat propped up on pillows in her huge iron bed. He brought the radio to keep her company, but she had called him in to turn it off. “Sorry, Love, but that incessant noise is enough to drive me to drink.” He puzzled over the expression and added gravely, “Uncle Henry drinks—a lot. When Dad went up to bed the other night he finished all the beer left on the table.” Nan grimaced, “I always said that the last drop in the bottle’s poison.” “Can we look in the cedar chest today, Nan? Please?”

His grandmother began to cough and reached for the Kleenex box beside her. When she caught her breath, she motioned him toward her and reached out and tousled his hair. “Very well. You’ve been patient, haven’t you? Open up the chest and you’ll see a small wooden box—take it out and bring it here.” Mikey opened the chest and paused inhaling the fragrance of the cedar lining. He spotted the box and fished it out and dutifully brought it to Nan’s bedside. She grasped the box and sat it on her lap and waited until Mikey climbed up and sat beside her before opening the lid. Inside were sepia photographs of unfamiliar people, all of whom were frozen in formal poses and all exhibited the same serious expression on their faces as they stared straight ahead into the camera lens. Their eyes all looked so dark and fierce that Mikey nestled closer to his grandmother’s side.

“Black Irish, we are, to be sure.” She laughed at the ridiculous formality of the dress and the stern faces of relatives, some of whose names even she had forgotten. “There’s a picture of Henry and Charles. That was taken at the barracks at the Exhibition grounds.” She flipped through the photographs and suddenly Mikey reached out and grasped her hand. “Who’s this Nanny?” The old woman smiled and shook her head. “He’s handsome, isn’t he? That’s Lou-Lou, your uncle— only sixteen there and too young for the War.”  The photo revealed a handsome young dark-haired soldier with a cigarette jauntily hanging from his lip. Unlike the other photos, this one seemed so spontaneous and real it took Mikey’s breath away.

“But Mom said Lou-Lou died in the War—that he was a sniper and was killed by a German machine gun. If he was too young, why did they let him go?” “Why indeed, that is the question.” His Nan looked away and daubed at her eyes with the balled-up Kleenex she clutched in her hand. “Is it true what Mom says, that Lou-Lou’s boots could be heard stomping up the stairs in the house on Atkin Avenue?” “Without a lie, it’s true. That house was haunted I swear. I remember that hot August in 1918 when I lay sweltering in a fever in the back bedroom. All your aunts and uncles were huddled in that little room with me, afraid of the creaking of the joists. They were only young then—except for your Uncle John who was at work at the General Electric plant on Dufferin Street.

I had the Spanish flu and I was burning up. I had been washing floors all that week for a family on Havelock Street, but that day was so weak I couldn’t get out of bed. The children were so frightened that they had closed the window and I was just sweltering in my bed. I kept crying out, ‘Won’t someone please open the window?’ but no one moved. Then, suddenly, the knob of the bedroom door spun around and around madly and the door blew open and buried itself in the wall. It hit with such force that the knob was wedged behind the wooden lathes under the plaster and when your Uncle John came home later, it took him and Jock forever to put their feet on the wall and pull on that door for all they were worth just to free it.”

Mikey swallowed hard. “Could it have been the wind, Nanny?” “There wasn’t a breath of wind that day and the house locked up tighter than a drum. Your Uncle John, God rest his soul, went all around the house looking for an explanation but found nothing amiss.” “Do you think perhaps it was Lou-Lou?” His grandmother looked sharply at him. “Lou-Lou, you say? And what would be making you think that?” She looked off into the distance then softened for a moment and whispered to him, “You’re a good boy Mikey. You have the second regard—I told your Mom that right from the start. You’ve been gifted, my boy.”

“Am I like you, Nanny? Will I be able to read tea leaves too?” “Well, I don’t know if your Mom would be wanting me to fill your head with such idle notions.” “Mom says that people would be lined up around the block waiting for a reading. Did they pay you, Nan?” “I never charged. The odd person would give me a few dollars and I’d go with Mrs. Franklin to play Bingo—I usually won.” She laughed and started to cough again. Meg appeared in the doorway, a stern look on her face. “Now come along Mikey, your Nan needs her rest.” 

Later that day, Mikey crept back into Nanny’s room. He felt sorry for her, bed-ridden and all alone. He sat by her bed listening to her regular breathing. Suddenly, she opened her eyes and stared at him. “Oh, it’s you, Child. Did you see them?” “See what Nanny?” “The pictures on the walls.” She motioned to a large white wall adjacent to her bed. “Yesterday I saw clouds and grass—trees waving and men upside-down walking and making merry.” “Why can’t I see the pictures, Nanny?” “You’ve come too late in the day, Mikey. You need to come just before tea. I swear I’ll see the cat and the fiddle one day here upon my walls.”

Mikey thought it marvelous and told Meg, his mother. She grew very stern. She threw up her hands and in desperation turned to his father. “I’ve just about had it, Ross. Ma’s filling his head with all sorts of foolish notions. Why just the other day I caught her drawing the picture for him—you know, the one of the snake curled around the rose? No good’ll come of it, and that’s for sure.” Mikey was sorry he said anything, but wanted to see the pictures. He made up his mind to visit Nanny at teatime the next day.

To be continued...

body.body:
> Ella lo cuenta y se ríe. Yo le miro los ojos, imagino la escena y también me río. Dice que fue a sacarse una muela. Quedó con la cara hinchada, como un globo. Y su nieto, que es un bandido —así lo llama ella—, se quedó al lado todo el rato. No para ayudarla. Para esperar el momento justo y sacarle una foto con la boca torcida. Ella no podía ni hablar, dice. Y se ríe. Y yo me río con ella. Esa imagen me queda dando vueltas. Una mujer mayor, recién salida del dentista, con la mejilla como un puño. Y un chico de quince años con el celular en la mano, acechando. Sin maldad. Por puro deporte. Porque ver a la abuela con cara de pescado es demasiado bueno para dejarlo pasar. Y ella lo sabe. Por eso lo cuenta. Por eso se ríe. Pero después que ella se va, me quedo pensando en otra cosa. Ese nieto, el bandido, un día treinta años. Veinte años después de esa foto. Y ella, la de la cara hinchada, ya no estará. O quizá sí, pero más vieja, más lenta, con otras muelas menos. Y entonces imagino al nieto. Un tipo grande, con hijos propios, con cuentas que pagar. Una noche cualquiera, aburrido, scrolleando el celular. Y se topa con esa foto. La cara de su abuela, torcida, ridícula, con la mejilla como un puño. ¿Qué hace? ***
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTF7yavw7UN32wkiCZ9BzRWFRcv3miPFgLAQqmezcWt39/1776736752987.jpg) [unsplash](https://unsplash.com/es/fotos/hombre-con-camisa-de-vestir-azul-montando-caballo-marron-durante-el-dia-8765Rq3vcfk)
***

>\n\nPrimero se ríe. Solo, en el sillón. Se acuerda de ese día. Del dolor de ella, de la paciencia de ella, de cómo ella igual se dejó fotografiar. Después, quizá, se quedará mirando la foto un rato largo. Y la risa se le irá poniendo rara. Porque ve los ojos de ella. Y en los ojos, aunque la boca esté torcida, hay algo que no es dolor. Hay ternura. Hay confianza. Hay un \

. Ahí el nieto, veinte años después, entiende todo. Entiende que esa foto no era un meme. Era un documento de amor. Ella sabía que él la iba a guardar. Sabía que algún día él iba a necesitar verla así: frágil, hinchada, pero riéndose igual. El crecimiento personal,, es eso. No es volverse perfecto. Es poder mirar atrás y encontrar las pruebas de que fuiste querido. Aunque las pruebas sean una foto de con la cara desfigurada. Aunque el cariño haya llegado disfrazado de broma de adolescente. Y el amor filial, el de verdad, es ese también. El que se permite ser torpe. El que no necesita poses. El que te saca la peor foto y la guarda, y veinte años después tú la ves y lloras un poco, pero lloras agradecido. ***
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbf6CBdf3bir1VHrpU7ocaDAUSHzQ7JxHx7AgKfPZ5tfo/1776736753040.jpg) [unsplash](https://unsplash.com/es/fotos/hombre-con-camisa-blanca-y-pantalones-negros-caminando-por-la-acera-durante-el-dia-EYVodv0WY5o)
***

> La abuela, mientras contaba la historia, no sabía que estaba dando una lección. Solo se reía de su cara hinchada. Pero esa risa, para el nieto de hoy, para el hombre de mañana, aunque nieto igual será tal vez, algo agradable para recordar. Y le alcanza. Así que eso. Sáquense fotos en los peores momentos. Guárdenlas. Cuéntenlas en una cocina con café de por medio. Dentro de veinte años van a entender por qué. **© Marabuzal, 2026. Contenido original. Todos los derechos reservados.** ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVDUKVA6YugQdRrhGACmnps8ddBkV8W6UwGEo9DwaNQxF/1768408479017.jpg)

> **A Touch of Tenderness (ESP-ENG)** She tells the story and laughs. I look into her eyes, imagine the scene, and laugh too. She says she went to get a tooth pulled. Her face was swollen, like a balloon. And her grandson, who's a rascal—that's what she calls him—stayed by her side the whole time. Not to help her. To wait for the perfect moment to snap a picture of her with her mouth twisted. She couldn't even speak, she says. And she laughs. And I laugh with her. That image keeps replaying in my mind. An older woman, fresh from the dentist, her cheek swollen like a fist. And a fifteen-year-old boy with his cell phone in his hand, lurking. Without malice. Just for fun. Because seeing his grandmother with a fishy face is too good to pass up. And she knows it. That's why she tells the story. That's why she laughs. But after she leaves, I'm left thinking about something else. That grandson, the rascal, thirty years later. Twenty years after that photo. And she, the one with the swollen face, will no longer be there. Or perhaps she will be, but older, slower, with fewer teeth. And then I imagine the grandson. A grown man, with children of his own, with bills to pay. One ordinary night, bored, scrolling through his phone. And he comes across that photo. His grandmother's face, twisted, ridiculous, her cheek like a fist. What does he do? ***
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTF7yavw7UN32wkiCZ9BzRWFRcv3miPFgLAQqmezcWt39/1776736752987.jpg) [unsplash](https://unsplash.com/es/fotos/hombre-con-camisa-de-vestir-azul-montando-caballo-marron-durante-el-dia-8765Rq3vcfk)
***

>\n\nFirst he laughs. Alone, in the armchair. He remembers that day. Her pain, her patience, how she still let him photograph her. Then, perhaps, he'll stare at the photo for a long time. And his laughter will start to feel strange. Because he sees her eyes.  And in her eyes, even though her mouth is twisted, there's something that isn't pain. There's tenderness. There's trust. There's a \

There, the grandson, twenty years later, understands everything. He understands that that photo wasn't a meme. It was a testament to love. She knew he would keep it. She knew that one day he would need to see her like that: fragile, swollen, but still laughing. Personal growth is that. It's not about becoming perfect. It's about being able to look back and find the proof that you were loved. Even if the proof is a photo with a disfigured face. Even if the affection came disguised as a teenage joke. And true filial love is that too. The kind that allows itself to be clumsy. The kind that doesn't need to pose. The kind that takes the worst picture of you and keeps it, and twenty years later you look at it and cry a little, but you cry with gratitude. ***
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbf6CBdf3bir1VHrpU7ocaDAUSHzQ7JxHx7AgKfPZ5tfo/1776736753040.jpg) [unsplash](https://unsplash.com/es/fotos/hombre-con-camisa-blanca-y-pantalones-negros-caminando-por-la-acera-durante-el-dia-EYVodv0WY5o)
***

> The grandmother, as she told the story, didn't realize she was teaching a lesson. She was just laughing at her swollen face. But that laugh, for today's grandson, for the man of tomorrow—though perhaps still a grandson—is something pleasant to remember. And that's enough for him. So there you have it. Take pictures of yourselves at your worst. Keep them. Talk about them in a kitchen over coffee. In twenty years you'll understand why. **© Marabuzal, 2026. Original content. All rights reserved.**

body.body: 3/5 🧵 The doc also ties a lot of that hardness back to childhood. Hogan describes growing up poor in South Tampa with a father who was “rough,” emotionally cold, and constantly comparing him unfavorably to his older brother Allan. That seems to be where the chip-on-the-shoulder engine got built: insecurity, toughness, and proving himself turned into the whole Hulk machine.

body.body: 4/5 🧵 On the career side, there are two big reveals. First: he wasn’t even sold on “Hulk Hogan” as a name because “Hogan” sounded Irish and he’s Italian. Second: his break with Vince McMahon Sr. over **Rocky III** was a real fork in the road. McMahon reportedly told him if he took the movie, he was done. Hogan took it anyway. body.title: 电车博物馆&挖泥船
body.body:
离隧道不远的地方就是老码头，老头子说带我去里面看看，因为那里面也有不少小景点，况且他每年还交了入门费， 不看白不看，于是我们俩就开车进到了码头里面。 

没想到里面的景点确实很多呢，关键是这个是被我忽略了的地方，我总觉得码头麽，就是旅客上下船的地方，有什么好看的！其实这里面不仅有很多好看的小景点，还有许多爱国教育基地呢，里面还有史记博物馆。 

最直接的进门就能看到的就是电车博物馆，但其实电车博物馆就是停在那里两个电车车厢，还有两个机车头，并没有详细的介绍电车的历史或者哪怕是简介啥的， 我觉得本来这个设计挺好的，可以让游客们看看电车的历史及发展，毕竟大连的电车是有历史年头的，但是并没有看到，后来问一个老师傅，这里到底有没有电车博物馆， 他说就是这两个电车车厢，其它的并没有。

![博物馆.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPDfGiP1oFUBwoA6TBWgFDnR16WNr3VZnr1ugS5dH5h4d/%E5%8D%9A%E7%89%A9%E9%A6%86.jpg)

![dianche.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSQHyMY9y1pg1QfUfwzxYJQLDnzmX2hjtFCxerepNTCen/dianche.jpg)
这个准备的有点不充分，如果真布置起来也不是什么麻烦事儿，在车厢里就可以准备呀，而这两个车厢都是空的！

不过车厢附近的航空卫星倒是很应景，游客们可以拍照打卡，尤其是小朋友们一定喜欢这个小景点。 

![hangtian.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSv2EjHwDb3ey9agTh981X2iuhGDLR4cL5P2aCfQzNGWA/hangtian.jpg)

![huojian.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmasCY9CiH5NX9ZcAhbGLry6MchpS6S3zitrCQB1aqj9M9/huojian.jpg)

附近还有很多的游船，游客们可以乘坐游船观光，穿上橙色的救生衣，排着队等待着上船，虽然没到旅游旺季，但也有不少的人在排队呢，看来还是有很多外地的游客喜欢这个体验，本地人我想是很少去坐这个观光船的。 

本来想去参观一个史记馆，没想到竟然吃了个闭门羹，隔着玻璃看了一下，里面是历史介绍啥的，可能是没到旅游旺季还没有对外开放吧！

![史记馆.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXMNmFzewBFLka4x84FCio3RsAZ2YV6pXRWuMNLCHmiCK/%E5%8F%B2%E8%AE%B0%E9%A6%86.jpg)


![room.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQma7De2VoffZFhjgsxqoA1q6zPcqyQdziMBMmXDEKEMnBg/room.jpg)


往码头的深处走去，那边有条船样子很奇特，从来没见过，老头子说是挖泥船，上面有两个想炮弹一样的长筒，那就是深入水下作业的工具，将泥沙从水下吸上来。 这个还是我第一次见，这庞然大物还真是气派，原来水下作业需要这么个大家伙！

![3 hao.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeGqPgWjMVn6n8crt9ad3GWDvULLGUiLYkftBTfi7NnGD/3%20hao.jpg)


挖泥船的旁边还有个庞然大物，看起来也是海上作业的一个平台！这次真的是见识了！😉

![chuanjia.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYmTYybxzqqnc9Mo1LaUX5mFTCeHnyCmHMvxxety4W6iL/chuanjia.jpg)
码头里面还有一个巨大的一起球场，也是一个训练基地，里面有个初中生正在接受训练，他不停的奔跑，教练在培训他，看样子孩子跑的不理想，教练不是很满意。 后来休息的时候，跟教练聊了一下，原来他是给中考的孩子做辅导，一个半小时大约200元左右，中考在即，这样要求培训的孩子还是挺多的！


![jiaolian.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQTU68Fnh3MvMvApdMCwk69hPgc1ahVnxb26px71YZqXt/jiaolian.jpg)

其实老码头里面很大，要走的话，没有一个小时左右是溜达不完的，不过我们俩只是在外围溜达了一会儿，没有在往里面走，现在游客也不多，一切看起来都是那么的寂静，现在还处于淡季期，人还是比较少的。

**Exercise 1 -- AI code audit:**

Typical AI-generated vulnerabilities: (a) SQL injection via f-string/format in SELECT query, (b) path traversal -- `open(filename)` without validating the path stays within allowed directory, (c) XSS via innerHTML assignment of user content, (d) insecure deserialization via pickle.load, (e) security group with 0.0.0.0/0 on all ports. body.body: 1/5 🧵 The creepy part isn’t “11 linked disappearances.” It’s that several people tied to sensitive defense and nuclear work vanished in ways that look almost staged: leaving home on foot, skipping wallets/phones/keys, and in two cases taking only a handgun. The article’s main point is simpler than the headline hype: the similarities are real, but there’s still no proven master connection.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 2/5 🧵 The central case is retired Air Force Maj. Gen. William “Neil” McCasland, 68. He disappeared from his Albuquerque home on Feb. 27 after his wife stepped out briefly. He reportedly left behind his phone, electronics, and prescription glasses, but may have taken his wallet, hiking boots, and a .38 revolver. In a 911 call, his wife said she feared he had “planned not to be found,” which shifts this from random missing-person mystery into something much darker.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/5 🧵 McCasland’s background is what fuels the speculation machine. He held senior Pentagon roles tied to nuclear science, space research, and defense programs, and had commanded the Air Force Research Laboratory. The article also drags in UFO-world intrigue: a congressman said he’d contacted McCasland about UFO research, and leaked Podesta-era emails allegedly linked McCasland to Tom DeLonge’s alien-intel orbit. That’s the flashy part — but it’s still atmosphere, not evidence.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 The article then lines up other New Mexico disappearances with overlapping patterns. Anthony Chavez, a retired Los Alamos engineer who worked at DARHT, vanished in May 2025 after leaving home on foot, with wallet, keys, cigarettes, and car left behind. Steven Garcia, a government contractor with high security clearance tied to nuclear weapons components, disappeared in August 2025 after leaving on foot carrying only a handgun. Melissa Casias, a Los Alamos employee, vanished in June 2025 after being seen walking alone; her car, purse, keys, wallet, and both phones were left at home, and the phones had been factory-reset.

So the takeaway is: there are disturbing pattern overlaps, a lot of sensitive-job context, and plenty of speculation — but not enough hard proof yet to call this a coordinated mystery. 📎 Source

body.title: Seeing Anew.
body.body:
Mama Chisom had been selling akara at that junction for eleven years, She knew everyone , the danfo driver who always collected change and never returned it, the NEPA man who liked his bean cakes extra-crispy, the secondary school girls who bought two and pretended it was just one. She knew everybody, so when the fine-looking woman in the white kaftan sat down on the bench beside her frying stand that Tuesday morning, Mama Chisom noticed.
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmdNm3q4M7yvwv4YWhCGWxotYtTwMLPbEj6AMWLkwRyoZi/1001406976.jpg 


\
the woman said, arranging her wrapper carefully like she was afraid of the world touching her.\n\n\
Mama Chisom replied without looking up from her oil. \

Mama Chisom glanced sideways, The woman's eyes were doing that particular thing scanning everything but landing nowhere, Like someone who had walked out of a house and wasn't sure whether to go back in.

Chukwuemeka the mechanic apprentice from across the road, jogged over was wiping his hands on a rag, \
\n\nShe hissed and scooped them anyway. He winked at the woman in white as he collected them. \

The woman smiled,
Just a small one, like she was testing whether smiling still worked.

The morning moved the way mornings do at busy junctions  loud, then louder, then somehow louder still, buses.
Argument about a pothole, a child screaming for reasons only children understand, the woman in white sat through all of it like she was watching a film she hadn't chosen but couldn't stop watching.

\

Mama Chisom asked eventually, nodding toward the estate behind the junction, no real reason, just the way Nigerians ask questions  not fully asking, leaving room for you to answer as much or as little as you like.\n\n\
\n\nMama Chisom turned to look at her properly for the first time. \

There was something in the way she said it — not proud, not sad, just… honest. Like someone who had recently discovered that sending yourself somewhere was the only reliable option.

\
Mama Chisom asked again.\n\nThis time the woman laughed. A real one. \

Mama Chisom wrapped three in newspaper and handed them over without counting the money. The woman looked up, surprised.

\

The woman took the akara and sat back down, eating slowly, watching the junction the way strangers always do — seeing everything at once because nothing is ordinary yet. A child chasing a tyre. Two men laughing over nothing. A goat that had clearly made peace with traffic.

Mama Chisom watched her watching, and thought: That is how the place looks when you have not learned to stop seeing it. And for just a moment, through the stranger's eyes, the junction looked almost beautiful.

*Image:MetaAI.*

​K-pop လောကကြီး တိုးတက်ပြောင်းလဲနေသလိုပဲ၊ ကျွန်မရဲ့ Rising Star ဂိမ်းခရီးစဉ်ဟာလည်း အဆင့်သစ်တစ်ခုကို ရောက်ရှိနေပြီ ဖြစ်ပါတယ်။ ကျွန်မအနေနဲ့ Level 109 ကို တရားဝင် ရောက်ရှိသွားပြီဖြစ်ကြောင်း ဂုဏ်ယူစွာနဲ့ ပြောပြပါရစေရှင်။ ဒီမှတ်တိုင်ကို ရောက်ဖို့အတွက် နေ့စဉ်မပြတ် ကြိုးစားမှုတွေနဲ့ mission တွေကို ဗျူဟာကျကျ ပြီးမြောက်အောင် လုပ်ဆောင်ခဲ့ရပါတယ်။ ဒီဂိမ်းထဲမှာ virtual career တစ်ခုကို တည်ဆောက်ရတာဟာ တကယ့်ဂီတလောကမှာ လိုအပ်တဲ့ ကြိုးစားအားထုတ်မှုမျိုးကို ထင်ဟပ်စေပြီး အခုလို level တက်လာတာဟာ ကျွန်မရဲ့ ကြိုးစားမှုတွေအတွက် ရလဒ်ကောင်းတစ်ခုလို့ ခံစားရပါတယ်။

​To keep growing as a player, I have been strategically adding new cards to my collection. I recently acquired the E156 Lyre Harp and the E67 Street Organ Epic card. These cards are special to me because they represent different facets of musical culture. The Lyre Harp brings a sense of classical elegance, while the Street Organ adds a unique, lively vibe to my inventory. These additions not only boost my stats in the game but also make the overall experience more diverse and enjoyable.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmW3WT96pCZqS32XcCGAPggu5HyB4A6DWyNgNLHRs18tbH/img_0.4485858976933855.jpg)

​ဂိမ်းထဲမှာ ပိုပြီးတိုးတက်လာဖို့အတွက် ကျွန်မရဲ့ ကတ်စုဆောင်းမှုတွေကိုလည်း ဗျူဟာကျကျ တိုးချဲ့နေပါတယ်။ မကြာသေးမီကပဲ E156 Lyre Harp နဲ့ E67 Street Organ Epic card တွေကို စုဆောင်းနိုင်ခဲ့ပါတယ်။ ဒီကတ်တွေက ဂီတယဉ်ကျေးမှုရဲ့ မတူညီတဲ့ အလှတရားတွေကို ကိုယ်စားပြုနေလို့ ကျွန်မအတွက် ထူးခြားပါတယ်။ Lyre Harp က ဂန္ထဝင်ဆန်တဲ့ အလှကို ပေးစွမ်းပြီး Street Organ ကတော့ တက်ကြွဆန်းသစ်တဲ့ ခံစားမှုကို ပေးပါတယ်။ ဒီလိုဖြည့်တင်းလိုက်တာဟာ ဂိမ်းထဲက status တွေကို မြင့်တက်စေရုံသာမက ကစားရတဲ့ အတွေ့အကြုံကိုလည်း ပိုပြီးစုံလင်ပျော်ရွှင်စေပါတယ်။

​Finally, I want to share a special achievement that I managed to capture recently. As shown in the image I’ve shared, I have successfully crafted the RSTAR D1333 (Drum Kit)! Crafting your own instruments in Rising Star is one of the most rewarding aspects of the game. It takes specific parts and a lot of patience to mint a new NFT like this. Seeing the confirmation on my screen that I was able to craft this Bass Drum kit was a moment of pure joy. It’s these small wins that keep me motivated to keep leveling up and exploring the vast world of music, both in-game and out.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPnAS6DFpEdcgdPyjFRZbTaPue13aMLbbbXm6c64WjSYs/1776855978267.png)

​နောက်ဆုံးအနေနဲ့ ကျွန်မ မကြာသေးမီကမှ ရရှိခဲ့တဲ့ ထူးခြားတဲ့ အောင်မြင်မှုလေးတစ်ခုကို မျှဝေပေးချင်ပါတယ်။ အခုပေးပို့ထားတဲ့ ပုံထဲမှာ မြင်ရတဲ့အတိုင်းပဲ ကျွန်မဟာ RSTAR D1333 (Drum Kit) ကို အောင်မြင်စွာ craft လုပ်နိုင်ခဲ့ပါပြီ။ Rising Star မှာ ကိုယ်ပိုင်တူရိယာတွေကို craft လုပ်ရတာဟာ ဒီဂိမ်းရဲ့ အကျိုးအမြတ်အရှိဆုံးနဲ့ ကျေနပ်စရာအကောင်းဆုံး အပိုင်းတစ်ခုပါ။ အခုလို NFT အသစ်တစ်ခုကို mint လုပ်နိုင်ဖို့အတွက် လိုအပ်တဲ့ အစိတ်အပိုင်းတွေ စုဆောင်းရသလို တော်တော်လေးလည်း စိတ်ရှည်ရပါတယ်။ Screen ပေါ်မှာ ဒီ Bass Drum kit ကို craft လုပ်ဖို့ confirm လုပ်ရတဲ့ အချိန်ဟာ ကျွန်မအတွက် တကယ့်ကို ပျော်ရွှင်စရာ အခိုက်အတန့်ပါပဲ။ ဒီလိုအောင်မြင်မှု သေးသေးလေးတွေကပဲ ကျွန်မကို ရှေ့ဆက်ဖို့နဲ့ ဂီတလောကအကြောင်းတွေကို ဂိမ်းထဲမှာရော ပြင်ပမှာပါ ပိုပြီးလေ့လာဖို့ ခွန်အားဖြစ်စေပါတယ်ရှင်။

body.title: Back to Baja
body.body:
My kids took so many beautiful photos during their 10 day holiday in Baja California Sur, Mexico during March that I have albums full of whales, birds, plants, flowers, sunsets, waves and beaches and I want to share a few more here! 


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmayVwUoTzvnrgFko7yhwKcQAHHigpF1StPjkJLMW7nWD6/1776860086459.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUBJG9rCnEhdcmHwB64KS2dPENJoKqziuqkRbGLyQ4Yh3/1776860086781.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSbMqs4cYrGRZBcuLa24fR1UfCx92xSGg7LuEPBX6Jk2J/1776860087272.jpg)

Most of these were taken at  Villa Santa Cruz near Todos Santos.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUNrwCoExj2cpfk3UviVvzyAKVku4WiBSgFP71wcDCtkN/1776860087592.jpg)

Bougainvillea is an interesting desert flower that has thorns and are often planted as security fences. If you look closely at the center of the magenta clusters, you'll see tiny, creamy-white trumpet-shaped structures. Those are the actual flowers. The colorful parts are bracts, which are basically leaves. 
![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZseVnK7xvBnnHHXZRingUKRVBV4nZDAnz4FiFzb8yQbE/1776860087726.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZgBGQ933uFCGqi5AnBY3YM8gDjSPaFub2P7kSrgbzotx/1776860110216.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR5nM4NkK1rv78BgJPsUBrhBQLsFyQZToQ9atNtRHFNfr/1776861500286.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmb2xSN86Tq94pPTdgWqk23YupDHsp9c3pwrxicd14Zde7/1776861500465.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmZoNZMHMsC9WW49yYiyRibn9Cxz3T7HawM387RgWiBLmz/1776861500643.jpg)

There was often early morning fog along the Pacific Coast and it offered ever changing views in the morning and evening, but always beautiful photo opportunities. 
Pelicans above the Waves in this golden hour seascape. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmQcKPbtLwxj9ZUWciNC5bKnwc8MmCHcFiCyxqdjH3iF7F/1776861500732.jpg)


Humpback whales migrate thousands of miles from their feeding grounds in the north (like Alaska) to the warm lagoons of Baja California Sur to mate and give birth. It takes hours of watching and a quick shutter finger to caprure action shots like this 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNUfvj7qoBNoSZQhbZwwTdx1c1UAbyhzeKPS9L7x9yPCu/1776861500798.jpg)

Love Locks in Todos Santos. 


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmesJrswieriUsNiUyET2GsTndjDzcLZFJtEoZ6xBhdKem/1776862662143.jpg)
Hummingbird


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmb3AxpywT82oZxKNnvFabnaBdoVpWtEBto18gtqreV92E/1776866024366.jpg)


There was a lunar eclipse while they were there. It was a perfect spot for sky watching.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTa5CqBWH1nEsuocCQm9WTQePK8HvYyUxeXSdgFGKeCAP/1776862662308.jpg)


Hope you enjoyed the photos. Some were taken with a Google Pixel 10 and others using a camera and tripod. Even after tons of research the tripod caused some airport chaos. No problems on the flight going there, but a costly baggage check when returning home. But at least it arrived safely!

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbLiAShjt4HSG7qLEDb9z4LQLEfuwzgdV5czqKEEpsEXs/1775938270033.gif)

body.title: Mcgi review: Does God want evil to happen // the old path
body.body:
The Bible teaches that God is sovereign over all creation, yet it also makes a clear distinction between what God permits and what He desires. Scripture shows that God’s original creation was good, without evil or suffering. Bad things entered the world through human sin and disobedience, not because God delights in them. From the beginning, God’s will has been for righteousness, peace, and life, not pain or destruction.

At the same time, the Bible reveals that God can allow difficult and even painful situations for a greater purpose. In a fallen world, suffering can lead to growth, correction, or a deeper dependence on Him. Stories like Joseph’s hardship or Job’s trials show that what was meant for harm can be turned by God into something meaningful and good. This does not mean God causes evil, but that He is powerful enough to work through it.
https://youtu.be/qUluFZhUsL0?si=fu1UqiJ-Ax7VxTBo
The bible encourages us that God is against evil and he is making plans to end it. He calls people away from sin and offers restoration, promising a future where pain and injustice will be no more. So while bad things do happen, the biblical view is that they are not God’s perfect desire, but part of a broken world that He is redeeming.

body.title: My Fruit Bearing Plants in the Garden : Jackfruit, Guyabano, Water Apple, Dwarf Orange , Mango and, Custard Apple.
body.body:
Good day to everyone here in HiveGarden who has the passion in gardening or planting. 
Just sharing some fruit bearing plants or trees that I planted on the ground near my house here in Lapu-Lapu City .

![1000089385.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jovan1978/23wqnLEYPi8XNbxsJAewVvy94iWWqcicbKoEtbARr2m6mt9izXNeF5qdxfHNCPo1cDkRi.jpg)


 When I was a young boy, I have the passion in farming or planting crops or fruit bearing trees. When we were living in a mountainous area of Cebu City ,my parents livelihood  was farming like planting some crops like , sweet potato, corns , cassava ,taro , bananas and cultivating mango trees . I was influenced by my parents in farming  for everytime they were going to the farm , I also went with them and helping them to plant the crops. We had abundance vegetables and fruit to eat before during 80s. 
 The passion of farming is in my blood until now . But,here in the City , the farm was gone because the lot is already subdivided by new generation children and we have a very limited area now to plant fruit bearing plants . During 1986 onward , I used to plant banana trees , casava and corns here in our residence. 
 I like planting fruit bearing trees for I love eating fruits  especially some of these that I am sharing here. Fruit bearing trees can give us shelter , supply sufficient oxygen for us to absorb and it can give us unlimited fruits . Planting at first need efforts and dedications for we need to water plants and put manure on its roots. Once the plants grow and getting  mature, it can give us unlimited fruits to eat. 

My Guyabano plants now . The first one is around two years old . It has some flowers already and maybe this year it will bear fruits . 
![1000089370.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jovan1978/23vsLSq6UDKrDvdVKDSLsCyUUxFNUxJpirqE9tfe1pFYe1YksMtkc8jvyNbLfGju3C6d5.jpg)

![1000089369.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jovan1978/23uFRTwTWeoq5JMNQJ4STHbgh2zWdekSYMKSVTiEjsGTchDuVi6czXqupJzsnMoR5JeyQ.jpg)
During early 80s, my lolo's ground was surrounded by some guyabano trees . I love eating it , for it is juicy something sweet and sour. I never know its health benefits. All I know is I like eating eat . I observe that it could cleanse our intestines and we can dispose easily our internal waste without smelly odor or simply give good digestion. 
 Now I know that guyabano fruit has a natural property as a good cancer prevention , I often buy it in the market but it is very expensive with prices ranges from 60-90 pesos per kilo. It can boost our immune system and also good source of vitamin C. Its leaves are also good remedy to lower blood pressure .  
 Due to its good health benefits , I planted  more on our ground and I excited to watch their fruits on its branches . 

Another favorite is the jackfruit. 
![1000089373.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jovan1978/23wWs6k5XgX6nqw39fmuwyEFv1DdPRz8QJunM7WarddZJkKHptpmQgEYWiwgGMiLfTeMQ.jpg)

I like jackfruit for it is juicy and has  a good smell once ripe . This fruit bearing tree can live as much as 100 years accordingly . Once mature , it can bear around 150 to 250 fruits per year. 
Jackfruits good health benefits are its high contain fiber aids for digestion with less smelly waste . It can boost immune system , antioxidant and helps lower blood sugar and promotes heart health. 

My Custard Apple . 
![1000089363.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jovan1978/23ywipd98STjemng3jzPo1ShJy3U5eT3D9B2ghMzkSW5hUS7aWTCoyMAMDcJ5Xg3aeEoZ.jpg)
In Filipino term it is called \

. One thing that I like this fruit tree is, it can easily live and can give unlimited fruits and seeds . After eating it , throwing its seeds on the ground it can live and grow , that is why we have some custard trees here in our ground . It has good health benefits like antioxidant , lowers blood pressure , good for skin and hair , boost immune system and aids good digestion due to its fiber contain .

Dwarf Orange 

![1000089367.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jovan1978/23uQrSGNw7GyCHoHnNmQjevwjfKTdwqqVNkqNBNNM9pY5PefsaigCtYtgxoDr9bdY3o3z.jpg)
I bought seeds online for this dwarf orange . Fortunately,I got one survive and live until now . I put it in a large pot since it was a little one . I will transfer it to the ground so that it will grow and its roots can dominate to the ground and soon will give fruits . 

Baby Mango plant 
![1000089371.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jovan1978/23xAZgzKdwecD44YsausiQrnHNgfqPcNNGxyyRGkxbzY46UJM4Np2sFwtMauFC1HmvF46.jpg)
This mango plant grows near in my house . My wife wanted it to grow because of its delicious fruits and its leaves benefits to remedy some diseases. 

Water Apple 

![1000089364.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jovan1978/23xAVXSrcjDHQd4FnYCDr5k2HKxiVNGPPRyuMTcAmktkFJC7RFKYkvAFtyvg8rXQcFFRB.jpg)
This is called \

in Cebuano term. Water apple can easily live here in the city . Some residents  has this tree on their ground. Its fruits are very juicy and crunchy, somewhat sweet and sour. I like eating this with matching salt. 

Till next time . Thanks for giving me the opportunity to share in this community , the @hivegarden . 

Disclaimer: All photos are mine and the lead picture is edited in canva . 

God bless everyone !

body.body: 2/5 🧵 The piece zeroes in on a loophole called **Broad-Based Categorical Eligibility (BBCE)**. In plain English: states can hand someone a pamphlet or hotline tied to TANF, count that as a “benefit,” and then treat that person as automatically eligible for SNAP rules that waive normal income or asset limits. The authors say 43 states plus DC use it to bypass federal guardrails and bulk up enrollment.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/5 🧵 The most explosive claim comes from a state-level dataset reviewed by the Foundation for Government Accountability. In that one state, SNAP enrollees allegedly bought **14,000+ new luxury vehicles**, while huge numbers of applications showed glaring red flags: unverifiable Social Security numbers, addresses that didn’t match, applicants linked to other states, and even IPs and emails tied to foreign countries. The article’s point is blunt: once you strip out verification, fraud doesn’t just happen — it scales.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 The authors also argue the problem isn’t only “rich people cheating.” Some of those luxury-car cases could be identity theft victims, which makes the system look even dumber. If a library card can satisfy identity proof and states stop cross-checking assets, income, residency, and SSNs, then stolen or synthetic identities can cruise through intake. The article pegs improper SNAP payments at **$10.4 billion a year**, while arguing the true cost is higher once trafficking and other schemes are counted.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body:
5/5 🧵 The policy takeaway is clear: the article backs tougher verification and says Trump’s 2025 **One Big Beautiful Bill Act** finally forces states with high SNAP error rates to feel financial pain. It also claims ending BBCE could remove millions of ineligible enrollees and save **$100B+ over a decade**. Fair warning: this is an **opinion piece**, so it’s making a case, not pretending to be neutral. But the core argument lands hard — a safety net stops being a safety net when it’s designed so badly that scammers treat it like a buffet. 📎 Source

body.title: Exploitation or Experience? The Truth About Internships in Nigeria
body.body:
Starting as an internship is a great approach to a career path, because it brings a new graduate or a high school student to experience the real world. Still, there is a problem with this in Nigeria or perhaps Lagos state, most of the interns I have experienced or witnessed people interning often complain of extortions from companies and how they treat them, I would n believe it if I had not experienced this before, I will also share my story below. 


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mikechrist/242DQpreoov2i879oDPbQS2mu2oBHe2MgiqMLTK8PUyJgw6Y8GBcaLp6EVxv2DvCxhgmb.png)

I understand Nigeria is a developing country, and there are so many companies that struggle to survive, but this doesn't mean they should be taking advantage of interns. Interns are paid less, but they're still exploited in a harsh way, given jobs twice their size, and quarreled with if they don't do it. I have once been an intern and I work more than any other staff member in the company, so they all know me so well. I remember I interned at a company as a graphic designer, and these people made me their comms person across all platforms, they also made me manage their emails and creatings news letter not only that they gave me their website to manage for them, and also managed two company social media accounts, struggling to meetup with target, so far it has been really crazy on top how much. i couldn't even have tike for myself managing two comapnies social media account and doing all that all at once the funny part is that this is not a small company a very huge company that there are a lot of engagement going on so there is a lot to post about, not just that again i will still be the grapjhcis designe r and lot of review will be there, threr most ananoying part is that they now even gave me an operatiosn job to manage call and reach out to people. It got to a stage where I had to leave even though I hadn't received any better offer, I just had to go because these people were really taking advantage of me in so many ways. The design jobs I do take time, and another annoying thing again is that there is always pressure in the company because there are only a few workers. 

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mikechrist/AKYNydEBnoVcFYHRBjNQJStF7XAhkkNG488TCBXJNbckLmuVQfPnQyxUwWfkZ8N.png)

Most organizations take advantage of interns because they feel they are fresh and inexperienced. My friend was paid 20,000 at one organization like that back then and they wanted him to come every day which is really crazy. Monday to Friday, he helps them manage their website which seems like a job that can be fully done remotely. Not just this experience again if friends come together to discuss their experiences back then it was really extreme and trust me, it 's really crazy. 

I feel there should be a reporting body based on this not just interns also staff extortion, most organizations take advantage of workers and workers cannot really complain because there is not work outside there. 

This is my entry to Hive Learners weekly prompt, week 214 Episode 2. 

Thank You for Reading my post,
-

body.body: 2/4 🧵 The strategic logic is obvious. Cursor’s value isn’t “AI writes code” — everyone has that. Its edge is **codebase context, workflow integration, and developer adoption**. SpaceX is one of the few companies where shaving engineering cycle time by even 5-10% could be worth absurd money across launch systems, avionics, manufacturing software, satellite ops, Starlink infrastructure, simulation, and internal tooling. If SpaceX can wire Cursor into a giant internal coding stack and maybe into systems around [xAI’s Colossus infrastructure, as described by InfoWorld](https://www.infoworld.com/article/4161997/spacex-secures-option-to-acquire-ai-coding-startup-cursor-for-60b.html), then this is less “buying an app” and more “buying a software acceleration layer.”

body.author: mobi72

body.body: 3/4 🧵 The catch: **$60B is eye-watering**. Cursor/Anysphere was already a monster private AI company, but this number implies SpaceX thinks one of two things is true: either 1) Cursor becomes mission-critical internal infrastructure worth controlling outright, or 2) the real asset isn’t today’s product, it’s future strategic dominance in AI-native software development. My take: if the option gets exercised, it won’t be because Cursor is a nice coding assistant. It’ll be because SpaceX believes control over AI coding systems becomes as strategic as control over launch cadence or compute. If they don’t exercise it, the option itself still blocks rivals and gives SpaceX privileged access.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/4 🧵 What the market should watch next is simple: **terms, exclusivity, and customer impact**. If enterprise customers start worrying Cursor is becoming a Musk/SpaceX-adjacent captive tool, neutrality concerns get real fast. If SpaceX keeps it semi-independent, this could look more like AWS+Anthropic-style strategic alignment than a straight absorption. On InLeo, there isn’t much substantive discussion yet beyond passing mentions like [@dashnode talking about building outside Cursor’s ecosystem](https://inleo.io/threads/view/dashnode/re-leothreads-25nmrkgw8). My read: smart move for SpaceX if the goal is engineering leverage; risky move for Cursor if its broader market wants vendor neutrality.\n\n#threadstorm

body.title: (ESP-ENG) The Pitt | Mental health matters - Series Review Season 2!
body.body:
**<center>Hola amigos, buenas vibras para todos.</center>** 


> Hello friends, good vibes to all.



![1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/javyeslava.photo/Eou7GCBAwvcewKDurpExHpuXCxcf9T2w7rhRRQ6cR9tt8XvY5mCJTyR7YV4bAg73uRa.jpg)


[Source!](https://www.primevideo.com/-/es/detail/The-Pitt/0P3OZNNH7QME4JFR3FU6EQFEAE)

<div class=\

>Si hay algo que las nuevas generaciones están haciendo hoy en día con referencia a la televisión es que todo lo que ven lo quieren convertir en una novela en donde exista puro romance y relaciones entre sus protagonistas, lo llaman \

y eso amigos es terrible. Esto lo digo porque a mucha de esta gente, no toda, que también hacen mucho ruido en redes no les ha gustado esta temporada precisamente por la carencia de lo que les comenté. Afortunadamente de ellos no dependen las valoraciones reales ni el valor real de la serie el cual es gigantesco. Esta segunda entrega creo que es mejor que la primera porque si de por sí la serie ya es realista con el tema de la salud mental y el colapso de los médicos debido a esto la trama da un salto sustancial.

> If there's one thing the younger generation is doing these days with television, it's turning everything they watch into a soap opera filled with romance and relationships between the main characters. They call it \

and that, my friends, is terrible. I say this because many of these people—not all, but those who make a lot of noise on social media—didn't like this season precisely because of the lack of what I mentioned. Fortunately, the true value and appreciation of the series, which is enormous, doesn't depend on them. I think this second season is better than the first because, while the series is already realistic about mental health and the strain on the medical system as a result, the plot takes a substantial leap forward.

>Esta nueva temporada se desarrolla un 4 de julio, un día festivo en Estados Unidos en donde las personas al parecer se vuelven locas por los fuegos artificiales y aprovechan para hacer parrilladas y beber bastante alcohol. Todo esto genera que obviamente ocurran accidentes de todo tipo y esto es lo que al final veremos en los 15 capítulos. El formato es el mismo, cada episodio es una hora del turno diurno de estos médicos en la sala de emergencia por lo que absolutamente todo se desarrolla en ese espacio; toda la tensión, el drama y el estrés queda encapsulado en esas \

y es con todo eso con lo que tendremos que lidiar como espectadores.

> This new season takes place on July 4th, a holiday in the United States where people apparently go wild for fireworks and take advantage of the occasion to have barbecues and drink a lot of alcohol. All of this obviously leads to accidents of all kinds, and that's what we'll ultimately see in the 15 episodes. The format is the same: each episode is an hour of these doctors' day shift in the emergency room, so absolutely everything unfolds within that space. All the tension, drama, and stress is encapsulated within those \

and that's what we, as viewers, will have to deal with.


![2.webp](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/javyeslava.photo/23xAZezNLELERpPoANsCEL4D1erGaaRwUDsaoxT3N9MusYVNghYZmpw3enqbyMxcusvJs.webp)


[Source!](https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/the-pitt-season-two-trailer-dana-langdon-1236350030/)

---


![3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/javyeslava.photo/23zkiCWQXtDZs4pNYkjzDJpSxcMLsntjU5iiHzjyqK5eE7UrgEJBNewe7WyKkSnyhFgrr.jpg)


[Source!](https://people.com/the-pitt-season-2-finale-ending-explained-11949623)

<div class=\

>Qué es lo que destaca en relación a la primera temporada? - pues que acá veremos un poco más el reflejo del deterioro mental tanto de médicos como de enfermeras producido por las circunstancias propias de una sala de emergencias. Un pequeño dato que se me olvidaba, TODO el sistema online/virtual se cae producto de un hackeo por lo que tendrán que trabajar manualmente, es decir, historias, pedidos de exámenes y pruebas, todo será a mano. El chiste de la temporada es que trabajarán como lo hacen día a día los médicos latinoamericanos porque si, esa es la triste realidad de este lado del mundo. La mente se puede abrumar por muchas cosas pero si a eso se le suma el caos de no saber trabajar de esta forma pues el colapso será inminente.

> What stands out compared to the first season? Well, here we'll see a bit more of the mental deterioration of both doctors and nurses caused by the circumstances of an emergency room. One small detail I almost forgot: the ENTIRE online/virtual system crashes due to a hack, so they'll have to work manually. That means patient histories, test orders, and everything will be done by hand. The joke of the season is that they'll be working the way Latin American doctors do every day, because yes, that's the sad reality on this side of the world. The mind can be overwhelmed by many things, but if you add to that the chaos of not knowing how to work this way, then a breakdown is imminent.

>Tenemos a un nuevo personaje, la médico adjunto que en teoría cubrirá a Robby en sus vacaciones, Sepideh Moafi (Baran Al-Hashimi), una figura de poder que llega para poner a prueba el temperamento y el control de Robby en un ambiente el cual tiende a estar bajo la mirada y las decisiones de él. Este choque de personalidades y egos hará que la estancia de ambos y la de los médicos que los rodean se llenen de tensiones. Sumar también que cada uno de estos personajes tienen sus \

internos los cuales en más de una oportunidad saldrán a la luz para agregar más drama a una trama que de por si está cargada con todos los casos médicos que constantemente están llegando. Y es que claro, en ese aspecto la serie sigue siendo espectacular, al estar un 4 de julio los casos son diferentes y las lesiones son distintas. El realismo de los diagnósticos y tratamientos sigue siendo bastante elevado y acertados, no al 100% pero si en un porcentaje bien alto.

> We have a new character, the attending physician who is supposed to cover for Robby during his vacation, Sepideh Moafi (Baran Al-Hashimi), a powerful figure who arrives to test Robby's temperament and self-control in an environment that tends to be under his watchful eye and decisions. This clash of personalities and egos will fill their stay, and that of the doctors around them, with tension. Adding to this, each of these characters has their own inner demons, which will surface on more than one occasion, adding even more drama to a plot already packed with the constant stream of medical cases. And indeed, in that aspect, the series remains spectacular. Since it's the Fourth of July, the cases are different, and the injuries are varied. The realism of the diagnoses and treatments remains quite high and accurate, not 100%, but certainly a very high percentage. ![4.webp](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/javyeslava.photo/23yJCYdu8TqG3dz9PGcwoSdiXTcfG3QPk1LcE9DutSsWCVYZQfBPe2naQxmW6GPGJHN7d.webp) [Source!](https://consequence.net/2026/01/the-pitt-season-2-review-hbo-max/) --- ![5.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/javyeslava.photo/EoyPXTKCoFyQT5GgfM8MPQNvjqm7UQHUqrLrbjkNPpHzXnBNeqiJwiWhKCeuoBN4FuS.jpg) [Source!](https://tucson.com/life-entertainment/nation-world/movies-tv/article_5f49dcf9-dc6a-551d-8d8b-39fc458aa629.html)

>Pero como dije antes el eje principal es la salud mental y su cuidado. Robby y varios están a punto de un quiebre, como lo gestionan es la clave de todo. La serie vuelve a mostrar las vulnerabilidades, esta vez de los médicos, ante un sistema de salud que tiene sus pro pero que también tiene muchos contras. El manejo de la carga y de la responsabilidad, el sentirse importante trabajando y no querer estar afuera porque la vida no tiene sentido o hay muchos problemas; usar el trabajo como un aislante es el error que muchos cometen y que acá lo representan muy bien. La serie es espectacular, la temporada 2 es mucho más humana y cercana porque abre un poco más a los personajes y permite a las personas que no estamos familiarizados con la profesión a conocer el lado bueno pero también su lado oscuro y negro. Muy recomendada a todos. Ya está confirmada la tercera temporada cosa que es una gran noticia. Un 9/10 esta entrega. Les dejo el trailer.

> But as I said before, the main focus is mental health and its care. Robby and several others are on the verge of a breakdown, and how they manage it is key. The series once again highlights vulnerabilities, this time those of doctors, within a healthcare system that has its pros but also many cons. Managing the workload and responsibility, feeling important at work and not wanting to be away because life is meaningless or there are too many problems; using work as an escape is a mistake many make, and this series portrays it very well. The show is spectacular; season 2 is much more human and relatable because it delves deeper into the characters and allows those of us unfamiliar with the profession to see both its positive and dark sides. Highly recommended to everyone. The third season has already been confirmed, which is great news. This season gets a 9/10. Here's the trailer. ![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/javyeslava.photo/23z7FdTcCm7Je1XAYAEfQ7HzM6QomKDL6MTYXVcEzEH3prHK1NPRKjEtv9HYVmZjQNegu) [Source!](https://www.cbr.com/how-long-between-the-pitt-season-1-and-2/) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xq8x47ky2Tw ***

Bueno mi gente por hoy es todo, espero que les haya gustado. ¡Un abrazo a todos, nos vemos en la próxima!
***

> Well folks, that's all for today. I hope you enjoyed it. ¡Hugs to everyone, see you next time!

body.body: ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYnfYkz4yfEPrr9kJvHBth3KoeUAkfXzrAoS9mcZGp7P7/img_20260419_183438_302.jpg)\nAtanasio Pérez Rigal, nacido en Ciego de Ávila en 1942, es mucho más que un nombre en el Salón de la Fama; es el corazón de la legendaria \

de Cincinnati. 

Durante su extensa carrera en las Mayores (1964-1986), Pérez no solo fue un baluarte en la primera y tercera base, sino que se consagró como uno de los bateadores más temidos en situaciones de máxima presión. 

Sus números finales son un testamento de constancia: 379 jonrones, 2,732 hits y 1,652 carreras impulsadas, cifra que lo sitúa entre los mejores remolcadores de todos los tiempos.

Su momento más icónico ocurrió en el Juego de Estrellas de 1967. El partido estaba estancado en un duelo de pitcheo épico que se extendió hasta la entrada 15. Fue entonces cuando Pérez castigó una recta del futuro inmortal Catfish Hunter con un cuadrangular solitario que le dio la victoria 2-1 a la Liga Nacional. Este batazo no solo le valió el MVP del juego, sino que selló su reputación como el hombre de los \

. Además, ostenta el récord (compartido con Miñoso, Palmeiro y Luque) de haber jugado 23 temporadas en el máximo nivel, demostrando una longevidad atlética casi inalcanzable.\n\nTony Pérez es recordado por ser el \

emocional de uno de los equipos más dominantes de la historia. Mientras Johnny Bench y Pete Rose acaparaban los titulares, sus compañeros sabían que, con hombres en base y el juego en la línea, no había nadie mejor que el cubano.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYvvDz7GHSpRUuQEHqWuqbcV2QYvv1x3xLZvKWxRzVHgJ/img_20260419_183433_180.jpg)
Hoy, es un símbolo de la nobleza y la eficiencia del pelotero latino, siendo el segundo cubano (después de Martín Dihigo) en entrar al Salón de la Fama de Cooperstown, abriendo las puertas para las generaciones actuales de la isla.

Tras colgar los spikes como jugador, Tony Pérez no pudo alejarse del diamante, trasladando su liderazgo silencioso al banquillo. En 1993, hizo historia al ser nombrado mánager de los Cincinnati Reds, convirtiéndose en uno de los primeros cubanos en dirigir una franquicia de Grandes Ligas. Aunque su paso por los Reds fue breve (apenas 44 juegos debido a una decisión gerencial muy cuestionada por la afición), su huella más profunda en esta faceta llegaría con los Florida Marlins.

En la temporada 2001, Pérez asumió el mando de los peces tras la salida de John Boles. Bajo su tutela, un joven equipo de Florida encontró estabilidad y respeto, logrando un balance de 54 victorias y 49 derrotas bajo su mando. Tony fue clave en la maduración de figuras que luego serían campeones en 2003, demostrando que su ojo clínico para el béisbol y su capacidad para gestionar egos eran tan afilados como su bate. Hoy, su legado como mánager es recordado no solo por las estadísticas, sino por la elegancia y la sabiduría con la que guió a las nuevas generaciones latinas en el dugout.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmY7suQd9PHbi76WY5LHhDn7qNBczkncJ4TtX5P5aJAXSf/img_20260419_183416_787.jpg)
En conclusión, Tony Pérez representa la excelencia del pelotero cubano: esa mezcla de humildad fuera del terreno y una frialdad absoluta ante la presión dentro de él. Para los cubanos, \

es un símbolo de orgullo nacional que demostró que se puede llegar a la cima del béisbol mundial manteniendo la elegancia y la sencillez.

Su legado no se mide solo por su placa en Cooperstown o sus anillos de Serie Mundial, sino por haber sido el pilar de la Gran Maquinaria Roja, el equipo más dominante de su era. Para el fanático del béisbol en cualquier rincón del planeta, el nombre de Tony Pérez es sinónimo de respeto y oportunidad; es el recordatorio de que, cuando el juego se decide en el último suspiro, no hay mejor garantía que un cubano con el bate en las manos. Su historia es el puente que une la época dorada de nuestra pelota con el brillo de las estrellas actuales.

His legacy is measured not only by his plaque in Cooperstown or his World Series rings, but by having been the pillar of the Big Red Machine, the most dominant team of its era. For baseball fans anywhere in the world, the name Tony Pérez is synonymous with respect and reliability; he is a reminder that when the game is decided in the final breath, there is no better guarantee than a Cuban with a bat in his hands. body.title: I’m Just Drifting Between Dreams and Reality
body.body: I'm a third year student and once my biggest dream in life was to become a doctor. Since childhood, I had seen my mother and grandmother battling illnesses and their suffering created a strange restlessness and passion in my heart. I wanted to become a doctor and treat not only them but also countless other people who are in pain. That very dream became the reason for my hard work. I scored good marks in matric and I also gave my all in FSc because for me this wasn't just studying but a purpose a dream that I wanted to fulfill at any cost.\n\n

>

But life doesn’t always go according to a person’s plans. After FSc, when the time came for admission to medical college my marks weren’t high enough to secure a spot in a government college and the fees of private colleges were beyond what my family could afford. That moment was extremely difficult for me. It felt as if all my hard work all my hopes had shattered in an instant. I broke down inside worry and disappointment surrounded me and I began to feel lost in a kind of darkness.

My parents became my support during that time and held me together. They encouraged me explaining that life isn’t just about one path many paths remain open for a person. Their words gave me some courage and I convinced myself that even if I couldn’t become a doctor, I could still work hard and become something in another field. With that thought I chose Computer Sciences but in some corner of my heart that same unfinished dream is still alive today.

Today, when I look at my life often only one feeling rises from my heart.I’m just drifting, I’m just flowing along. I am studying I am moving forward too but that inner purpose I had that passion I had has been left somewhere behind. Sometimes it feels like I am going along with time but I have lost my true direction. Maybe this is just a phase maybe this too shall pass but for now it just feels like I’m quietly drifting through my own life.
body.author: alijawad

That wasn’t just money; it was a credibility stamp saying, “these guys might actually be building the future interface for programming.” For a young startup, that kind of backing changes hiring, press, user growth, and investor appetite overnight. [Anysphere on the OpenAI fund](https://anysphere.inc/blog/openai-fund?_bhlid=d5a8dda8cc1455acecf609b4f8ff8c5e97f4d594)

That’s an insane climb for a company founded just a few years earlier, but it also tracks with what the market rewarded: tools that turn AI into measurable developer productivity, not demo theater. Hay días de esos, en los que levantarse de la cama es una gran proeza, donde lo que más resalta en las emociones es la pereza, días en los que tan solo la idea de correr hace que la flojera se haga más presente todavía. Pues bien, para mí, hoy es uno de esos días.


No quería levantarme de la cama, no quería calentar y mucho menos salir a entrenar. Pero lo hice, me obligué. Y no fue fácil porque a cada paso que daba, la mente solo me decía que me detuviera y me devolviera. No le hice caso y seguí adelante porque mi meta eran los 5 km.


Intenté callar la mente yendo a un ritmo muy alto pero no funcionaba, luego iba lento y seguía insistiendo en que parara. Y aún así conseguí correr los 5 kilómetros a un ritmo promedio de 6:32. Nada mal para alguien que en otro momento se habría quedado acostado sin más ni más.


Para evitar que fuera una carrera rutinaria, decidí correr en una ruta que hace tiempo no uso: la avenida Orinoco. Allí tomé algunas fotos y luego empecé a trotar. Fue muy agradable porque tiene mucha vegetación. La desventaja de este trayecto es la gran cantidad de carros y personas que lo transitan, pero me sirvió para correr hoy y no perder mi entrenamiento.

Les comparto algunas de las fotografías que tomé. Y aprovecho la oportunidad para decirles que aún sin querer, aún sin tener ganas de puede correr, y la satisfacción que se siente al terminar bien vale la pena. Feliz día para todos. Hasta mañana.
