body.title: Learning Shouldn’t Mean Struggling
body.body:
>


I have always found this conversation about internships a bit funny… because the people who argue that interns should not be paid are usually not the ones waking up early, rushing to catch buses, and trying to survive on almost nothing just to gain experience.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYv8sDz39k4C713149bQRY8AhBpXZXRMNvE4jjBQYwjSX/1776864397673.png)

For me I believe that interns should be paid, maybe not a full salary like permanent staff, but at least something reasonable, call it allowance, stipend, whatever name makes it sound softer, but it should exist, I say this not just from theory, but from what I have seen up close.

I remember my sister’s internship period like it was yesterday, she was working at the airport, going about four days a week, sounds normal, right? but the real story was in the background, “Ah ah, transport again?” she would say one morning, standing there calculating her last cash.

And I would just be looking at her like, “You are going again today?”

She would sigh, “What choice do I have? If I miss today, they will mark me absent.”

See ehn that thing used to pain me. Because this was not someone being lazy or unserious, she was committed, showing up, learning, doing actual work, but at the end of the week?Nothing.

There was no allowance, no support. Just  _ Thank you for your service.


And that is  where I have a problem, Yes, internships are about learning, nobody is arguing that, you go there to gain experience, understand how things work, build yourself, but lets not pretend like interns are just sitting in one corner watching life happen.

They work, they contribute, Sometimes, they even do the kind of tasks full staff try to avoid.

So how does it make sense that someone is giving their time, energy, and even money, because transport in this country is not beans and gets absolutely nothing in return? That’s where it starts to feel less like “learning opportunity” and more like quiet exploitation.

Because imagine this… An intern resumes by 8am, they leave their house by maybe 6:30am, They spend money on transport, they work till 4 or 5pm, Sometimes they are tired, stressed, even hungry.

And then they go home with… experience, experience is good, no doubt, but experience doesn’t pay transport fare, It doesn’t solve basic needs.

At least give them something to ease the burden, even if it is small, even if it’s just enough for transportation, that alone can make a huge difference.

I havee seen people quit internships halfway, not because they did not want to learn, but because they simply could not afford to continue, and that is sad, because it means opportunities are now only accessible to people who can financially sustain “free work\

body.title: Interns are not people [EN/PT]
body.body:
This was a phrase I once heard at a company where I worked. At the time, it was said in a joking tone, when the topic was the division of a bonus among employees. This tone, as relaxed as it may sound, carries a message that has ended up becoming cultural nowadays, the idea that interns do not have rights, only duties. Within this culture, even the question of whether they should be paid or not comes up. Shouldn’t they be financially compensated?

We can think that yes, the intern is just going through a phase to acquire knowledge and, in the future, apply it. We can see it as a moment of learning, and in fact it should be that way. However, many companies use this to obtain cheap labor or, many times, free labor, and the knowledge that should be passed on simply is not. Interns are often exploited with nothing in return, no salary, no teaching. They are seen only as someone who should be exploited or made the target of jokes.

I understand that, by gaining knowledge as an intern, a right is being exercised. After all, interning is about absorbing experience to apply in a future profession, and this is a requirement of many colleges and technical schools. There is no problem in exchanging time for knowledge, and sometimes this can be worth more than monetary compensation. I myself have exchanged days of work for learning, with no money involved, and I felt I came out ahead. But the reality of day-to-day life is different. Many companies open positions for interns thinking only about the benefit of cheap labor, without structuring a process that makes this exchange fair. That is why, in my opinion, to avoid mistakes and injustice, interns should be paid, regardless of the situation.

By doing this, we ensure that injustice does not prevail. Interns are people who are making an effort and, many times, depend on this compensation to ensure their livelihood. In some cases, they are fathers or mothers seeking qualification to provide a better life. In others, they are children helping with household expenses. There are also those who have no support at all and depend entirely on themselves to survive. In all cases, they are people dedicating their time to becoming professionals and seeking a better life in an honest way.

So, even if they are not yet fully qualified, in my way of thinking, it should be mandatory to pay interns. Because, regardless of the knowledge gained, payment is a matter of justice. We never know each person’s real needs, but we do know that, while interning, many are in a moment of financial vulnerability. And, many times, compensation is not just fair, it is what determines whether someone can continue on this path or not.

Those who are learning also need to live and have bills to pay. It is not just an act of justice, it is an act of empathy, and it conveys a different message from the one many are used to hearing, that “interns are not people.” It sends the idea that \

. A company that acts this way may, in the future, have that same intern back after they graduate. And what company does not need qualified people, and even better, grateful ones? Having someone who was well received, who feels valued, and who carries gratitude tends to generate a much more positive return. Everyone benefits.

Em meio a essa cultura, até mesmo o questionamento sobre se devem ser remunerados ou não entra em pauta. Não deveriam ser remunerados financeiramente?

Podemos pensar que sim, o estagiário está apenas passando por uma fase para adquirir conhecimento e, no futuro, aplicá-lo. Podemos encarar como um momento de aprendizado, e de fato deveria ser assim. No entanto, muitas empresas utilizam isso para obter mão de obra barata ou, muitas vezes, gratuita, e o conhecimento que deveria ser transmitido simplesmente não é. Estagiários são, com frequência, explorados sem nada em troca, sem salário, sem ensinamentos. São vistos apenas como alguém que deve ser explorado ou alvo de chacota. 

Eu entendo que, ao obter conhecimento como estagiário, um direito está sendo exercido. Afinal, estagiar é absorver experiência para aplicar na futura profissão, e isso é uma exigência de muitas faculdades e escolas técnicas. Não há problema em trocar tempo por conhecimento, e às vezes isso pode valer mais do que uma remuneração monetária. Eu mesmo já troquei dias de trabalho por aprendizado, sem dinheiro envolvido, e senti que saí em vantagem. Mas a realidade do dia a dia é diferente. Muitas empresas abrem espaço para estagiários pensando apenas no benefício da mão de obra barata, sem estruturar um processo que torne essa troca justa. Por isso, na minha opinião, para evitar erros e injustiças, o estagiário deveria ser remunerado, independentemente de qualquer situação.

Fazendo isso, garantimos que a injustiça não prevaleça. Estagiários são pessoas que estão se esforçando e, muitas vezes, dependem dessa remuneração para garantir o sustento. Há também aqueles que não têm suporte algum e dependem exclusivamente de si para sobreviver. Em todos os casos, são pessoas dedicando seu tempo para se profissionalizar e buscar uma vida melhor de forma honesta.

Então, mesmo que ainda não estejam totalmente qualificados, dentro da minha forma de pensar, deveria ser obrigatório remunerar estagiários. Pois, independentemente do conhecimento adquirido, o pagamento é uma questão de justiça. Nunca sabemos a real necessidade de cada pessoa, mas sabemos que, ao estagiar, muitos estão em um momento de vulnerabilidade financeira. E, muitas vezes, a remuneração não é apenas justa, é o que define se alguém pode continuar ou não nessa jornada.

body.body: 1/5 🧵 Dave Mason helped write the soundtrack of a generation, then spent much of his life trying to avoid the whole “rock star” circus. Now the Traffic co-founder is dead at 79, passing peacefully at home in Nevada. The sharp part of this story isn’t just the loss — it’s how much of classic rock he shaped while never really wanting the spotlight.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 2/5 🧵 Mason’s family confirmed his death and described a life centered on music and the people he loved. He’s survived by his wife, Winifred Wilson, daughter Danielle, plus nieces and nephews. His cause of death hasn’t been announced. The article also notes he had been dealing with serious health issues in recent years, including a severe infection in 2024 that forced tour postponements into 2025.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 3/5 🧵 His legacy is bigger than casual fans probably realize. Mason co-founded **Traffic** in 1967 with Steve Winwood, Jim Capaldi and Chris Wood, and wrote two of the band’s best-known songs: **“Feelin’ Alright?”** and **“Hole in My Shoe.”** That alone would be enough for a career. Instead, he kept stacking credits like a man allergic to staying in one lane.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body: 4/5 🧵 After leaving Traffic following their first album, he came back more than once — in 1971 and again in 2004. In between, he built a solo career, landed a hit with **“We Just Disagree”** in 1977, worked with the **Rolling Stones** and **Jimi Hendrix**, and even joined **Fleetwood Mac** for their 1995 album *Time*. Quiet résumé. Absolutely absurd range.
body.author: askrafiki

body.body:
5/5 🧵 The most human detail in the piece is Mason’s own view of fame. In a 2020 interview, he basically said: I’m not a rock star, I just wanted to write great music, make some money, have fun, and — very honestly — meet girls. That self-awareness fits the whole arc here: huge influence, low ego, lasting catalog. 📎 Source

📎 [Source](https://pagesix.com/2026/04/22/entertainment/dave-mason-legendary-traffic-co-founder-dead-at-79/)

近年感觉公司的人事部负责安排学习讲座的同事很给力，常常都安排到商家到门提供健康讲座之余，还让商家们提供午餐给出席者。

昨天就安排了主题为三高的健康讲座，听就听很多次了，每次都可以温故知新之余，还可以领免费午餐，何乐不为？

不过这一次还蛮多知识的，不止不好高糖分，高盐也是不健康的行为。

算来算去真的如果要吃得健康，只能吃鱼片汤了。很多那些有汤、芡汁类的都高盐分。

这一次讲座也学到新词 Body Roundness Index (BRI)， 算是额外收获。

主办方还挺大方的，还赠送治膝盖的粉包，诚意满满。

1小时讲座准时结束就领饭盒去食堂用餐了，也没硬销。

body.title: Tulsa King - Let's Hit the Road
body.body: Watching Tulsa King is really like hitting the road and experiencing, facing the expected and unexpected. Though, it is inclined towards expected more than unexpected, not too much to anticipate, but what they say, \

.

<center>![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mobi72/23z7SWMCpDrdCgDPgPBtg7B61L5sj5bHE47v1oa4vyWjVs1AneZV41GbmSutdSsQ2LSKq.png)</center>
<sup>[Source: Tulsa King wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tulsa_King_title_card.jpg)</sup>

I like Sylvester Stallone's Tulsa King more than Arnold Schwarznegger's Fubar in terms of story, narrative, plot and/or performances.

It could be said that Tulsa King is a one man show, Stallone's perfromance and presence in the show is that strong. Even though Stallone's performance remained at its best, somewhere at the top, other actors performances not only support Stallone but also they are not very far below his.

The story of this series is gang related, I know, not a new genre, may be not that exciting, as well, as it used to be. Writers/Creators made some changes in the story and plot. I liked these changes, they keep the show interesting. You'll notice them while watching the show. 

Main character, played by Sylvester Stallone, is Dwight Manfredi. He was prisoned for 25 years. After getting released, instead of rewarding him for his silence and services for the gang, the boss, under the influence of his son, sends him to a city, Tulsa. Tulsa is completely free of any of the gang related activities. Despite of this, Dwight turned the city into a profit making venue. It is interesting to watch how Dwight made this happen, no doubt, a fun to watch journey. 

Dwight's character is so strong that I got emotionally invested in this character. I am sure, others viewers would have the same reaction. One of the strongest attribute of Dwight's character is being loyal, whether this loyalty is for his boss or gang or for his friends and members of his newly formed gang. He also rewards them generously and back their actions when they are right *(or not 🙂)*. He believes in fulfiling his liabilities and responsibilities, even the forced ones. 

The reason to love this show is Dwight. He is more a businessman than a gangster who has ideas and know exactly how to implement them. He knows how to turn the tide in his favor. He has a keen eye for the details. At the begining of the show after reaching to Tulsa, he came to know that selling \

is legal in the state. Even after getting this information, he went to a local store that sell it and offered the owner (Bodhi, played by Martin Starr) protection. You must be laughing or smiling just like I did *(Selling is legal, man, why does he need protection?)*. Dwight was serious, though, and had a logical reason for this offer. No doubt, the business was legal but it was made very difficult by the law to dispose of the money earned. This was the very issue the owner, Bodhi, was facing. He had millions of dollars in his office safe and was unable to spend them. Bodhi understood the offer and accepted it. Dwight didn't take the money, instead he became his partner for laundering the money, a win-win situation for both, mostly for Dwight.

<center>![MV5BMzM2NmEzNmYtM2E4NS00YjVjLTljYjctYTM0ZDdhMDllMTFiXkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mobi72/23yJ3idEk7g6uek4dHu8NvhDzm8gZTJTwdDd2yvXfiEtgKBVYJ9hEzE6icRHdPoKPrtB1.jpg)</center>

Interactions and conversations between Dwight and villians are some strong scenes of the show. They kept me fully occupied in the show and didn't let my attention to divert somewhere else without even for a second. Dialogues from both, dwight and villian/s, had the same impact *(Watch the last scene from the second episode of the third season as an example)*. Interactions and conversations among other characters are also enjoyable. No preference there. Though, Bodhi and Goodie are remarkable. Despite its genre, mafia, this series has a flavor of light comedy and humor, and is used quite intelligentally throuhout all of 3 seasons.

All of the characters are interesting and fun. One of the characters is Dennis Goodie Carangi, played by Christopher Caldovino, a recurring character. Goodie was high ranking old-school mafia member of New York Invernizzi Crime family and sent to Tulsa to keep an eye on Dwight. Dwight turned him to his site and made him second-in command. Though, where his actual loyalty lies is still questionable. Even though he is an old-school mobster, after joining Dwight he solves their problems sensibly, calmly, and in the most practical way possible. It is also fun to watch him dealing with the issues in his own way. Writers have written the dialogues, situations in all of his scenes very smartly and Christopher Caldovino's style of delivering them and performing the scenes makes them even more iinteresting to watch. Despite being serious, his scenes are among the best comic scenes of the series.

Dwight took some misfits of the society under his wings and turned them into gangsters. Very villionous of him. But, this is what made it interesting. The behaviours of these misfits after turning into the gangsters is what fun to watch. A salute to the creators/writers for making this smart depiction part of the story.

The story which was started with gang, mafia, crime, has reached to political influences and political powers in the third season. Tulsa King is one of the series' which get better with every episode and season and finally becomes one of most wanted show to watch. 

Third season is better than previous two, and the most exciting one, as well, up until the second last episode of the season. I didn't get satisfied with the way they have wrapped up the season in the finale. How they developed the character of Dunmire, it needs a little more efforts to end.

body.body:
En el món de les criptomonedes, la fragmentació entre diferents blockchains continua sent un dels grans obstacles per a una adopció massiva. Canviar actius entre cadenes sovint implica ponts complexos, comissions elevades, tokens embolicats i riscos de custòdia. **Altera** (accessible a través de https://altera.magi.eco/), desenvolupat per la **Magi Network**, arriba per canviar aquesta realitat. Es presenta com “One Wallet. Every Chain” (Una cartera. Totes les cadenes), oferint una solució no custodial, sense comissions i amb intercanvis natius entre múltiples xarxes.

### Què és exactament Altera?

Altera és una aplicació de cartera (wallet) no custodial que permet gestionar i intercanviar actius de diverses blockchains des d’una única interfície. Està impulsada per la **Magi Network**, un protocol de nova generació enfocat en la interoperabilitat cross-chain, contractes intel·ligents natius i liquiditat unificada.

A diferència de moltes solucions actuals, Altera no requereix que els usuaris creïn una nova cartera ni memoritzin una seed phrase addicional. Pots connectar les teves carteres existents, com MetaMask (per a cadenes EVM), Keychain (per a Hive) o qualsevol altra compatible, i començar a operar immediatament mantenint el control total de les teves claus privades.

### Les característiques principals que el fan únic

- **Intercanvis cross-chain natius**: Pots intercanviar actius reals com BTC (Bitcoin), DASH, HIVE o HBD sense necessitat de ponts, wrappers ni exchanges centralitzats. Els actius es liquiden de manera nativa a la seva cadena original, de forma trustless (sense confiança en tercers).
- **Zero fees en transaccions**: Gràcies al model de crèdits de recursos de Magi, les transferències són gratuïtes si mantens HBD (un stablecoin lligat al dòlar). Això elimina una de les barreres més grans per a l’ús quotidià de cripto.
- **Seguretat no custodial**: Tu controles sempre les teves claus. No hi ha custòdia centralitzada, el que redueix dràsticament els riscos d’hacks o fallides d’intermediaris.
- **Generació de rendiment**: Des del tauler d’Altera pots staking HBD i obtenir fins a un 15% d’APR (rendiment anualitzat). A més, els usuaris poden proporcionar liquiditat a pools o convertir-se en validadors per guanyar recompenses addicionals provinents de les comissions d’intercanvi.
- **Interoperabilitat avançada**: La xarxa Magi permet interaccions entre ecosistemes com Hive, Bitcoin, DASH i cadenes EVM, obrint la porta a un veritable DeFi unificat.

### Com funciona la tecnologia darrere d’Altera?

Magi Network actua com una capa que connecta diferents blockchains mitjançant light clients, proves de coneixement zero (ZKPs) i esquemes de signatures de llindar (TSS). Això permet operacions segures i descentralitzades sense dependre d’intermediaris.

El resultat és una experiència fluida: selecciones els actius que vols intercanviar, confirmes l’operació i tot es resol de manera nativa a les cadenes respectives. A més, la integració amb Hive permet velocitats altes i costos mínims, mentre que la compatibilitat amb Bitcoin obre possibilitats interessants com pools de liquiditat natius de BTC.

### Per a qui està pensat Altera?

Altera és ideal per a:
- Usuaris de Hive que volen expandir-se a Bitcoin o EVM sense complicacions.
- Holders de BTC que busquen rendiment en DeFi sense haver de moure els seus bitcoins a ponts poc segurs.
- Entusiastes del DeFi que valoren la seguretat, la simplicitat i l’absència de comissions.
- Persones que volen participar en la xarxa com proveïdors de liquiditat o validadors.

### El futur de la interoperabilitat blockchain

Magi Network (anteriorment conegut com a VSC Network) posiciona Altera com una eina fonamental per a un ecosistema cripto més connectat. Amb actualitzacions constants en l’aplicació, millores en l’UX i expansió de funcionalitats (com la gestió de liquiditat avançada o operacions amb Bitcoin), el projecte avança cap a un DEX testnet complet i més integracions.

En un moment en què la fragmentació entre cadenes limita el potencial de la tecnologia blockchain, projectes com Altera demostren que és possible unificar l’espai cripto de manera segura, ràpida i econòmica.

Si estàs cansat de ponts complicats, comissions altes i riscos innecessaris, et convidem a provar **Altera a altera.magi.eco**. Una sola cartera per a totes les cadenes: el futur de les finances descentralitzades ja és aquí.

**Enllaços útils:**
- Lloc web: https://altera.magi.eco/
- Documentació: https://docs.magi.eco/ o https://docs.vsc.eco
- Xarxa principal: https://vsc.eco/

La revolució cross-chain ha començat. Benvinguts a l’era d’Altera.

body.title: Involución Social: Cuando la Hipocresía se Convierte en Nuestra Mejor Gala
body.body:
![568947.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/maxipiano78/23tvcSL8AvBPc4tcUEWRdNEe3CDXsxst4Q9CW39VCeh9MccsFBUnqxaR6Be9v5D5P3YSq.jpg)
>

Involución Social: Cuando la Hipocresía se Convierte en Nuestra Mejor Gala

>
¿Evolución o involución social? He estado dándole vueltas a la cabeza sobre la hipocresía social y sus porqués. Comencemos por algo simple: ¿Por qué felicitar a alguien en un día especial si, en realidad, no te importa cómo vive ni lo que pasa en su vida? Siempre he pensado en eso, pero mi reflexión va más allá. He vivido situaciones en las que perdí a amigos y vi cómo todos fingieron quererlos el día de su muerte. La verdad es que, en vida, no les importaba nada de lo que les pasara; o peor aún, su situación era objeto de mofa y tema de conversación, no de preocupación. Es aquí donde resuena con fuerza esa frase lapidaria:
<hr>
<hr>
«He visto velorios donde sobra la comida, pero el muerto pasaba hambre».
<hr>
<hr>
Y no hablo solo de comida física, para el que sepa entender la profundidad de esas palabras.
<hr>
<hr>
La máscara de la empatía en la era digital
Hoy en día, la involución y la hipocresía nos consumen mientras fingimos ser las mejores personas del mundo. Un ser con depresión, por ejemplo, suele ser más digno de críticas que de ayuda. Recordando aquel video de Marcos sobre la depresión, me pregunto: ¿Por qué fingir que alguien te importa solo en un día especial o cuando ya ni siquiera está en este plano terrenal?
<hr>
<hr>
Las redes sociales nos han dado la falsa creencia de que tenemos derecho a opinar de todo o a juzgar sin contexto. Recuerdo un video filtrado hace años sobre el abuso a una niña donde, en lugar de indignación pura, muchos comentarios se enfocaban en que la víctima «parecía disfrutar». ¿Qué tan podridos debemos estar para emitir un juicio así?
<hr>
<hr>
Religión, dinero y el pedestal de la superioridad
Siguiendo con esta involución, no puedo dejar pasar el hecho de que vivimos en una sociedad donde se cree que profesar una religión te hace automáticamente \

y te otorga un mazo de juez. Hablan en nombre de un Dios que es amor, pero lo que emana de sus bocas es puro odio.
<hr>
<hr>
Lo mismo sucede con el estatus económico. Tener un trabajo o dinero parece dar derecho a juzgar al que no lo tiene, ignorando su realidad. Somos juzgadores de oficio por excelencia: creemos que entre más señalamos, más perfectos somos, cuando la realidad es que esa actitud solo oculta un vacío interno.
<hr>
<hr>
La caridad como espectáculo
Incluso la caridad ha involucionado. Hoy, regalar un plato de comida parece no tener valor si no hay una cámara grabando para ganar likes o validación. Se hace por el \

, no de corazón.
Jamás había entendido la frase: «Me río del hambre después de que como». A veces venimos de abajo y, al llegar arriba, olvidamos que los procesos y tiempos de cada persona son distintos. Lo que para ti es desperdicio (como esa comida que botas porque no te gusta), para otro sería una bendición absoluta.
Reflexión Final Para entender ciertas cosas, hay que tocar fondo o ponerse en los zapatos de los demás desde la realidad, no desde la comodidad de una pantalla. Como bien decía aquella frase de la película venezolana Hora Cero:
«La vaina cambia cuando al que le duele es a uno».
Debemos dejar de ser espectadores de la tragedia ajena y jueces de vidas que no conocemos. La verdadera evolución no está en la tecnología que usamos, sino en la calidad de la humanidad que nos queda.

ENGLISH

Social Involution: When Hypocrisy Becomes Our Finest Attire

>
<hr>
<hr>
Social evolution or involution? I’ve been turning it over in my mind, thinking about social hypocrisy and its \

Let’s start with something simple: Why congratulate someone on a special day if, in reality, you don’t care how they live or what is happening in their life? I’ve always thought about this, but my reflection goes deeper. I have lived through situations where I lost friends and saw how everyone pretended to love them on the day of their death. The truth is, while they were alive, no one cared what happened to them; or worse, their situation was an object of mockery and a topic of conversation, not concern. This is where that devastating phrase resonates with force:
<hr>
<hr>
\

<hr>
<hr>
And I am not just talking about physical food, for those who understand the depth of those words.
<hr>
<hr>
The Mask of Empathy in the Digital Age
Nowadays, involution and hypocrisy consume us while we pretend to be the best people in the world. A person with depression, for example, is usually more worthy of criticism than help. Recalling that video by Marcos about depression, I wonder: Why pretend that someone matters to you only on a special day or when they are no longer even on this earthly plane?
<hr>
<hr>
Social media has given us the false belief that we have the right to have an opinion on everything or to judge without context. I remember a video leaked years ago about the abuse of a girl where, instead of pure indignation, many comments focused on the victim \

How rotten must we be to issue a judgment like that?
<hr>
<hr>
Religion, Money, and the Pedestal of Superiority
Continuing with this involution, I cannot ignore the fact that we live in a society where it is believed that professing a religion automatically makes you \

and hands you a judge's gavel. They speak in the name of a God who is love, but what flows from their mouths is pure hatred.
<hr>
<hr>
The same happens with economic status. Having a job or money seems to give one the right to judge the person who doesn’t, ignoring their reality. We are professional judges by trade: we believe that the more we point fingers, the more perfect we are, when the reality is that this attitude only hides an internal void.
<hr>
<hr>
Charity as a Spectacle
Even charity has involuted. Today, giving a plate of food seems to have no value if there isn't a camera recording to earn likes or validation. It is done for \

not from the heart.
<hr>
<hr>
I never understood the phrase: \

Sometimes we come from the bottom and, upon reaching the top, we forget that everyone's processes and timelines are different. What is waste to you (like that food you throw away because you don't like it) would be an absolute blessing to someone else.
<hr>
<hr>
Final Reflection
To understand certain things, you have to hit rock bottom or put yourself in others' shoes from a place of reality, not from the comfort of a screen. As that phrase from the Venezuelan film Hora Cero (Zero Hour) aptly said:
<hr>
<hr>
\
We must stop being spectators of others' tragedies and judges of lives we do not know. True evolution is not in the technology we use, but in the quality of the humanity we have left.

That afternoon the café was really quiet. You could hear every sound, like the cups clinking and the fan humming, there were people talking at tables but it was not very loud.
Ella and Sheila were sitting across from each other, they were not saying anything, they just say , the silence between them did not feel any thing like peaceful at all.

Ella and Sheila had been friends for a time, they had laughed together talked all night and shared secrets for many years, but that day something was not right.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmW3wVAzgFDYGa9BURmv7kHMrxHykuxu5Y3ftRRvY85aNY/1776863062412.png)

Sheila was the first one to talk, \
she said.\n\nElla leaned back in her chair and crossed her arms. \
she said.\n\nSheila looked upset, She was trying not to say something, but you could tell she wanted to say more \

Before Sheila could respond, someone approached their table.

“Wow… this looks intense.” It was Tory.

He pulled out a chair and sat down casually, glancing between the two of them, “Should I be here, or am I interrupting something serious?”

Sheila sighed. \

she said.

Sheila ignored Ella, “Let me ask you something, If someone you care about just cuts you off without explanation, how would you feel?”

Tory paused, thinking for a moment. “Honestly? I would feel confused… maybe even hurt, Ella scoffed. “Oh, great, now we are taking opinions?”


Tory looked at her calmly. \
he said. Then he asked Ella \
\n\nElla hesitated for a second before answering, \
she said.\n\nEllas voice got a little louder, \

she said.

That surprised both Sheila and Tory.

Sheilas voice was softer0She still did not back down. \
he said.\n\nElla looked down at the table, she did not seem confident anymore, \

she said.

There was a pause, It felt less tense and more like they were thinking about what they had said.

Sheilas voice was quieter now, \
she said.\n\nElla looked up at her, you could see the guilt on her face, \
she said.\n\nTory leaned back in his chair. \

he said.

Neither Ella nor Sheila argued with that.

Ella nodded a little, \
she said.\n\nTory smiled, he could tell the atmosphere had changed. \

he said.

Sheila laughed a little and even Ella managed a smile.

The tension at the table started to go and it was replaced by something softer, Understanding or, at least the start of it.

Sometimes all it takes is someone Perspective to make people see things they could not see before.. Sometimes all it really takes is a conversation.

body.title: [ESP/ENG] Día internacional de la Madre Tierra /  International Mother Earth Day
body.body:
**Una introducción necesaria **


Cada 22 de abril, el Día Internacional de la Madre Tierra nos recuerda que habitamos un planeta vivo, generoso y frágil. Hoy, más que nunca, la Tierra nos pide actuar. Los océanos se llenan de plásticos y se vuelven más ácidos; el calor extremo, los incendios forestales y las inundaciones afectan a millones de personas; y cerca de un millón de especies están en peligro de extinción.


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWxgMoKWKiEppYstV1bDGbjDArtejZCYVJqn8h9wcMUjr/1776862527006.jpg)[fuente](https://share.google/EWoXM4PlUC3iLsX9E)



Estos fenómenos, impulsados por el cambio climático, la deforestación, el uso intensivo del suelo y el comercio ilegal de vida silvestre, aceleran la destrucción de los ecosistemas que sostienen toda forma de vida. 

La salud de los ecosistemas es la salud del planeta y de quienes lo habitamos. Cuando se degradan, aumentan la pobreza, la vulnerabilidad ante enfermedades y la pérdida de biodiversidad. Restaurarlos, en cambio, contribuye a combatir el cambio climático, prevenir extinciones masivas y fortalecer la resiliencia de las comunidades. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTV6NoEQ87sSdMjkuXgsULomKoJq8vknarS3pRtY7xZf8/1776859375057.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPYWUb3Ww9YdyKEo7RL5jykuUx4etMckUZY8nddV7R6a7/1776859398168.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTtMumUNsA5fxgFgfiGj4QiQak1ebbTbYo9jF2CqVcBRt/1776861826915.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbSCRNxkqeG7AoAkLGKhpv4D6pV3chreYCsSNVBKnYZsg/1776861847617.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR5fLUDWHKHeAmiGjAeMFVPVySTTKPhjC5DsJmrTmNEgB/1776861770461.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmd8HVD6Sp9zXHGLyCj4bXW1XyhchL2UGim5GDMZJRjJnp/1776861870108.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNULPdLQZD3ADVTaeAxeFw9yKoyi8g5fuYo4kDQZXWArS/1776861965018.jpg)




**La importancia de cuidar y conservar nuestro planeta**

Cuidar la Tierra no es un gesto simbólico: es una responsabilidad colectiva de una gran importancia. La ONU recuerda que necesitamos un cambio profundo hacia una economía sostenible que funcione tanto para las personas como para el planeta. Esto implica repensar nuestros modelos de producción, consumo y relación con la naturaleza, promoviendo la armonía con ella y reconociendo que somos parte de un sistema interdependiente. 


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR4w8NzZPvA1jPEkNt1ZTuxJKjjUdx2gnawNRgDaAw187/1776862251016.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVh61T3P6yDBz5jrBmPpZfwQXX155nrcyHZAQmVbKfUUK/1776862197329.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdZVmk6UoCzfWZezdDokPy1rgo2Y6ots4e4Mr17kWkun9/1776862132338.jpg)


Además, la crisis ambiental actual —la triple crisis de pérdida de biodiversidad, cambio climático y contaminación— amenaza el cumplimiento de los Objetivos de Desarrollo Sostenible y exige una respuesta integral. Los pueblos indígenas y las comunidades locales, guardianes históricos de la biodiversidad, nos muestran que otra relación con la Tierra es posible: una basada en el respeto, el conocimiento tradicional y la reciprocidad. 




**Acciones para un planeta mejor**

Aunque los desafíos son enormes, cada persona puede contribuir a la restauración del planeta. La campaña global Actúa Ahora propone acciones simples y cotidianas para reducir nuestra huella ambiental:  

- Reducir el consumo de energía y optar por fuentes renovables cuando sea posible.  
- Disminuir el uso de plásticos de un solo uso.  
- Priorizar el transporte sostenible: caminar, usar bicicleta o transporte público.  
- Adoptar dietas más responsables, con menor impacto ambiental.  
- Proteger y restaurar espacios naturales en nuestras comunidades.  
- Educar y sensibilizar a otros sobre la importancia de la conservación. 

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdCmi1T7jxdSTnj3s5RjYtLmA3kj3eswisQpiX8pD4Jbv/1776863134994.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPBmLuUKZmBMe24Q28oKayaboHG41PHnVm59TjLbM9PQf/1776863213532.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSVtoTHwQuzf3TyusBA1SuEVBT4zZTFNsAm77ig8hfpEP/1776863342700.jpg)


A nivel global, los acuerdos internacionales —como el Marco Mundial de Biodiversidad de Kunming-Montreal— buscan detener y revertir la pérdida de naturaleza mediante metas concretas y la participación de toda la sociedad. 


**Un comentario final **

El Día de la Madre Tierra no es solo una fecha: es un recordatorio de que aún estamos a tiempo de restaurar lo que hemos dañado. Cada acción cuenta. Cada gesto suma. La Tierra nos sostiene, nos alimenta y nos da hogar. Cuidarla es, en esencia, cuidarnos a nosotros mismos y a las generaciones que vendrán porque sin ella no podemos vivir.


*Nota: He utilizado el traductor DeepL Translate.
Las fotos son de mi propiedad.
La imagen está referenciada*.



**ENGLISH**



A Necessary Introduction 

Every April 22, International Mother Earth Day reminds us that we inhabit a living, generous, and fragile planet. Today, more than ever, the Earth is asking us to act. The oceans fill up with plastics and become more acidic; extreme heat, wildfires, and floods affect millions of people; and about a million species are in danger of extinction.

These phenomena, driven by climate change, deforestation, intensive land use and illegal wildlife trade, accelerate the destruction of ecosystems that sustain all life. 

The health of ecosystems is the health of the planet and those who inhabit it. When they are degraded, they increase poverty, vulnerability to disease, and biodiversity loss. Restoring them, on the other hand, contributes to combating climate change, preventing mass extinctions and strengthening the resilience of communities. 


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTV6NoEQ87sSdMjkuXgsULomKoJq8vknarS3pRtY7xZf8/1776859375057.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPYWUb3Ww9YdyKEo7RL5jykuUx4etMckUZY8nddV7R6a7/1776859398168.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmTtMumUNsA5fxgFgfiGj4QiQak1ebbTbYo9jF2CqVcBRt/1776861826915.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbSCRNxkqeG7AoAkLGKhpv4D6pV3chreYCsSNVBKnYZsg/1776861847617.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR5fLUDWHKHeAmiGjAeMFVPVySTTKPhjC5DsJmrTmNEgB/1776861770461.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmd8HVD6Sp9zXHGLyCj4bXW1XyhchL2UGim5GDMZJRjJnp/1776861870108.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmNULPdLQZD3ADVTaeAxeFw9yKoyi8g5fuYo4kDQZXWArS/1776861965018.jpg)


**The importance of caring for and conserving**

Caring for the Earth is not a symbolic gesture: it is a collective responsibility. The UN reminds us that we need a profound shift towards a sustainable economy that works for both people and the planet. This implies rethinking our models of production, consumption and relationship with nature, promoting harmony with it and recognizing that we are part of an interdependent system. 


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmR4w8NzZPvA1jPEkNt1ZTuxJKjjUdx2gnawNRgDaAw187/1776862251016.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVh61T3P6yDBz5jrBmPpZfwQXX155nrcyHZAQmVbKfUUK/1776862197329.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdZVmk6UoCzfWZezdDokPy1rgo2Y6ots4e4Mr17kWkun9/1776862132338.jpg)


In addition, the current environmental crisis – the triple crisis of biodiversity loss, climate change and pollution – threatens the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals and requires a comprehensive response. Indigenous peoples and local communities, historical guardians of biodiversity, show us that another relationship with the Earth is possible: one based on respect, traditional knowledge and reciprocity. 

**Actions for a better planet**

Although the challenges are enormous, each person can contribute to the restoration of the planet. The global Act Now campaign proposes simple, everyday actions to reduce our environmental footprint:  

- Reduce energy consumption and opt for renewable sources where possible.  
- Reduce the use of single-use plastics.  
- Prioritise sustainable transport: walking, cycling or public transport.  
- Adopt more responsible diets, with less environmental impact.  
- Protect and restore natural spaces in our communities.  
- Educate and sensitize others about the importance of conservation. 



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdCmi1T7jxdSTnj3s5RjYtLmA3kj3eswisQpiX8pD4Jbv/1776863134994.jpg)


![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPBmLuUKZmBMe24Q28oKayaboHG41PHnVm59TjLbM9PQf/1776863213532.jpg)



![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmSVtoTHwQuzf3TyusBA1SuEVBT4zZTFNsAm77ig8hfpEP/1776863342700.jpg)


At the global level, international agreements – such as the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework – seek to halt and reverse nature loss through concrete targets and the participation of the whole of society. 

**A final comment** 

Mother Earth Day is not just a date: it is a reminder that we still have time to restore what we have damaged. Every action counts. Every gesture counts. The Earth sustains us, feeds us, and gives us a home. To take care of it is, in essence, to take care of ourselves and the generations to come because without it we cannot live.

*Note: I used the DeepL Translate translator.
The photos are my property.
Image is referenced.*

body.body: As a football fan, I enjoy debates about which club deserves the title of “best in the world.” In reality, that kind of label changes depending on the era, the squad, and the manager's philosophy. Some clubs dominate because of tactical innovation, while others succeed through strong team chemistry and consistency. What fascinates me most is analyzing how clubs adapt to different competitions and opponents. I spend a lot of time reading match analyses, and during one discussion about performance metrics I actually saw a [Melbet India review](https://english.webdunia.com/article/sports-news/how-cricket-tournament-became-indias-economic-driver-melbet-india-review-126031300005_1.html) mentioned in the middle of a conversation about statistical evaluation of teams. It showed how even fan discussions sometimes drift toward deeper analytical topics. Ultimately, every supporter has their own reasons for believing their club is the best. That passion is what makes football culture so exciting.

body.title: The internet can Mar You
body.body:
![243661.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josediccus/23yJV5NjcANr4pJsekE5FwyxuMxpbFypk9xnL71gPfEb3HzcsdA3wykMNXfACBaYkPz31.png)



<hr>

Recently a particular influencer posted about lying in an interview to secure a 350$ job per day, the funny thing is that the video went very viral and his employers saw the video and decided to sack him and his colleague that made this same video. 

This guy has been living in the UK for a long while now, he basically has a stable income, a good paying job, and a healthy family. 

It's that type of life that anyone will give anything to have, but he decided to start creating contents about his life but graduated to making a more unique type of content. 


The content he does makes fun of real life events in a way that attracts engagement, he basically talks about his bosses, his duties, his promotion and all that. 

He was actually the manager in his place of work, so I'm not sure he would be working somewhere else, so it seems like this was the particular job he lost, but even though it wasn't. 350$ a day gig is one hell of a job to actually lose. 


So back in the day I used to watch his videos, I found it very humorous, but at some point I unfollowed him I think because they started adding a tint of sexual hue to their content. 

Also this guy's video goes viral because he was know to always post videos or images of private chats and conversations, and I'm sure that people actually wanted more of these contents.

 He was always posting close-relationship moments with clients and relatives and stuffs like that and that was how he got to grow his page. I think people wanted more of those contents and he usually go extreme and probably went too extreme this time and it caught up with him. 

He probably just wanted to make another video like he always does, but people would probably want to know what type of job paid him that money. 

If he was earning 10$ a day, maybe no one would have cared if he lied or not. These are fbr types of content that create reactions, reactions create curiosity which them brings virality. 


The dream of every content creator is to go viral. This actually attracts audience, which brings more attractions and automation bump in social media earnings. 

Perhaps he never minded if he lost, maybe or maybe not, maybe he wanted to go full-time content creating, but that is in a country like UK where going viral for the wrong reasons can actually get you blacklisted.

 It might just be difficult to get a job in another place, or he might no longer attract the quality type of job he always had, and all that years he's spent building his reputation, brand and CV all tainted by just one unintentional video he's posted on the internet. 

### The internet virality & sensation 

He may have lost his recommendation and all that, and we'd only find out how much this might impact him going forward. He's however come out to debunk the new that he was sacked, he claimed be wasn't and that he is still doing the job.

 This might be some form of damage control, but truth is I saw the video and he actually confessed to lying to get the job. 

It's crazy because people cannot understand that some information aren't supposed to make the internet, this is something he wouldn't have necessarily said or lied to get which makes it quite hard from people from his demographs who are struggling to actually secure jobs. 


The internet is truly full of money making opportunities, and some people are not drawing the line on the information they intend to give off.

body.title: Wednesday Walk - Strolling through the streets of a city full of art, discovering it step by step. / Paseando por las calles de una ciudad llena de arte, descubriéndola a cada paso. 😃❤️
body.body:
> If there’s one thing I never got tired of doing on my last trip, it was going out for walks. Exploring new and beautiful places is something that fills my soul, and luckily, during my journey through the Northeast of Argentina, I got plenty of that. When I finally arrived in Corrientes to meet up with Gabi and Luis, friends from Hive, I was eager to go explore the city and see what it was like. Fortunately, it was even more beautiful than I had imagined, and I had the privilege of exploring it with two great local guides ❤️.
Si hay algo que no me cansé de hacer en mi último viaje, fue salir a caminar. Recorrer lugares nuevos y hermosos es algo que me llena el alma, y por suerte, durante mi paseo por el Noreste de Argentina pude tener mucho de esto. Cuando finalmente llegué a Corrientes para encontrarme con Gabi y Luis, unos amigos de Hive, estaba ansiosa por ir a recorrer la ciudad y ver cómo sería. Por suerte, era más hermosa de lo que pensaba, y tuve el privilegio de ir con dos grandes guías locales ❤️.
---

> --- During the days I spent visiting the city of Corrientes, Gabi and Luis were very kind to accompany me on some outings. From their home, we had to take a bus to the city center, and in just a few minutes we arrived. That day marked the beginning of a walk that took us through several of the most beautiful spots in the city, with its traditional buildings and murals, as well as the must-see square with historic buildings all around it.
Durante los días que estuve visitando la ciudad de Corrientes, Gabi y Luis fueron muy amables acompañándome a pasear un poco. Desde su casa, debíamos tomar un bus hasta el centro de la ciudad, y en pocos minutos llegábamos. Ese día empezó la caminata que nos hizo recorrer varios de los puntos más lindos de la ciudad, con sus edificios y murales tradicionales, además de la infaltable plaza con los edificios históricos alrededor.
---

> --- One of the things I liked the most about this city was how decorated it was. In many corners, there were murals in a similar style, with warm colors and textures that gave it a unique identity. During our walk, we visited several of them adorning different spots, but the city is full of the marks left by the artists who created them. According to the internet, there are more than 400 of these murals in the city—amazing.
Una de las cuestiones que más me gustó de esta ciudad era lo decoraba que estaba. En un montón de rincones de la ciudad habían murales con estilo similar, en colores cálidos y relieves que le daban identidad propia. Durante nuestro recorrido, visitamos varios de ellos adornando distintos puntos, pero la ciudad esta llena de las huellas de los artistas que los hicieron. Según internet, en la ciudad hay más de 400 de estos murales, increíble.
---

> --- Another interesting spot during our visit to the city was the waterfront promenade. In this area, we were able to get closer to the riverside and the yacht club, where we saw all the boats and started to notice some of the golden sand that characterizes the coast of Corrientes. I really liked this place because of how neat and clean it was—it was clear that the city makes an effort to keep it well maintained.
Otro punto interesante durante nuestra visita a la ciudad fue el Paseo Costero. En esta parte nos pudimos acercar un poco a la costanera y al club náutico, en donde vimos todos los botes y se empezó a ver algo de la arena dorada que caracteriza la costa de Corrientes. Este lugar me gustó mucho por lo prolijo y limpio que estaba: se notaba que la ciudad se esfuerza en mantenerse prolija.
---

> --- I found the city of Corrientes incredibly photogenic at every turn: everywhere there was something beautiful to see and capture, like the lighthouse, the boats, the monuments, the shoreline, and the murals. Being there in person, I understood why Luis and Gabi enjoy taking photos for Hive: their city is truly beautiful and deserves to be shared. I was glad we started our walk early because, in the absence of trekking in the mountains, we ended up exploring all over the place.
La ciudad de Corrientes me pareció muy fotografiable a cada paso: en todos lados había algo lindo para ver y retratar, como el faro, los barcos, los monumentos, la costa, los murales. Estando en vivo y en directo ahí entendí por qué a Luis y a Gabi les gusta sacar fotos para Hive: su ciudad es bellísima y merece ser compartida. Me alegré de haber arrancado nuestro paseo temprano porque a falta de trekking en las montañas, anduvimos por todos lados.
---

> --- I will always be grateful to Gabi and Luis for showing me their city with so much care, and for welcoming me into their home with such kindness. The province of Corrientes was the last one left on my travel list, and sharing this achievement together was very special. I truly enjoyed everything we saw, and continuing to discover my country, Argentina, was very fulfilling—without a doubt, we live in a very beautiful land ❤️.
Siempre voy a estar agradecida con Gabi y Luis por haberme mostrado su ciudad con tanto cariño, y por haberme recibido en su casa con tanta amabilidad. La provincia de Corrientes era la última que me quedaba por visitar dentro de mi lista de viajes, y compartir este logro juntos fue muy especial. Me gustó mucho cada cosa que vimos y seguir conociendo mi país Argentina fue muy satisfactorio: sin dudas, vivimos en una tierra muy hermosa ❤️.
--- ---

❤️ Hope you liked this post! Thanks for reading. ❤️

❤️¡Espero que les haya gustado este post! Gracias por leer. ❤️
--- ---

> ---
With lots of love. / Con mucho amor. Lau 💕.

body.title: Understanding the Importance of In-Home Care Services in Colorado
body.body:
## In-Home Care Services in Colorado

In today’s fast-paced world, families are constantly looking for reliable ways to support their loved ones without compromising their independence. In-home care services have become a trusted solution, especially for seniors and individuals who prefer the comfort of their own homes. Staying in a familiar environment helps maintain emotional well-being, routine, and a sense of security.

As more people move away from institutional care, the demand for flexible and compassionate support continues to rise. In the middle of this shift, [Non-Medical In-Home Care Colorado](https://www.premiercarecolorado.com/services-offered/) has become an essential option for those who need help with daily living activities without requiring medical treatment, allowing individuals to live safely and comfortably at home.



![Nurse-speaking-with-couple.jpeg](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/926943481bc7c56e5d406406e159ece39da2dc9f6c655d1d11b6792f881cd716)



## What Is Non-Medical In-Home Care?

Non-medical in-home care is a type of service designed to assist individuals with everyday tasks while promoting independence and dignity. Unlike medical home health care, it does not involve clinical procedures or licensed medical professionals, but instead focuses on personal support and companionship.

Caregivers help with routine activities such as bathing, dressing, meal preparation, and light housekeeping. They also provide emotional support, which plays a vital role in reducing loneliness and improving overall mental health, especially for seniors living alone.

## Key Benefits of Non-Medical In-Home Care

One of the biggest advantages of non-medical in-home care is the ability to maintain independence. Individuals can continue living in their own homes while receiving the assistance they need, which helps preserve their dignity and sense of control over daily life.

Another important benefit is personalized attention. Care plans are tailored to individual needs, ensuring the right level of support at the right time. This flexibility allows services to adapt as needs change, providing long-term comfort and peace of mind for both clients and their families.

## Services Included in Non-Medical In-Home Care

Non-medical in-home care services cover a wide range of daily needs that support both physical and emotional well-being. These services are designed to make everyday life easier while ensuring a safe and comfortable living environment.

Common services include personal care assistance, companionship, meal preparation, light housekeeping, transportation support, and medication reminders. Each service can be customized based on the individual’s preferences and lifestyle.

## Who Can Benefit from These Services?

Non-medical in-home care is ideal for seniors who want to age in place while maintaining their independence. It allows them to stay connected to their home, community, and daily routines while receiving the support they need.

Individuals with disabilities or those recovering from surgery can also benefit greatly. Additionally, busy families often rely on these services to ensure their loved ones are well cared for when they cannot provide full-time assistance.

## How to Choose the Right In-Home Care Provider in Colorado

Choosing the right care provider is a crucial decision that requires careful consideration. It’s important to look for a provider with a strong reputation, experienced caregivers, and a commitment to delivering personalized care.

You should also ensure the provider offers flexible care plans and maintains open communication with families. Transparency, reliability, and compassion are key qualities that define a trustworthy in-home care service.

## The Future of Non-Medical In-Home Care

The demand for non-medical in-home care is expected to grow as more people recognize its benefits. With an aging population and a preference for home-based care, this service is becoming an essential part of modern healthcare support systems.

Technology is also playing a role in improving care delivery, making it easier for caregivers and families to stay connected. Providers like [Premier Care Colorado](https://www.premiercarecolorado.com/) continue to lead the way by offering compassionate, high-quality care tailored to individual needs.

***

## FAQs About Non-Medical In-Home Care

**1. What is non-medical in-home care?**

It is a service that helps individuals with daily activities such as bathing, cooking, and companionship without providing medical treatment.

**2. Who needs non-medical in-home care?**

Seniors, individuals with disabilities, and those recovering from illness or surgery can benefit from these services.

**3. Is non-medical in-home care customizable?**

Yes, care plans are tailored to meet each individual’s specific needs and preferences.

**4. How is it different from medical home care?**

Non-medical care focuses on daily living support, while medical care involves clinical services provided by licensed professionals.

**5. Can care be provided full-time?**

Yes, services can be arranged on a part-time, full-time, or live-in basis depending on the needs.

body.body: >No flotes a la deriva, rema con propósito.
>Don't float adrift, paddle with purpose.
>Pront: Simplemente estoy a la deriva.
>Hace unos días, me encontré con un amigo y me puse a conversar sobre la situación política nacional, mundial y sobre nuestra economía familiar en estos tiempos de crisis.

>En medio de la conversación, me di cuenta de que el discurso era el mismo de hace meses, es decir, la crítica a los malos servicios, el problema del dólar paralelo, el alto costo de la vida y la merma de nuestra economía.

>Y al despedirme, me di cuenta de que realmente me estaba dejando llevar por las situaciones y que prácticamente parecía un barco a la deriva que se dejaba llevar por las diferentes corrientes por las que cruzaba.

>Y al tomar consciencia de esa realidad, simplemente decidí darle nuevamente un camino a mi vida, decidí tomar las riendas y dejar de ser llevados por las corrientes, decidí simplemente ya no estar a la deriva, y para hacerlo comencé a planificar y tomar decisiones.

>Y aunque hay situaciones en las que no puedo tener una injerencia directa, como la falla de los servicios públicos o el alto coste de la vida, también me di cuenta de que sí puedo decidir el cómo me afectan esas realidades y el cómo enfrentar las mismas.

>Así que me hice un método; ya no espero que no falle un servicio, sino que ya tengo preparado por si llega a fallar. Además, creé un plan de actividades para hacer útil y creativo el tiempo sin servicio eléctrico o de agua.

>También decidí retomar actividades que me hacían feliz, me mantenían creativo y me ayudaban a aumentar mis ingresos, y así, al darme cuenta de la realidad en que vivía por una conversación, decidí tomar las riendas, dejar de estar a la deriva y disfrutar y estar agradecido por cada instante de mi vida.
>A few days ago, I met a friend and started talking about the national and world political situation and about our family economy in these times of crisis.

>In the middle of the conversation, I realized that the speech was the same as it was months ago, that is, the criticism of bad services, the problem of the parallel dollar, the high cost of living and the decline of our economy.

>And as I was saying goodbye, I realized that I was really getting carried away by the situations and that I practically looked like a drifting ship that was being carried away by the different currents I was crossing.

>And when I became aware of that reality, I simply decided to give my life a path again, I decided to take charge and stop being carried by the currents, I simply decided not to be adrift anymore, and to do so I began to plan and make decisions.

>And although there are situations in which I cannot have a direct interference, such as the failure of public services or the high cost of living, I also realized that I can decide how those realities affect me and how to face them.

>So I made myself a method; I no longer wait for a service not to fail, but I already have it ready in case it fails. In addition, I created an activity plan to make the time without electricity or water service useful and creative.

>I also decided to resume activities that made me happy, kept me creative and helped me increase my income, and so, realizing the reality in which I lived by a conversation, I decided to take charge, stop being adrift and enjoy and be grateful for every moment of my life.

>Thank you very much for reading me.

body.title: In the night (oil on paper)
body.body:
Hello hivers, an happy Wednesday to you all! It's a warm sunny day here and a lot of beautiful birds are flying around and singing in my backyard and in the garden close to mine. The fruits on my plum tree are growing up and soon they will be ready to eat and to cook a good jam (I can't wait to eat the new jam!). ❤️ This morning, like I use to do every day, I woke up soon to work with my brushes and colors on a new artwork during the first hours of the day. I have to give some other touches to a painting on canvas, but while I'm waiting it will dry enough to add some details, I worked on a new oil on paper. I just finished to paint it so now I can show you the final result: ![DSCN9963bis2.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/silviabeneforti/23vsFsKAs4FbgaUBKjTSLQNTvAnKthFjStu6eUyR8TXjnRX5KWjCD9qci4bSxFCs3yELq.JPG) ![DSCN9963bis.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/silviabeneforti/23uFMgeJuMk6D3dtBeFCHKKxG1RgzfjhoT88TcmF6BB4wz65oWYQhoy2SKDLSkdMTmfM3.JPG) As you can see, the main subject is one of my usual women in profile with long hair in dark brown color where I painted a scene about home using just some touches of white. It's an oil colors painting on 200 gsm paper in A3 size and, as usual, I took some pics while I was painting it so you can see the process too: ![WhatsApp Image 2026-04-22 at 14.47.17.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/silviabeneforti/EoAbhjvSmeWRwQh1WxoxDPWd5rs4X8ZP1ejtgjLqQwdkWXM9HNHP5rcoQMUgbnjWFYY.jpeg) ![WhatsApp Image 2026-04-22 at 14.47.17 (1).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/silviabeneforti/EoGyMDAsq87wA11LXRfuR3UiQqyX8xGw23Lya3uvkDZ57YWiGz8orEVn1mMHERuaDvB.jpeg) ![DSCN9951.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/silviabeneforti/Eoc84XhnSKhzTsNvEjhtrMCD19LFKgPw5bryUtj7o8ZUQUmUwjZeNoiRazB7AEuwHDr.JPG) ![DSCN9952.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/silviabeneforti/EoeErmbmujc39zRGmFMNnPznn9317JE3cENyFtBbqP2sUWod3Wet7PDPuwomJgNx7bc.JPG) ![DSCN9953.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/silviabeneforti/EogMqcn6yK8NaHU7aKCvtMWhKT4SjefM2uYXdwvUNKHjkhsTuodxS9NwnCn14U9zNn9.JPG) Soon I'll add this new artwork to my Artfinder and Saatchi shops (link at the bottom), hoping it will find a new home! body.title: Spring turns the parks lush and green
body.body:
I think I like spring the most of all seasons. Winter is barren and cold and summer is often too hot. Fall has beautiful colors, but is often windy and rainy. 
But spring makes nature wake up! Plants start growing. Trees are blossoming and starting to grow new leafs. And you hear birds everywhere. I love to go for a walk in nature. And even though I live in an urban area, there is nature in the neighborhood in the form of parks. 

I actually have quite a few nice parks nearby where I live. They aren't really big, but you can certainly make a nice short walk in them and experience a bit of nature.

![path.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23y8m6hDast9nB9Zb2vxc7aLh3hqt7DNsS89Uv7vdHE2ZymBayuL6PTvVESMirie4VXjE.png)

just look at that view. A pathway through a green environment. It's really calming to go for a walk there. It also helps to clear your mind (when you are not thinking about shooting nice photographs all the time that is 😂)

![stinzen.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23vhuD5sYZxyJZgH8MSVsgZKj7KB3LKuRc57nFQ4nDKrmRL32y53xKJVyDjQyy8PYXFhJ.png)

The plants alongside the path are so-called stinzen plants. They cover a large part of the floor in the park and they have a slightly onion-like smell. Very faint, though, so it’s not unpleasant when you walk through it.

![fountain.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/Ep1WueoSXssW11QjgFDwhMNZLGYhU41J49biYMMVHKwKzeaj9RKPTSfkXqmB5Ltprz2.png)

In the middle of the park there is a pond with a fountain. It's a nice sight. Last year there was a swans nest in the reed at the side of the pond. It's nice to see the swans in the pond, but I didn't spot them this day.

![blossom.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/EowE8NFfaqs9sfi7HB1RcKALjiXUuA1PeNFpJ8PDWxNdEd5CtAtX2Kx3fRYTZGX34e7.png)

The flowers on this tree are almost wilted. A lot of trees are in bloom at the moment. I made a separate blog about it earlier. But most of them are losing their flowers now.

![growth.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23wWtdKYZnhJG21UJycvoZyEVVTRp54xPQ2TeyNDXq1GbogzxC4Qyvn8anR4NetVxctnq.png)

And this is why I find nature so amazing! Just look how this tree develops new twigs and leafs. The twig seems to be cut off, but the tree just develops some new shoots. I find it cool that how I can still be amazed by these kinds of little things.

![divider.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7YWoNDewJkbQoM9yiSvwjFh4yHJuCWXPjgX31Eep5JGnZChA88ZNWdDr6H5FBgdVaj.png)



I’d love to hear your thoughts on my blog. Feel free to share your perspective in the comments.

</center>

body.title: The Company That Collected Her Time and Called It Opportunity
body.body:
I have heard a lot of stories and instances about this IT thing, and I will be sharing some things I personally know. Around late 2024-2025, my cousin went to Lagos to do her internship with one of these firms I wouldn't like to mention; she was there for the duration of her internship without collecting a single Naira. Before then, she had complained to her boss, and that one gaslighted her that she should be grateful for working with them because a lot of her mates were out there looking for where to do their internship. She had no choice, or lemme say her boss made it look like she had no choice. When we talk about people going to a firm or organization for their internship and they get zero pay, that argument looks reasonable when we discuss it. Because some companies give them free accommodation, some usually give them breakfast and lunch. They get a lot of experience and training, including travel and exposure, and some even get connections from there. Without any argument, I will say that is a big value. But in all sincerity, a lot of people have always failed to argue one thing. Do you know that those interns are also providing a lot of value back? Because when we look at it, some are doing most of the workload of the firm. They get to the office very early, filling the empty gaps. They are organizing a lot of things, from writing to picking up calls, attending to people's needs, and going to different meetings with a lot of other workloads on their desk. The funny thing is that some of these interns even do work that is meant for another person, which is not in their payroll. Then, left to me, if the company is also using their services, then the interns should also get something in return. That is not a complex thing because that is how it should be done. You work for me, and I get something back. It's just a simple, honest exchange. ![211900.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenproject/EoCfi2UQfYHuFj9nF4W9CGtprae61eeuQqir6XCUyfp1ACw8tdLjC9uvvrXpkS2o7wo.png) But in some places in this country, that doesn't work because interns are fresh graduates or those about to finish school. Some departments, like Architecture, and others usually do internships before graduating. While some other professional courses, like nursing or medical-related lines, usually go for internships after they are done. So a lot of companies usually take advantage of the opportunity that because some interns are desperately in need of them, they will rather refuse to pay them because the desperation is so real and the system has even failed us, so a lot of people won't talk. And another thing some people don't usually see is that class difference. An intern who is from a struggling family will not be able to do that because he has a lot on his neck. While someone from a well-to-do family might not even bother about the pay. So what I will say is that an internship where there is no payment separates people based on financial background and not their character or ability. And that is totally unfair, and it piles up over time because some industries are shutting their ways towards certain people that can give more extra value. So my thought is that interns should be paid , not out of charity. ![43948333-ai-generated-8777715_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kemmyb/AKHyiQAQWfcbMXyF37Btg1MfzTgLyUaJrYTxVfbykGtX5uLwwCX9z9eDyxWkYTJ.jpg)![divider curl .webp](https://img.blurt.world/blurtimage/kemmyb/a75ed810b8aaff74d2505ddf85186840400c52a1.webp)

<div class=text-justify>

Calls from the hospital never brought good news. Madeline watched her phone buzz on the coffee table. The dreaded call came when she least expected it.

*1 missed call.*

Her phone screen dimmed for a few seconds, then lit up, blinking insistently.

When Curtis held her hand in church, softly touching his lips to her wedding ring before the congregation of friends and family, he promised to never leave her. Her lips curved slightly into a faint smile as the memory returned. Some of them had booed him for refusing to kiss her in front of them.

A year later, she could have sworn that paradise was real. Her smiles and laughs were melodious. Her eyes, bright and beautiful. Her olive-toned skin glowed in a way it never had before. 

She and Curtis were happy.

A violent cough tore him awake one morning and the mucus was laced with blood. She went with him to the hospital and just like that, her paradise began to fade. The green trees and blooming flowers turned brown, shriveled and dried up, falling apart.

If only they had caught the disease earlier, the doctors said. 

She stayed with him through every test and treatment. Her laughter stopped, her smiles became rare, reserved only for him whenever he woke up. Then one night, he didn't wake up and the doctors intubated him.

“We can't report any progress yet, Mrs Zane,” the lead doctor of the medical team explained. “His response to the treatment is slow and if it declines further, we may have to pull him off life support.”

She was numb through the update. The doctor quietly left the room. And so she stayed day after day, watching him slip away. Her mother visited, prayed for him and pulled her into a tight embrace. “Cheer up, Maddy. Sometimes it gets worse before it's better.”

The nurses urged her to go home, take a bath and change. That was their polite way of saying she looked worn down. After much persuasion, she gave in.

*4 missed calls.*

That was an hour ago and now, the hospital was calling. How could Curtis die while she had left his side to freshen up? She wanted to be there with him till the end. 

Her screen lit up again. *Not more news*—she couldn't take it any more. She shook her head, wiping the tears from her face before picking the call.

A shriek rang in her ears, making her flinch. It was one of the nurse. “Mrs Madeleine! Come quickly, it's a miracle—”

Her breaths were coming fast. “Wha-what is it?”

“He's awake,” the nurse gasped. “Your husband is awake.”

Madeline slid to the floor, sobs racking her slender body, the phone still in her hand. This was the best news.

body.title: Sympathy for a Psychopath
body.body:
>

> Trust your gut.

Over the last few decades, there has been a global push to put far more weight on our feelings and to act on our gut, our intuition. It has even been positioned that our intuition knows better than our conscious thought, so acting on how we feel is the logical thing to do. What of course has been omitted from the drive to be emotional actors, is that our intuition is based on our experience and therefore, can be found very lacking, as it answers the wrong question and therefore, suggests the wrong course of action. Not only that, because acting on how we feel automatically makes us feel like we are doing the right thing. It is only in hindsight we might be able to recognise that upon reflection, what we thought was right, was not right at all. What we often omit to protect our ego, is that if we had slowed down and thought about the situation a little longer, we would have realised that our intuition was giving false positives. 

---


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/23u5T8nsE7sZG9CXkpp7DrGQCmhG4vDb7MDfqtPPPy3W8wRxq2YMUUPJMoawmAdkgNB9K.png)


---

Do you know anyone who has been conned? A member of my extended family was swindled by one of those online love scams, where she (an elderly woman) was convinced to send tens of thousands of dollars to a person who she thought needed help for some family issue and blah blah. It was *obviously* a scam but with her inexperience, rather than thinking through the situation logically, she used the sympathy she felt for the person as her guiding force for action. 

> Sympathy for a psychopath.

I don't think that the person was necessarily a psychopath, but the play they run for this type of scam resembles the behaviours of a psychopath, as it preys on the vulnerabilities of emotional decision making. And without experience, the intuition of the mark says \

and doesn't engage the slow thinking processes that would uncover all the inconsistencies and subsequent risks of the situation. Often, even if the person seeks advice from others (they didn't in this case) the emotional decision making process will overpower the advice of others who would warn against trusting the conman.

> Our emotions are extremely strong triggers.

Which is why they are so dangerous to trust. The idea of \

has become popular in recent years with people getting *triggered* by this and that. But I think that it isn't the event that causes the trigger as mush as a lack of ability to apply the right processing system (type 1 as fast and type 2 as slow) before acting. We have been encouraged to trust our system one thought process, which means we aren't going to wake up the system two one at all. We will feel empathy and sympathy and also feel that we are correct in feeling those things, without vetting whether we should or not. 

> While the situation can trigger the emotion, should the emotion trigger an action? 

I am not so sure. At least, some of the time when stakes are higher. For instance, an elderly woman losing her life savings for retirement is a pretty high stakes situation for her, which should automatically set the system two processes into gear. But those processes also have to be trained for what to look for, and where to get help, and who to actually trust *prior* to the decision making process, otherwise it might just kick it back to system one, which often happens. 

As I see it, critical thinking is becoming weaker in people and the new technologies are making it even weaker in us again. Essentially, we are becoming increasingly gullible, because instead of thinking through a problem, we are feeling through the problem instead. And it feels *rational* to do so, because we have been conditioned to \

even when the problem we face is an unknown that we have no experience in. And of course, because we are lazy thinkers and actors by nature, we will end up choosing the solution that is the easiest for us to accept. For some, that means trusting people in situations where consideration is needed, which makes us blind to all the red flags waving about. We are using our attention to act on the feeling, rather than our attention to understand the situation. What is interesting is that pretty much everyone believes that their actions are carefully considered, even though the majority of what we do in a day is automatic. We don't want to believe that we would leave important decisions up to unchecked emotions, so we don't believe it. We create a story that our actions are based on what we consciously decided, instead of an emotion triggered by our unconscious. So much of our daily experience can no longer be trusted, which is why it is so easy to be taken advantage of. There is so much scam, manipulation and influence being pushed at us, and we are so poor at using our slow thinking, that the flood of information overwhelms us and we just take it all at face value, whether it be a phishing scam, or the plethora of AI-generated content that pours through the platform feeds. Even if we do try and slow down our thinking, our fear of missing out will overpower the system again to force more intuitive solutioning, instead of critical thought. There are times and a places to act on emotions. Live in the moment when you are playing with your child, act on feeling when in bed with your partner. But when the stakes are high or when money is involved, slow down and think consciously. body.title: Heritage Meets Gastronomy — The Restaurant Success Story Of Hahndorf
body.body: Australia's oldest surviving German village, Hahndorf, hidden on the fringes of beautiful Adelaide Hills Visiting the historic timber framed buildings has always had great appeal, but now the region's fine dining culture is making its own name. Hahndorf top restaurant locals love bringing guests that beautiful blend of old-world European tradition and contemporary Australian culinary style.\n\nOne of the most important characteristics a great restaurant hahndorf may have is its in-depth \

philosophy. These menus speak of direct access to the area's handmade small goods-makers; they cry out (in mute form) about those rolling hills, still visible land use limited to cream-rich pasture and fine turf. David Chapman Unsurprisingly, the traditional German staples—think smoked bratwurst or perfectly pan-fried schnitzels—will always have a firm cultural foothold but increasingly these days we see long-established menus fused with modern, sophisticated methods for particular worldwide preferences. Frequently accompanied by a benchmark wine list filled with star cool-climate varietals sourced paddle-pushers from South Australia's own back vineyards.

Moreover, the aesthetic experience here is — almost always— just as interesting as the food. The majority of the restaurants are housed in well-preserved 19th century buildings, providing an elegant and historic setting for any business functions or celebratory dinners. With over the top service that makes it easy for tourists and locals alike to 'beef', these venues serve visitors with verb options.

The Hahndorf of today, with its 600+ bus tourists each day, is not a place for the faint-hearted when hoping for authenticity and good hospitality. By reserving an exclusive [restaurant hahndorf](https://theoakbankhotel.com.au/restaurant-hahndorf/), and more often than not makes every trip back worthwhile, whether it is for a stay to soak in modern history politics or just enjoy a combination of gourmet offerings. And this is that classic balance of tradition and modern quality just speaks to the soul of local hospitality.

 

---
