body.title: [ENG/ESP] A Wednesday stroll full of little stories
body.body: > **Greetings, dear #wednesdaywalk community! I hope you have a wonderful day filled with positive energy. As I do every week, I’m happy to connect with you all to share a little bit of my daily routine, thanks to the wonderful initiative by @tattoodjay, who always encourages us to share our walks and enjoy others’ as well. It’s a lovely way to connect, to see our everyday surroundings through fresh eyes, and to appreciate those simple moments that make every day special. My day started very early, as it usually does when we have work to do. We had to head to the Parque Costa Azul Shopping Center to complete a job that had been put on hold the day before, and then we had to find an asbestos gasket to fix an annoying noise in the manifold of the work truck. So, without wasting any time, we got ready and set out in good spirits. The weather was excellent at dawn, one of those days when the sky seems wider and the colors more vivid. That kind of light that makes both urban and natural landscapes look radiant and beautiful. I took the opportunity to capture a few moments with my phone, because I always think of you and how nice it is to share what we see on our journeys.**

> *Mis saludos, querida comunidad de #wednesdaywalk, les deseo un día genial y lleno de buenas energías. Como cada semana, me alegra encontrarme con ustedes para compartir un pedacito de mi rutina, gracias a la hermosa iniciativa de @tattoodjay, que siempre nos motiva a mostrar nuestros recorridos y disfrutar también de los de los demás. Es una manera bonita de conectarnos, de ver nuestros paisajes cotidianos con otros ojos y de valorar esos momentos simples que hacen especial cada día. Mi jornada comenzó bien temprano, como suele ser cuando tenemos trabajo pendiente. Teníamos que dirigirnos al Centro Comercial Parque Costa Azul para realizar un servicio que había quedado en espera el día anterior, y luego debíamos buscar una junta de amianto para corregir un sonido molesto en el múltiple de la camioneta de trabajo. Así que, sin perder tiempo, nos alistamos y salimos con buen ánimo. El clima amaneció excelente, de esos días en los que el cielo parece más amplio y los colores más vivos. Ese tipo de luz que hace que tanto los paisajes urbanos como los naturales se vean radiantes y hermosos.  Aproveché para capturar algunos instantes con mi teléfono, porque siempre pienso en ustedes y en lo bonito que es compartir lo que vemos en nuestros recorridos.*
![photo_2026-04-21_23-41-20.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EppKBettZX2daVmu8Jj4F368wRagpohm6gisX2sg21KjcLrP517ThUuFsj6EHpS72Cv.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-41-14.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EpVA5ReZjwtb17b6Zn49HwD6eMgxZQcSp3DdS3tND4srwHqFpUtc5nN3USzaQBi4aYq.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-41-15.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EqFrzWFD67CtAMdkqudrFQWMKE1PhBAPQynoDZ3DgVc6kgnmWp5cJUSawS9qZcfgYpD.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-41-07.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/23zS7FrP9E3LVbkEs18QszHEorR14qG9JNfcm31nZQ21wPdQXhKf3WCHXy9oXmvCcmQfm.jpg)

> **Between enjoying the scenery and a pleasant conversation with my husband, we arrived at Costa Azul Park, where the maintenance department welcomed us with their usual kindness. We hadn’t been able to perform the service the day before because they were filling the tanks with water, so today was the day to finish the job. After completing our routine chlorination and disinfection, we stayed to monitor the readings until we were sure everything was within the correct ranges. We didn’t leave until we confirmed that every parameter was as it should be.**

> *Entre paisajes y una agradable conversación con mi esposo, llegamos al Parque Costa Azul, donde el departamento de mantenimiento nos recibió con la amabilidad de siempre. El día anterior no habíamos podido realizar el servicio porque estaban surtiendo agua en los tanques, así que hoy tocaba completar la labor. Después de hacer nuestra rutina de clorado y desinfección, nos quedamos midiendo los valores hasta asegurarnos de que todo estuviera en los rangos correctos. No nos retiramos hasta confirmar que cada parámetro estuviera como debía ser.*
![photo_2026-04-21_23-41-04.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/Ep3cPzi5vb4wDZaH5tWiktLLiHmVVs1ieZuuJezeLoFidCn59ZJbjpDUvzPH3sVWdmZ.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-40-04.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/Eqd8VBBEu5DAjz1mY7x6hCs1T5N7LXFipbsoJs7cQYCdYqrRSTGqiSfAugPebWDvmmP.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-40-04 (2).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EqBcjA6qA1DXnmAUu7ED4rJ4DuJ8v38iaDWDroCGrVsJP7eoHiNTWGCmSvvTcm6on6q.jpg) ![a.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EpLf79dJbxMsbwCJp44i8qXr31hr51PFxVwWPM9MT8XD6mTZ8sUdHwBsGywEW9aUU74.jpg)

> **To wrap things up, we took a quick tour of the mall’s food court. It was decorated in a very unique way; all the decorations were made of balloons, forming truly beautiful shapes and details that gave the place a festive atmosphere. Since it was almost lunchtime, we decided to grab a snack at the bakery. They serve a mini-lunch of ham and cheese there that’s absolutely delicious, and we washed it down with an ice-cold malt that hit the spot perfectly.**

> *Al concluir, dimos un pequeño recorrido por el área de comida del centro comercial. Estaba decorada de una manera muy singular; todos los adornos eran de globos, formando figuras y detalles realmente hermosos que le daban un aire festivo al lugar. Como ya estaba cerca la hora del almuerzo, decidimos merendar en la panadería. Allí preparan un minilunch de jamón y queso amarillo que es una delicia, y lo acompañamos con una malta bien fría que nos cayó de maravilla.*
![z (2).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/Eos1Nc2PFEoxj2jwDuHmaRgs4NdVshtxyrbbeYuPMAyJB3RgaJe9V3KP5tdjxxkQstu.jpg) ![z (4).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EqSWwygRtVPY68yUeU4W4EGAcDW1DMyUXxYmqYqxT3wLGppsvrpGaNjPbR2hujPa2nM.jpg) ![z (3).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EoptQrhwHWg1sCewY8aWA6rpzvtqiKevmuur3ckbmCkueg4tfB51gNKHebjzcRqVWoP.jpg) ![z (1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EpQwGF1ZBk8XcT51xf5rSA1yv9j6a4aURJT7fuTXBvCxeCm4mQ6sCC8pT1zAiQhrUr4.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-40-56.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EoCiXCTuYcRDQQjT6Xc9pmTbTRpF58VYKCuKfUd4V5BSxhqekogrKQqH5X66uX4Uuvw.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-40-55.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/23uR3C5FTkzN8jraYpd7CN9janCVseDycw54z1XAAcbQZQco41N8j78gkeo1hgfaDVKqH.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-40-48.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EoK6Nh1uqJfHXfjEz1c5VnehSFrUR6ssc9fx9yfDG3UBfCtdLCHcfU9V1UwyWrH6M8e.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-40-47.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EoGxrqH1jnvFuLBYHXsF4xHeDeeqncEc8HMEcBMs7S8s7qxuRdiCB6AaHXpYTfd4WRx.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-40-46.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EoK6E3kdyJqGZCScsrvphHHuHMCLWtUUKrEFU4xrj1QR3GJm8zeo2Q8B1RUWLN6My8W.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-40-43.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EowGdCYHi8Lg7DpsCgKApsP77PM8pHS5KNhH7MAhwYHwTL8tPxTif3JvQTGZFSvJiwU.jpg)

> **With our stomachs full, we continued our journey into town to look for the asbestos gasket. We were heading specifically to Ferremundo Mangueras, where they could either custom-make the gasket for us or sell us a piece of asbestos so we could make it ourselves. My husband preferred to buy the material and do the work at our own pace at home.**

> *Con el estómago contento, continuamos nuestro viaje hacia la ciudad para buscar la junta de amianto. Íbamos específicamente a Ferremundo Mangueras, donde podían hacer la junta a la medida o vendernos el pedazo de amianto para elaborarla nosotros mismos. Mi esposo prefirió comprar el material y hacer el trabajo con calma en casa.*
![photo_2026-04-21_23-41-13.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/23yTgyyJ9kYYkDXc2FTxRF2qop3xE2TNNtUfPsE6ekgnGsybxurWKcaj69hpB1wC8WJZw.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-41-08.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/Eos1qtHbrPRJT8reeDw9zsVwmqSwT5Wmt143R3HkhycoxhRNUnd2wueB8qNTCqXrm9X.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-41-06.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EpxrGAMzUtgAo9fDmaJPKHmnfn2EiNS35bHqnJseSCEMcMQ4iBqYaNCLq35Ro47u2rK.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-41-05.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EppLgN7op82dpwGfXPbL7KK6Ns3eJ2cGDorE79kTdH6rpjJZ7iALPDz5iCjteHjXgp5.jpg) ![a.jpg](24)

> **As we were leaving the shop, we ran into our friend Rober, who is a blacksmith. His truck was damaged, and he needed to get to a job on time where he had to install an air conditioner. Without a second thought, we loaded his tools into our truck and drove him to his destination. After dropping him off, we headed home, satisfied that we had completed all our tasks for the day.**

> *Al salir del local, nos encontramos con nuestro amigo Rober, que es herrero. Tenía su camioneta dañada y debía llegar a tiempo a un trabajo donde tenía que instalar un aire acondicionado. Sin pensarlo dos veces, cargamos sus herramientas en nuestra camioneta y lo llevamos hasta su destino. Después de dejarlo, emprendimos el regreso a casa con la satisfacción de haber cumplido todas las tareas del día.*
![photo_2026-04-21_23-48-35.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/23w2h2eVG4XDQqE8HkPYbADU1pxEZWqG84P36LKDsjV4ftsPFNr2C3pUEZbFvzJTP9TYN.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-40-19.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EptaVBmwea88oabFjpDhe1sTw5ppGBEjM58xuMtrvyfEZEyht7JDsRNNU4RiNUQcpKm.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-40-18.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EppKhuU4VskPsWyoVosRsh7aqhdQMe6bkuGxStZStM2cxFMV3aQXLF2a9sLvxbm9CAZ.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-40-14.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EqL8mVFTUxnGyfATbAYCVqtHW44qf9GPLhrsFw64hJRev1KYiAp8Y4rswnveThVSFes.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-40-08.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EqFrwhMgA8fYKvqmw1g36qcNWiAg7cpUWuBkDfGMEBinkKyMqJSjgcnWpH7XGd2nqYK.jpg) ![photo_2026-04-21_23-40-07.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EqfHME6ZhbjxES2jQs3YX9AsfptGysLZgNRDPbZyQbgiK36EQr6wbPYgQgUrAXRZ1vu.jpg)

body.body:
Гуляючи, пригадала слова з чудового віршика, якого вчила з дитиною багато років тому, і як би я не старалась, повністю відтворити його в пам'яті так і не змогла. Проте, щоразу коли прогулююсь цією ділянкою дороги, знову і знову повторюю, навіть наспівуючи - а від кладки до дороги, стежка стелиться під ноги, йду по ній я до воріт, вируша все далі в світ.

body.body:
![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/cb173015-c87a-4bb1-9d5c-2fb188eb4b4d.jpg) Well, today was much like every other day. Wake up in the morning and take the dog for his walk. Hmm... Actually wake up in the morning and get my stretches done. Chat with my wife for a bit, do a bit of scrolling through the news, have breakfast, and then look for flights to the Philippines for my parents in the fall... Then take the dog for a walk. But the first part doesn't really give me any steps. While I was walking the dog? Bright and beautiful day. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/96b7808a-d6d0-44c5-9e39-0da805c83a4e.jpg) It really was a nice morning until I saw vandalism on a poor defenseless tree in the park. ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/7690dba4-d87a-4758-9415-a1c52e21dca1.jpg) I could smell that they burnt the poor tree. That made me pretty unhappy. I mean I try not to let negative emotions in but still.... Poor tree. Other than that I will admit that I was distracted during both my morning and evening walk with the dog. Trying to figure out which hotel to stay in, which area to visit, and which flight to catch for my European trip. Looks like I'll be visiting a couple places in Spain and then Edinburgh before returning to Canada. I'm looking forward to a little exploration with my wife. Other than that? Went to the gym for a basic workout today plus some time on the treadmill to boost the steps to over 14K. I went to work and asked my boss about what was happening when he goes on vacation. Seems there will be a relief pharmacist coming in but I'll also be on more days than I really care for :( Went shopping for ingredients to make Chilli with... It's cooking now in the crock pot and should be ready for tomorrow morning. Hope that works out .. And that was pretty much my day. Well, I guess I could add that I wrote my Hive Learners post and that took me an hour or so. Plus a slothsavers post as well as an update on how my foray into saving HIVE and HELIOS and GLD is going. Honestly, slowly but surely :) Thanks for dropping by and that's my report for today :)

body.title: Crónicas de lo Absurdo #15. El Azucar. [ES/EN]
body.body:
- - -
🇪🇸 En Español
- - -

# Crónicas de lo Absurdo #15  
## El Azúcar  

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmb3NvVAsbZhj5UcmfmCRxH6q3AtGxMfsAdq9JjzRW4cj3/sarangib_sugarcane_223457_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/sugarcane-field-harvest-ox-cart-223457/)

---

Hola querida comunidad @holos-lotus, regreso una vez más para compartir una nueva entrega de esta serie:

#### Crónicas de lo Absurdo.

> Esta es una serie de crónicas sobre lo cotidiano, sobre esas escenas que se repiten tanto que dejan de parecernos extrañas. Aquí no hay exageración ni ficción forzada. El absurdo no se inventa, se observa. Son textos nacidos de la experiencia diaria, de la espera, de las normas sin sentido, de los gestos que todos conocemos y que casi nunca cuestionamos. No pretenden dar respuestas, solo detenerse un momento y mirar con atención eso que hemos aprendido a aceptar.

En esta la decimoquinta edición el tema es:

#### El azúcar.

---

Desde pequeño aprendí que mi país era una potencia azucarera.

No era una idea vaga ni un comentario aislado. Era algo que se enseñaba en la escuela, que se repetía en las clases de historia, que formaba parte del orgullo nacional. Cuba, el azúcar, la caña. Todo parecía estar conectado de forma natural.

Se hablaba de la colonia, de los ingenios, del desarrollo de una industria que había marcado la economía durante siglos. Más adelante, de los centrales, de la producción, de las exportaciones. De cómo el país había sido uno de los mayores productores de azúcar del mundo.

Para mí, aquello era simplemente una verdad.

Algo que existía.
Algo que siempre estaría ahí.

Con el tiempo, no solo lo estudié.

También lo vi.

Recorrí lugares donde la caña dominaba el paisaje. Extensiones largas, verdes, que parecían no tener fin. Durante la zafra, el movimiento era constante. Camiones cargados, trabajadores en traslado, actividad en cada punto del proceso.

Había centros de acopio.
Había vías.
Había ritmo.

Todo giraba alrededor de algo que parecía sólido.

Después llegó la universidad.

Estudié ingeniería química, y entre muchas cosas, volví a encontrarme con el azúcar. Esta vez desde el proceso, desde la técnica, desde lo que ocurre dentro de un central. En más de una ocasión estuve en prácticas, viendo de cerca lo que antes solo había imaginado.

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV43kvjtVekxa1yS8Y8Fw7KVozopiHPJaWLXRphLSKaL9/bm10777_factory_185756_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/factory-sugar-production-ethanol-185756/)

---

Y también escuché.

Recuerdo conversaciones, debates, opiniones distintas. Algunos decían que el azúcar ya no era negocio. Que los costos eran altos. Que no era sostenible.

Pero también recuerdo a un profesor que cuestionaba esa idea. Hablaba de inversiones, de estructuras ya existentes, de un sistema que no empezaba de cero. Decía que no todo era tan simple como parecía.

En aquel momento, más que entender, observaba.

Porque lo que parecía seguro comenzó a cambiar.

No de golpe.
No con un anuncio.

Simplemente empezó a desaparecer.

Primero fueron menos cañaverales.
Luego menos movimiento.

Los rieles que antes llevaban caña dejaron de tener prisa.

Los centros de acopio quedaron en silencio.

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVPYavE1Xfh224Lx3UW7NfMEEBEBeGZJq39ZVTbguxbUp/camera_man_tracks_8181296_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/tracks-rails-railroad-8181296/)

---

Los caminos seguían ahí.
Pero ya no llevaban lo mismo.

Los pueblos alrededor de los centrales, los bateyes, comenzaron a cambiar también. Lugares que antes vivían al ritmo de la zafra, poco a poco fueron perdiendo ese ritmo. No de un día para otro, sino con el paso del tiempo.

Hasta que un día, sin saber exactamente cuándo ocurrió, la realidad era otra.

Hoy, el azúcar ya no es algo que se da por hecho.

Puede faltar.

Puede comprarse.
Puede venir de fuera.

Y eso es lo que desconcierta.

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVaSDaVmdGTjXXohQMTBh9AoNU4MzRfGur8wfoxZTgRFs/422737_sugar_485055_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/sugar-trickle-spoon-cutlery-485055/)

---

Porque no se trata solo de economía.
Ni de producción.

Se trata de memoria.

De haber crecido pensando que algo era parte esencial del país… y descubrir que ya no lo es.

Antes, el azúcar estaba en todas partes.

En las casas.
En los dulces.
En los jugos.

Era tan común que no se pensaba en ella.

Hoy, puede convertirse en algo que se mide.

Que se calcula.

Que se dosifica.

Y en ocasiones, incluso, que se sustituye.

El absurdo no está en que las cosas cambien.

Eso es natural.

El absurdo está en la distancia entre lo que fuimos y lo que somos.

En haber tenido tanto…
y necesitarlo ahora.

Porque cuando un país que fue símbolo de algo deja de tenerlo, no pierde solo un producto.

Pierde una parte de su historia cotidiana.

Y entonces uno entiende que el problema no es el azúcar.

Es lo que representa.

---

Hasta aqui esta decimoquinta crónica Gracias por leer y espero comentarios al respecto. Las imágenes son de pixabay y utilicé el traductor de Google para la versión en inglés.

# Chronicles of the Absurd #15  
## Sugar  

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmb3NvVAsbZhj5UcmfmCRxH6q3AtGxMfsAdq9JjzRW4cj3/sarangib_sugarcane_223457_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/sugarcane-field-harvest-ox-cart-223457/)

---

Hello dear @holos-lotus community, I come once again to share a new entry in this series:

#### Chronicles of the Absurd.

> This is a series of chronicles about everyday life, about those scenes that repeat themselves so often that they stop seeming strange to us. Here there is no exaggeration or forced fiction. The absurd is not invented, it is observed. These are texts born from daily experience, from waiting, from meaningless rules, from gestures we all know and almost never question. They do not seek to give answers, only to stop for a moment and look carefully at what we have learned to accept.

In this fifteenth edition the theme is:

#### Sugar.

---

Since I was a child, I learned that my country was a sugar powerhouse.

It wasn’t a vague idea or a random comment. It was something taught in school, repeated in history lessons, part of a national identity. Cuba, sugar, sugarcane. Everything seemed naturally connected.

We learned about the colonial period, the plantations, the development of an industry that shaped the economy for centuries. Later, about mills, production, exports. About how the country became one of the largest sugar producers in the world.

To me, it was simply a fact.

Something that existed.
Something that would always be there.

Over time, I didn’t just study it.

I saw it.

I traveled through places where sugarcane dominated the landscape. Long green fields that seemed endless. During harvest season, everything moved. Trucks loaded with cane, workers being transported, activity at every stage.

There were collection centers.
There were railways.
There was rhythm.

Everything revolved around something that felt permanent.

Then came university.

I studied chemical engineering, and once again, sugar appeared—this time from a technical perspective. I saw the process, the inside of a mill, the transformation that once had been abstract.

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmV43kvjtVekxa1yS8Y8Fw7KVozopiHPJaWLXRphLSKaL9/bm10777_factory_185756_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/factory-sugar-production-ethanol-185756/)

---

And I listened.

There were discussions, debates, different opinions. Some said sugar was no longer profitable. That costs were too high. That it didn’t make sense anymore.

But I also remember a professor who questioned that idea. He spoke about existing infrastructure, about investments already made, about systems that didn’t start from zero. He suggested things were more complex than they seemed.

At that time, I didn’t fully understand.

I just observed.

Because what once seemed stable began to change.

Not suddenly.
Not with a clear announcement.

It simply started to fade.

Fewer fields.
Less movement.

The rails that once carried cane no longer seemed in a hurry.

Collection centers fell silent.

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVPYavE1Xfh224Lx3UW7NfMEEBEBeGZJq39ZVTbguxbUp/camera_man_tracks_8181296_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/tracks-rails-railroad-8181296/)

---

The roads were still there.
But they no longer carried the same purpose.

The small towns around the mills began to change too. Places that once lived by the rhythm of harvest slowly lost that rhythm. Not overnight, but gradually.

Until one day, without knowing exactly when it happened, reality was different.

Today, sugar is no longer something taken for granted.

It can be missing.

It can be bought.
It can come from elsewhere.

And that is what feels strange.

---

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVaSDaVmdGTjXXohQMTBh9AoNU4MzRfGur8wfoxZTgRFs/422737_sugar_485055_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/sugar-trickle-spoon-cutlery-485055/)

---

Because it’s not just about economics.

Or production.

It’s about memory.

About growing up believing something was an essential part of your country… and realizing it no longer is.

Before, sugar was everywhere.

In homes.
In desserts.
In drinks.

It was so common that no one thought about it.

Today, it becomes something measured.

Calculated.

Used carefully.

And sometimes, replaced.

The absurd is not that things change.

That is natural.

The absurd lies in the distance between what we were and what we are.

In having had so much…
and needing it now.

Because when a country that was once defined by something no longer has it, it doesn’t just lose a product.

It loses a piece of its everyday history.

And then you understand that the problem is not sugar.

It’s what it represents.

---

This is the end of this fifteenth chronicle. Thank you for reading, and I look forward to your comments. The images are from Pixabay and I used Google Translate for the English version.

---

body.title: My nights without electricity in Venezuela(eng-spn)
body.body:
Early this morning, I got my children ready for school, a routine I follow daily. My daughter to her school, my son to his daycare, and I to my job teaching math, just a few classrooms away from my children's school.

When I arrived, there was no electricity, so I had to teach in the sweltering heat. It was a typical morning without power.

Today, my workday was supposed to end at 2 pm. After leaving the school, I went to buy some things for dinner and the children's snacks.

I got home with my children around 5 pm. I was tired, so I made a snack, we ate, and just as I was about to rest, **whoosh** the power went out. I couldn't rest; I immediately had to take advantage of the little natural light to cook dinner and get tomorrow's clothes ready because our electricity rationing lasts six hours.

![1000000855.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yusmelys/EoCZyohxNHLtqDMojk35xF7mbpXmazZvUSuSQ74dheUjELbYd4yCo5fXtMyrD5i3py6.jpg)

And here I was, waiting for the light to arrive, taking pictures of the moon to share on #hSnaps, when suddenly a cat appeared on the roof of my neighbor's house, and so I took the opportunity to take these nighttime photos.


And here I was, waiting for the light to arrive, taking pictures of the moon to share on #hSnaps, when suddenly a cat appeared on the roof of my neighbor's house, and so I took advantage of the situation to take these nighttime photos. ![1000000853.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yusmelys/EnymeWnRRSXedaPniUm51cgaeRtfyympQBV6ZkJUxPsWPUSUAz6iG1i7Kqd8J4bwcrq.jpg)

The moon was beautiful with three bright lights very close to it. I'm curious what those three little lights near the moon are. I'll investigate; perhaps some AI knows what those little lights are.


![1000000850.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yusmelys/EnymXPd2e5qqRyBRMdT3Aw7boj9FucxbaGcoV4KrdBAcy2ZxdP7ax4pp7Zt6joQYaxJ.jpg)

I'm finishing this post and the electricity still hasn't come back on. It's been 5 hours. How sad my country is in total darkness. But at least I managed to take these dark photos of a cat on the roof.

![1000000859.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yusmelys/EoGpfYhcVSrB2mDbzcFKJkFxCDnbuJ26mtWPjXyzjdBMY9fCJfGtWunmeQhmXxcFbvf.jpg)

![1000000857.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yusmelys/EobyHAAgDfTpG2VL2VFW48Bf3aMdsAc9yTSYFtbBBCBzen8nbKVauCTdkDVsdG5SyzM.jpg)

It's a pleasure to share this beautiful story with you. Even without electricity, we must appreciate the good and beautiful aspects of life.

----

*Images from my gallery
I used Google Translate*





![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yusmelys/Eo4EPouCcivt2mNuqUdcx9P9vhLjLiDuRKtmi1qHijyrpikY3PBMwFc2xqgzxacZzKJ.png)

Desde temprano prepare a mis hijos para su escuela, una rutina que hago diariamente. La niña a su escuela, el niño a su guardería, yo a mi trabajo dando clases de matemáticas muy cerca del colegio de mis hijos a unos cuantos salones de distancia. 

Al llegar no había electricidad, así que correspondia dar clases con las fuertes temperaturas. Fue una mañana normal sin el servicio eléctrico. 

Hoy tocaba terminar la jornada laboral a las 2pm, al retirarme de la institución fui a comprar algunas cosas para la cena y la merienda de los niños. 

Llegue a casa con mis hijos casi a las 5pm, estaba cansada, así que preparé una merienda, comimos y cuando iba a descansar **zaaass** se fue la electricidad, no pude descansar, inmediatamente había que aprovechar lo poco de luz natural para cocinar la cena, arreglar la ropa de mañana porque nuestro racionamiento eléctrico dura 6 horas. 


![1000000855.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yusmelys/EoCZyohxNHLtqDMojk35xF7mbpXmazZvUSuSQ74dheUjELbYd4yCo5fXtMyrD5i3py6.jpg)


Y aquí estaba esperando que llegara la luz, tomándole fotos a la luna para compartirla en #hSnaps, cuando de repente apareció un gato en el techo de la casa de la vecina y asi aproveché para tomar estas fotos nocturnas. 

![1000000853.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yusmelys/EnymeWnRRSXedaPniUm51cgaeRtfyympQBV6ZkJUxPsWPUSUAz6iG1i7Kqd8J4bwcrq.jpg)

La luna estaba hermosa con tres luceros muy cerca de ella, me causa curiosidad que serán esas tres lucesitas cerca de la luna. Investigaré, tal vez alguna IA sepa que son esas lucesitas. 


![1000000850.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yusmelys/EnymXPd2e5qqRyBRMdT3Aw7boj9FucxbaGcoV4KrdBAcy2ZxdP7ax4pp7Zt6joQYaxJ.jpg)


Termino este post y todavía la electricidad no llegado, 5 horas, que triste mi país en una oscuridad total. Pero por lo menos tomé estas oscuras fotos de un gato en el techo.


![1000000859.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yusmelys/EoGpfYhcVSrB2mDbzcFKJkFxCDnbuJ26mtWPjXyzjdBMY9fCJfGtWunmeQhmXxcFbvf.jpg)


![1000000857.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yusmelys/EobyHAAgDfTpG2VL2VFW48Bf3aMdsAc9yTSYFtbBBCBzen8nbKVauCTdkDVsdG5SyzM.jpg)

Un placer compartir esta hermosa historia con ustedes, aunque no tengamos electricidad hay que ver lo bueno y hermoso de la vida.

body.title: Deep Cover (2025) || Movie Review
body.body:
![1000104299.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/23wX3FCynfqacyiGUjndhaPpZ3Wkh13wTxfZZbmMacFE5W617cxLvT6ovy1AQMMC6jBYB.jpg)
I don't mind watching movies that deliver strong messages and life lessons but even better, I love to relax with those ones made purely for entertainment. **Deep Cover (2025)** is one of such entertaining movies and after watching, I was neither impressed nor disappointed. Considering the cast selection, I expected it would be impressive or a blockbuster. *Deep Cover* is a British action comedy directed by Tom Kingsley and written by Derek Connolly, Colin Trevorrow, Ben Ashenden and Alexander Owen. It stars Bryce Dallas Howard as Kat, Orlando Bloom as Marlon, Nick Mohammed as Hugh and Paddy Considine, Ian McShane, Sean Bean and others as supporting characters. ![1000104311.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/23zGa8Njbc2aEXWBKCwWaPDx1Sjch88wcWYNfuM74DwQDX2afNjE9QCjuBe8sM113E1zd.jpg) ![1000104312.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/Eq7MLp3iyEWUvfLmWP1D4E2ZvWuR9wBcY6nzJLjRUGeKdKctCzH1zgaLif7stZrBMgk.jpg) Set in London, the first scene introduces Marlon, a washed-up actor (he embodies his character deeply with dramatic monologues) looking for a job but keeps getting rejected. Then there's Kat, a tutor of improv class, a job she does to make ends meet while all her friends are established. Marlon is one of her students. ![1000104297.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/23tvAUypv8d38z52fk5V8ePPNYJ3PJx72RuCcetuU6MaWZ13QtFRbLTY4oninFLnK14zG.jpg) ![1000104310.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/23wqXt2aF4PfGvhquUubF4vcVAgonkuCGP6sJNixPNVrs8c6DbE8cp4j6XRBL4bY7JoFe.jpg) There's also Hugh, a lonely and insecure technical support worker at a brokerage where his colleagues don't socialise with him because he says inappropriate things. He stumbles on Kat’s tutor local ads and decides to join the class. ![1000104306.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/Eoni5APxxsqxLGCrnhxPR1zJFcbH6Db4n7YVEhFAUoizLco2M4oU9azo7axbEXC9QvC.jpg) ![1000104307.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/EobzoqbYUgTmLuE1aD4rd5nq23WZmmgpFUGRvkox89258PjgGYkvfVavjwPAKBgesHN.jpg) ![1000104305.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/244eAS2g6WbmJtF56PPeLN7EaZdutAgfF3wPgrmnrbt8WZ1nepZFtjDsw36BsFgwAuVmT.jpg) One night, DS Graham Billings of the Metropolitan Police (Sean Bean) approaches Kat in class and tells her about a police program police where improv actors are employed do light undercover job for a few pounds. Kat agrees to this deal and tells Marlon and Hugh to join her. Together they become a trio involved in a low-level undercover sting operation to expose a local store associated with illicit cigarette trades. Then they discover a much larger operation. Can this inexperienced trio take down this larger operation? #### My Review And Rating. This movie turned out fast-paced and a bit funny. It's not one to be taken seriously. Though I wish the producers took their time to make this movie properly. It would have been a blast. The plot is a unique one - employing students of improv classes to infiltrate drug organisations. This is not a storyline I see often in movies so its fresh in my opinion. I wish the writers and director had put it in more effort to explore this plot differently and give it more substance. The ending is predictable hence my disappointment. The cast’s performance is not bad. Its been a while since I've seen Orlando Bloom in movies. His role in this one appears silly and a bit funny. As the movie progresses, he evolves and becomes smarter. On the other hand, Bryce Dallas Howard is a fine actress and she really embodied the role of class tutor and leader of the trio in the undercover job. Hugh is the third person in the group but I didn't find him convincing as the humor of the movie. Their chemistry as a trio undercover agents is unbalanced which dimmed the movie for me. Metcalfe (Ian McShane) is a formidable antagonist as a druglord. He brings tension, suspense and some danger to the movie, upping the stakes a bit. I enjoyed his performance. He's one of the good old actors I know of. The cinematography is fine. The visuals are clear and impressive. The cast’s costumes are not bad but I take offence at Orlando Bloom’s wig. It made him look weird and unlike him. Rating this movie, I will give it 6 stars out of 10. The plot is a fine one but the storytelling is not as impressive as I expected. The writers and director could do better. The acting makes this movie bearable solely for entertainment. https://youtu.be/1x--MaHsbEc?si=GZT1W1o7ktocrkno ![3yZiouw5jgtrj8RZntzpYvPkttnUNCNB3bKsugcDmKrZysEhsVCu7HmxWG7sYd9c3PJiWe24wRnpAB7HXq2WMvHX9AyxjgRuTY38KWSsv8...GFDdhx4UzPxqzjjpVMXNYgRDyspwo7pFw2RpyHZvde1tK7QLmYqnXBk9hDVg1dAooe2nLquVnXKjzS2uR5yQNqx1V5qutNgmqpFfKYLpS93ajRQosgFNPk3e1s.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/esther-emmanuel/23t7BFjADUCGjsLPt1YzFafTb9BeZ3Err5bNPwTi6RYNWED9TfZAhqAcZ8JCb2rGLLeT6.gif) *All images above are from the movie screenshots* *[Poster image source](https://pics.filmaffinity.com/Deep_Cover-582599206-large.jpg)* *Thank you for visiting and supporting my blog* 🤗

body.title: Compute! (March 1989)
body.body:
>
Cover of the March 1989 issue of Compute!
Compute! was a popular computer magazine for home computer users in the 1980s. It covered various popular home computer systems and had spinoffs dedicated to particular systems. The most popular of those was probably Compute!'s Gazette which covered Commodore's 8-bit computers. The March 1989 issue of Compute! includes:

Features

  • Coming Together - A guide to getting your computer to talk to and share information with other computers. This article includes info for MS-DOS, the Commodore 64/128, Apple II, Amiga, Macintosh, and Atari ST.

  • Warning: Games Under Construction - A look at game construction sets including Arcade Game Construction Kit (Apple II, Commodore 64), Wargame Construction Set (Atari 8-bit, Atari ST, Commodore 64, DOS), Adventure Construction Set (Apple II, Amiga, Commodore 64, DOS), World Builder (Macintosh), and Pinball Construction Set (Apple II, Atari 8-bit, Commodore 64, DOS, Macintosh).

  • Buyer's Guide Arcade Games - This buyer's guide covers a variety of games including aargh! (Amiga), Alcon (Commodore 64), Alien Mind (Apple IIGS), Amegas (Amiga), Arkanoid (Amiga), Awesome Arcade Action Pack (Amiga), Better Dead Than Alien (Amiga), Bubble Bobble (Commodore 64), Contra (Amiga, Commodore 64, DOS), Fire and Forget (Amiga, Atari ST, DOS), Gauntlet (Amiga, Atari, Atari ST, Commodore 64), Ikari Warriors (Apple II, DOS), Marble Madness (Amiga, Apple II, Atari ST, Commodore 64, DOS), Jackal (Amiga, Commodore 64, DOS), Rampage (Apple II, Commodore 64, DOS, Apple IIGS), Rush 'N Attack (Amiga, Commodore 64, DOS), Technocop (Amiga, Apple II, Atari ST, Commodore 64, DOS), and many more.

>
Table of contents from the March 1989 issue of Compute!

Reviews

  • Fast Looks - Previews of Rebus Writer (Apple II) and Police Quest (Apple IIgs, Atari ST, DOS).

  • Tandy 1000 SL - Tandy's latest computer includes an 8 MHz 8086 CPU, 384K of RAM, and more for $899.

  • Final Assault - A mountaineering game from Epyx for the Amiga, Apple IIGS, Atari ST, Commodore 64, and DOS.

  • Slide Shop - Software for creating presentations (Apple II, DOS).

  • Appleworks GS - A new version of Apple's integrated software package for the GS.

  • Times of Lore - An RPG for the Apple II, Commodore 64 and DOS from the makers of the Ultima series.

  • Solitaire Royale - A collection of solitaire games for the Amiga, DOS, and Macintosh.

  • The Perfect Career - Software that is supposed to help you find the career that is perfect for you (Amiga, DOS, Macintosh).

  • Jack Nicklaus' Greatest 18 Holes of Major Championship Golf - The most popular golf game of its time for the Amiga, Apple IIGS, Commodore 64, and DOS.

  • AlphaWorks - An integrated software package for DOS.

  • Z88 - A portable computer that reminds me of the TRS-80 Model 100 though this one is not PC compatible.

>
Table of Contents from the March 1989 issue of Compute! (continued)

Columns

  • Editorial License - A look at celebrities that try to sell you computers including William Shatner (Commodore PET), Isaac Asimov (TRS-80), Alan Alda (Atar), the crew of MASH (IBM PS/2), and others plus recommendations for future salespeople.

  • News & Notes - Aline, an online chat service; 688 Attack Sub from Electronic Arts; CheckFree check writing software; and more.

  • Gameplay - Orson Scott Card writes about game designers vs. programmers.

  • Impact - The threat of computer viruses in computer networks.

  • Discoveries - Improving your child's reading skill with computers.

  • Levitations -
  • Letters - Letters from readers about NeXT's magnesium cases, Multiplan and Sky Travel for the Commodore 64, and more.

  • New Products! - Street Cat from U.S. Gold (Commodore 64, DOS, Amiga), the Commodore PC40-III, Anchor 2400TLT modem for Toshiba laptops, F-14 Tomcat from Activision for the Commodore 64, and more.

Compute! Specific

  • MS-DOS - Upgrading PC RAM and understanding the difference between conventional RAM and the various versions of extended and expanded memory.

  • 64 & 128 - More GEOS applications and game releases for the Commodore 64.

  • Apple II - Modem Wars, AppleWorks GS, and more.

  • Amiga - Commodore expects to sell 300,000 Amigas during the last quarter of 1988 plus speculation on the upcoming Amiga 3000.

  • Macintosh - Software for NeXT and Macintosh.

  • Atari ST - Starglider II, Spectre 128 Macintosh emulator, and more.

body.body:

<center>
![2Po080dWeWmbYeEE_mmexport1773825792380.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/jaychoumjs/images/2Po080dWeWmbYeEE_mmexport1773825792380/2Po080dWeWmbYeEE_mmexport1773825792380.webp)
![4UDmDvzpOz47byfe_wx_camera_1774065781317.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/jaychoumjs/images/4UDmDvzpOz47byfe_wx_camera_1774065781317/4UDmDvzpOz47byfe_wx_camera_1774065781317.webp)
![iDYHwsGfPKAI8enS_IMG20260324084411.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/jaychoumjs/images/iDYHwsGfPKAI8enS_IMG20260324084411/iDYHwsGfPKAI8enS_IMG20260324084411.webp)
![9oJKRfmG0EXayvmf_Screenshot_2026-03-23-20-25-03-52_e39d2c7de19156b0683cd93e8735f348.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/jaychoumjs/images/9oJKRfmG0EXayvmf_Screenshot_2026-03-23-20-25-03-52_e39d2c7de19156b0683cd93e8735f348/9oJKRfmG0EXayvmf_Screenshot_2026-03-23-20-25-03-52_e39d2c7de19156b0683cd93e8735f348.webp)
</center>
</liketuimages>

上周末，本来打算好好打场篮球然后再补上一觉，但是呢，计划不如变化，虽然事与愿违，但是也过得足够充实。
朋友叫我去玩，于是周六我们去郊区公园放风筝，我们几个人都在各自风筝上写上彼此的名字，然后趁着一股特别大的风劲，把风筝放在了天上，不同类型不同样式的风筝在天上飘着感觉挺震撼的，当然本来就是这方面的小白，所以第1次尝试还是有点困难的，不过后来朋友教着教着我就可以把风筝自然的放在天上，挺喜欢放风筝的感觉，风筝在天上自由飞翔
下午老师又布置了一些手绘的机械制图作业，只能绞尽脑汁的的拿着那个装配体去图书馆画，这一画就不知道时间为何物，简直过得飞快，2点到的图书馆，回来的时候已经9点了，中间就吃了一次饭，上了一两次厕所，然后一直埋头于作业中，五六个小时高精度集中的画，最后才完成，真的是工作量太大了
晚上打了一会儿游戏，然后开始一个长为一世纪的睡眠，因为这学期的课太多了，每天都是早八，真的是心有余而力不足，所以补觉对我来说是一个续命的好方法，从晚上11点开始睡，睡到了第2天早上的9点多，真的是自然醒了，好久没有这么惬意的睡过觉了，起床洗了个脸，然后吃了个早饭，就去外面骑车了，我们学校的花和树都开的差不多了，沿途欣赏着学校里的景色，当时入学的时候太忙了，都没有好好的看看，现在这么一看，确实挺不错，让人心情更上1层楼，中午吃了个饭，下午就和朋友又去打球了，然后周天下午是有晚自习的，打完球之后就去上晚自习了，周末就这么快就完了！

---

body.body:
>






#### Saludos amigos bienvenidos a mi blog 🌟

 

</center>

<div class=\

> Siempre he mirado a el mar con respeto siempre digo que es otro mundo, cuando estaba pequeña me encantaba cuando mis padres me llevaban a la playa y lo que más me gustaba era saltar las olas, habían olas que lograban revolcarme e iba a parar hasta la orilla toda llena de arena y por supuesto había tomado mucha agua con sal que se hace tan amarga que logra meterse hasta por la nariz, es una sensación muy incomoda y amarga.

> Estuve en natación y esto me da más seguridad al momento de saltar esas olas y que además si venia por debajo ese arrastre de agua no me iría pues sabia nadar, pero pasar las olas por debajo cuando eran muy grandes era algo que me encantaba, pues habia aprendido a pasarlas sumergiendome y ellas pasaban por encima de mi. Al leer esta iniciativa de la semana me atrapó, pues la vida es como surfear la ola o saltar la ola, hay días que son calmados, suaves, tranquilos, que no dan ningún problema, de hecho esos días nos dejan felicidad, tranquilidad y alegrías o simplemente pasamos ese día, son días buenos de esos que quisiéramos tener siempre pues nos dejan cosas buenas o simplemente pasamos el día.

> Hay días donde las olas no son tan fuertes ni bajas, sino medianas, no son días tan buenos como otros, pero tampoco tan malos, estos días tienen sus complicaciones, pero podemos salir de ella sin mucho esfuerzo, saltamos La ola y pasamos a otro nuevo día, puede que estos días donde la ola sea mediana pueda durar uno, dos, quizás tres días, puede que sean un poco difíciles, sin embargo, hemos aprendido a saltar esa ola y seguimos adelante. Pero hay días que vienen olas del tamaño de un tsunami y esta ola si nos golpea, nos arrastra contra el piso, nos arrastra hasta la orilla o quizas quiera llevarnos a lo profundo, y son esos días que hemos pasado por circunstancias que nadie quisiera pasar, me ha tocado pasar esas olas y aprender hacer resilente, pues en esa ola puede que se lleve parte de nosotros, sin saber cuando volver a levantarnos o si estaremos de pie pronto, estos días que me han tocado vivir es como si estuviéramos dentro de la ola y en total oscuridad, nos ahogamos y no sabemos como salir de allí.

>



Pero en esa ola uno aprende a salir adelante, a hacerse fuerte, a salir adelante, a levantarse nuevamente, pocos se quedan allí en la ola y se ahogan, pero muchos salen adelante y aprenden, pues en la vida esas olas vienen como enseñanzas, aunque sean fuertes siempre nos van a dejar algo que más adelante en nuestro andar lo vamos a necesitar. Gracias a @angelica7 por esta iniciativa de la semana,

When I was little, I loved it when my parents took me to the beach, and what I liked most was jumping over the waves. There were waves that would knock me over, and I’d end up on the shore covered in sand. And of course, I’d swallowed a lot of saltwater—it’s so bitter that it even gets up your nose. It’s a very uncomfortable and bitter sensation. > >

> > >I used to swim, and that gave me more confidence when jumping over those waves; plus, if a undertow came from below, it wouldn’t sweep me away because I knew how to swim. But passing under the waves when they were really big was something I loved, because I’d learned to get under them by diving in, and they’d roll right over me. > >When I read this week’s initiative, it really resonated with me, because life is like surfing a wave or jumping over a wave. There are days that are calm, gentle, and peaceful—days that present no problems. In fact, those days leave us feeling happy, at peace, and joyful, or we simply get through the day. They’re the kind of good days we’d like to have all the time because they leave us with good things, or we just get through the day. > >

> > >There are days when the waves aren’t too strong or too weak, but just moderate. They aren’t as good as other days, but they aren’t that bad either. These days have their challenges, but we can get through them without much effort. We ride out the wave and move on to a new day. These days with moderate waves might last one, two, or maybe three days; they might be a little difficult, however, we’ve learned to ride that wave and keep moving forward. > >But there are days when waves the size of a tsunami come, and if this wave hits us, it knocks us down, drags us to the shore, or maybe tries to pull us into the deep. Those are the days when we’ve gone through circumstances no one would want to face. I’ve had to ride those waves and learn to be resilient, because that wave might take a part of us away, without knowing when we’ll get back up or if we’ll be on our feet again soon. These days I’ve had to live through feel as if we’re inside the wave and in total darkness; we’re drowning and don’t know how to get out of there. > >

> > >Pero en esa ola uno aprende a salir adelante, a hacerse fuerte, a salir adelante, a levantarse nuevamente, pocos se quedan allí en la ola y se ahogan, pero muchos salen adelante y aprenden, pues en la vida esas olas vienen como enseñanzas, aunque sean fuertes siempre nos van a dejar algo que más adelante en nuestro andar lo vamos a necesitar. links.title: Calm footsteps of gray clouds in the lush green expanse of rice fields
links.body:
Among the rows of rice that stood neatly like time keepers, a man stepped slowly on the path that cut through the rice fields. The sky hung gray clouds, as if holding back the rain so as not to disturb the tranquility of that afternoon. With his outstretched hand holding the camera, he captured simple moments that were never truly ordinary, the vast greenery, the whispering wind, and the land that faithfully gave life.

On the right side, young rice waves gently, while on the left side the grains that are starting to turn yellow look ripe, like two chapters in the same story. The man smiled faintly, raised his thumb, as if to say that everything was fine. There is no hustle and bustle of the city, only the sound of leaves touching each other, and footsteps blending into the earth.

In the silence of nature, he found something that was often lost elsewhere, a sense of contentment. In the midst of endless green expanses, he realized that peace is not a distant goal, but is present in every step taken with a calm heart.

links.title: How we were Successfully able to preserve Cassava Plants for this year planting
links.body:
# Hello Hive 



![1000196252.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23xAXcXrPUq97r992Qy99JC2bkjb1VHfr9DJZw3bNQH2Ezh9M2FUbkhExMzeAfbADuQ9e.jpg)


A  happy new day to us all, I hope that we all had a peaceful night rest with some good health and strength that will carry us through a new day. The weather condition here has improved greatly as the harsh and extremely hot weather has been replaced by cooler temperatures ever since  the rains began to fall.
The crops in the fields are now feeling better and getting revived 


![1000196206.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23tmNALqDWiCieisRfBbDLFdRwR1MgXHq67GcfFfraSuqSTgd9NnJcDTPxCRRtRXRfvAw.jpg)


The success of every year farming season depends also on the type and quality of see of seeds we are able to preserve for planting along side other factors . Alot often happens during the dry seasons and for biannual crops like cassava we have to watch out for the plants so longs as they remain in the fields during the dry season
 

![1000196200.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/243Lvi4RPv5EFc43EDWZ6L5ga35U9dgpHoHnBwQhCES6DFjiPA1Aq5T8KxPVmacXJnFAS.jpg)

![1000196210.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/242Y1PqLLPLpfNdXVDSqa1fk6gdrLKpPzeE8vwbGMb89yhx66hSA1ZpzCKsMkQQwvaChX.jpg)


For this particular cassava that have grown to large extent before the raining seasons came, they were able to survive on their own. And have now picked up their growth phase  from where they have earlier stopped. This is the reason that you can see them all green and looking fresh almost as soon as the rain began



![1000196209.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23vi1YPcq92AYRhAaTHSzmHtF8ckcwhmbRRX43GGbqWn6AfcQNTiKua79UKWy8m3JhHzk.jpg)


For cassava in this other location, some witnessed extreme dryness and forest fires penetrated some of the farm.Due to the fact that these ones produce quality tubers if cassava, we decided to employ a trick to protect this specie of the plant for this year's planting.

After the fire engulf the farm,  we plucked out a few of the trees as the trees are what is often planted as the cassava seeds. 

![1000196206.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23tmNALqDWiCieisRfBbDLFdRwR1MgXHq67GcfFfraSuqSTgd9NnJcDTPxCRRtRXRfvAw.jpg)
We kept them under a tree for cooler temperatures and have continued to water those stems till date l.

Look here they are now very much viable and ready for planting

links.title: I simply do not care about the UFO talk going on now
links.body:
Is the media bored and needs more controversy outside of simply focusing on Trump all the time?  Are they unhappy that MTG stopped being relevant.  Have the run out of time to spend on crazy Mark Ruffalo and Robert DeNiro?  Has Rosie O'donnel just accepted the fact that she is irrelevant these days no matter what European country she flees to?   

The news is at an all time ridiculous these days, at least in my lifetime, and I miss the days of getting the paper in the morning in New Bern, North Carolina where they only had a few actual journalists on staff and got most of their national and international stories by I guess paying a fee to much larger big-city publications.   Instead of having thousands of stories per minute to pick through, we had 20 pages that covered all manner of things and of course the stock page.   

Can you imagine that there was a time when people checked stock prices just ONCE a day?  

The amount of information that we have access to these days is just too overwhelming and I think it was wise for me to just bow out.  I no longer really have any idea what is going on in the world but every now and then I take a peek when I have done all really useful things in my life already.   one thing that pops up every now and then are these stories about extra-terrestrial life and how the government has proof of it.

<center> https://img.freepik.com/free-vector/cute-alien-riding-ufo-space-cartoon-vector-icon-illustration-science-technology-icon-isolated_138676-8224.jpg?semt=ais_hybrid&w=740&q=80
[src](https://img.freepik.com/free-vector/cute-alien-riding-ufo-space-cartoon-vector-icon-illustration-science-technology-icon-isolated_138676-8224.jpg?semt=ais_hybrid&w=740&q=80)</center>

people that spend entirely too much of their lives being concerned about politics will say things like \

or something similar to that which they were taught to say like good little parrots by whatever their social media of choice is.  

For me, I think I have been so traumatized by the constant bombardment of propaganda that these claims of UFO's could be 100% true and I still wouldn't care.  

<center> https://static01.nyt.com/images/2020/07/28/us/28xp-UFO/28xp-UFO-superJumbo.jpg
[src](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2020/07/28/us/28xp-UFO/28xp-UFO-superJumbo.jpg)</center>

Apparently there is video and all sorts of things that have been declassified by the CIA or Navy or whoever, and honestly, I think that a majority of people have gotten the news cycle beatdown for so long that they could have a news conference with an actual alien and not very many people would care.

I can't be the only person out there that has just been beaten into submission by the overzealous people involved in the news and especially anything related to politics.  Hell, even sports pundits annoy me these days because instead of just watching a game and having someone really knowledgeable like John Madden draw on the screen and explain plays we now have a roundtable for several hours that go through every minute detail of everything to the point where I no longer care about sports anymore.  Don't get me started on the fact that we now apparently have to have a certain number of women authoritative experts on the panel as well even though they have never played the sport and would get broken into pieces if they ever tried.

The news charlatans have turned me off to even attempting to stay up to speed on what is going on in the world and while that might make me uninformed I don't believe that the people who \

every day are any better informed than I am.  The psychologists have figured out what works on people and I'll be damned if there are basically zero free thinkers out there anymore, it's just people repeating what they heard on whatever show they already agree with.  Conservatives annoy me just as much as liberals on this even though I am far more conservative than I am liberal. 

Are UFO's real?  I am one of those people that believes there absolutely must be life on other planets given the infinite nature of space.  It is likely so unimaginably far away from us that we are never going to meet one another though.  

So the UFO business can kiss my ass just like the never-ending stuff about all the politicians and military \
If you need me I'll be at my job doing Sudoku in my spare time and also working on my garden.  It's spring after all.

title.title: Thrash (2026) Review
title.body:
/>

To some extent, yes, but I noticed some flaws too. Above all, however, the flood’s originality should be applauded. What do I mean?

Before deciding to watch this movie, I saw a BTS clip posted by Netflix on Facebook showing how the flood scenes were shot, and I couldn’t imagine how they managed to create a real flood in such a large environment. That was superb.

The plot is good. The government foresaw that a heavy flood was coming and warned everyone to vacate the town. Many people heard and obeyed, while some took it as a mere warning, believing there was no way a flood could come and swallow two-story buildings or break through well-reinforced structures. But, just like in a play, the flood came, swallowing houses and even breaking through the best reinforced buildings. Not only that, the flood came with sharks.

The few and stubborn people left in the city were attacked by both the flood and the sharks. Then comes Lisa, a heavily pregnant woman who got stuck on the road when her car was trapped by a tree branch in the midst of the flood. I feared she was going to die on the spot because of her physical state of health . The water rose to her head, and she struggled to survive. The first set of guys who came to rescue her were killed by the sharks with no mercy.

Then Dakota, who saw everything from the top floor of the building she was, decided to go rescue her and that was very brave but hey, I couldn't just grab how she got to pull the pregnant woman to the top floor. I questioned the lapse in the movie there.

The shark effects aren’t bad compared to many other movies I’ve seen, where the CGI(computerised effect) was too obvious.  
But, the sharks were not properly directed in their attacks. Fgs! The sharks are angry and hungry and there's no way they'll see a prey and won't attack. I understand that the producers wanted to save lives and didn’t want the sharks to kill everyone, but there were scenes where the sharks had clear and good opportunities to strike, yet they just moved around the people.

The actors did excellently well, and I think the casting was spot on. Dakota is the standout character for me. She was emotionally shaken throughout due to the death of her mom which happened a few months before the outbreak, but her bravery truly stood out.

I’ll rate the movie 6/10.

Thanks for reading.

title.title: All Rap
title.body:
I'm a known listener of rap and hip-hop, everyone who knows me knows that.
Yet my musical library is quite a concept as when I'm listening to music, I tend to listen to different albums of different genres or different songs of different genres or styles.
Well yesterday, I did something entirely different, just off the rip, on a whim.
I listened to six hours of music and five hours of rap.
***
## All Rap

![1003447956.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/seki1/23wM51uMQe6ZtEbtaDWQeS6KTj97SAxmvcnvFiN2jcd2HPEnKEFVHtaHohpXGHQHFaT8n.png)

***
Rap music isn't a genre for everyone.
Most people think of it as violent and loud, or the words being too fast to hear and some even go as far as saying that they're talking rubbish (because they can't hear or comprehend the words.)
Thus, because the songs I'm about to list are tunes I want everyone to actually understand. I'll urge you to watch this video about rap.
https://youtu.be/4gqhYY2AfyI?si=ZmQJg1TKlj2jHV4q
It talks about the hidden meanings in my favorite album and favorite song from Kendrick Lamar.
***
Sadly, these songs I'm about to show aren't from Kendrick Lamar, I think you all have had enough of that.

Regardless, we see some new songs but traces of the old artists.
***
### Lie To Me ~ Earthgang 
***
Earthgang is part of J. Cole's agency, Dreamville and that kind of environment is one where different sounds, flows and ideas collude to bring up musical masterpieces.
In this song, Earthgang talks about the lies about the celebrities gimmick, lies about relationships and lies about life.
It was unexpected for me to hear and tune is one you wouldn't easily forget.
https://youtu.be/bKmZfW3jCBs?si=Y4kU6vatVu_z9kv6
***
### Baguetti ~ Smino ft Jid 
***
Now this song is one from two talented writers who are on the same mind place and they're just having fun.
Jid and Smino talk about their past relationships and their struggles now looking small as they're big fishes in the rap industry.
The Baguetti being a French bread and a type of diamond was used in the song.

https://youtu.be/-IdbbH_OWhc?si=aHH2qVP0pjJ7QxGf
***
### Saturday Mornings ~ Cordae ft Lil Wayne 
***
This song is something you can call a coming of age tune.
I remember Cordae back when he was carried by Eminem and Jack Harlow. 
Now here he is saying everything he's gotten and all the knowledge he's gotten.
It's different from the empty bluffs and sayings in [\

](https://youtu.be/lTVqLUozo2E?si=H6rmGdE5J3X1-O-H), this one is with experience.
The addition of Lil Wayne was just a cherry on the top❤️✨

https://youtu.be/z2GYJua09F0?si=WoVqMofxikUDZAo6
***
That's my 3 rap songs chosen, listen and then listen against and then you'd understand what is so beautiful about them.

I wonder which song y'all like the best🔥

</center>
</liketuimages>

我现在几乎每天都会因为学习的问题和Sheya大吵一架。工作已经压得我喘不过气，回到家看到她的作业更是火冒三丈。一开始我都会尽力克制怒火，好好跟她沟通，可说不上几句，就会爆发一场争吵！

她今天带回了语文和数学两张单元随堂检测试卷。一般她不主动说分数，多半就考得不怎么样，果不其然，语文89分，数学83分。粗略一看，语文有一道3分的题空着没做，数学单页就扣了15分。我其实早有心理准备，对她的成绩也没抱太高期待，只是觉得她实在太不仔细，居然还会漏题。

我又翻看她的练习册，一个大大的C格外刺眼。题目结果是对的，但过程出错，十位加减时不知道补0。我问她：“这种题为什么错？知不知道为什么要加0？”她立刻很不耐烦：“我知道啊！只是没加0，我的结果是对的。”

这种不屑的态度让我很难接受。再看她刚做的一页，还是同样的问题：漏题、不补0。我让她先停下手里的事，她却像完全没听见，继续抄写语文。我伸手按住她的手，她直接对着我翻白眼。

这种不尊重人的行为已经不是第一次了。她成绩不理想我不强求，但这种自以为是、敷衍了事的态度问题很大。她平时做题反应慢、速度也慢，不会主动思考，不懂的题只会反复来问，做完也从不知道检查。

我稍微指出她的错误，她就不停反驳，甚至用谎言辩解。昨晚我想帮她重新讲一遍错题，讲完后问她：“我的方法可能和老师不一样，老师是怎么讲的？”她复述了一遍。我接着问：“既然老师这么讲，你为什么不用？”她接下来一句让我十分无语，居然改口说老师没讲过。简直自打嘴巴，让人又气又无奈。

我已经不知道该怎么跟她相处了。想让她成绩提升，首先要改的就是她的学习态度。我现在也不纠结别的，关键是她总觉得自己没错，认为只要结果对，过程就不重要。老师讲课的时候，她大概率根本没有认真听。这样下去，成绩根本不可能提高，我也越来越感到无力。

---

## Welcome to the Weekly Writing Prompt from The Ink Well
We provide *one weekly writing prompt* for short story writers. You may choose to use the prompt to write a fictional story (made up from your imagination) or a creative nonfiction story (based on your real life experiences). 

**IMPORTANT**: To be considered for curation, you *must* include one of these tags on your post:
* Fictional stories: #fiction
* Creative nonfiction stories: #creativenonfiction

You must also read and comment on the work of two other community members. Remember: We look for this when we curate your story. If we don't see this engagement, we will provide a reminder.

It is also *very* helpful to the admin team when authors add Fiction or Creative Nonfiction (or CNF for short) to the story title!

![TheInkWell Section Seperator.png](https://files.steempeak.com/file/steempeak/theinkwell/X4DfQH87-TheInkWell20Section20Seperator.png)


### Before You Post in The Ink Well
Be sure to check out our community rules before posting in this community. You can find them at the top of our [home page](https://peakd.com/c/hive-170798/created). They also appear at the top of a new post window.

Please also check out these additional helpful resources:
* Learn more about our community and the expectations of community members in our [FAQ post](https://peakd.com/hive-170798/@theinkwell/important-faqs-about-the-ink-well-dos-and-donts-rules-and-tips) and our [treasure trove of tips and guidelines](https://peakd.com/hive-170798/@theinkwell/the-ink-well-treasure-trove-of-tips-reminders-and-guidelines).
* Peruse our collection of great writing resources on everything from character development to how to write dialogue in our [catalog of storytelling tips](https://peakd.com/hive-170798/@theinkwell/catalog-of-fiction-writing-tips-from-the-ink-well). 
* Learn more about creative nonfiction, how it differs from fictional stories, and tips for success in [our post on creative nonfiction tips](https://peakd.com/hive-170798/@theinkwell/creative-nonfiction-what-it-is-and-tips-for-success).
* Remember that we are *always* about quality first. Never about *quantity.* To achieve awards in The Ink Well, take the time to write quality stories and check them for errors. See the topic of the month, \

in the [March 2025 newsletter](https://www.pexels.com/photo/woman-walking-alone-on-a-field-in-dense-fog-16254468/) to learn about using tools (and using them properly) if you are not already doing this. **We do notice when you don't take the time!**

![TheInkWell Section Seperator.png](https://files.steempeak.com/file/steempeak/theinkwell/X4DfQH87-TheInkWell20Section20Seperator.png)

## Last Week's Winning Story of the Week

Thank you to everyone who shared a story for the last prompt, \

!

Each week we pick one of our favorite stories of the week and award the author 5 Hive. 

And we have a winner! Congrats to @offia66 for his story [*This Place Doesn't Fix Anything, But It Helps*](https://peakd.com/hive-170798/@offia66/cnf-this-place-doesn-t). 

Here's what our curators had to say:

> @offia66 writes a simple, but meaningful piece about finding a quiet place in a life that is far too noisy. Life has been disappointing so far. Offia66 does not have the job he trained for. He is underpaid. His housing is cramped. He takes to sitting in an empty classroom for a few hours after his teaching duties are finished. He needs peace, time to collect his thoughts. The school's cleaning woman asks him why he is still in school. He explains his situation. Her response lifts his spirits and motivates him. She explains that his pay may be low but that he is a great teacher. He is motivating students who didn't care about math before. One of the those students is her son. After this conversation offia66 realizes there is value in what he does. He faces the coming days with greater optimism. Very nicely written.    

Congratulations, @offia66! 

![TheInkWell Section Seperator.png](https://files.steempeak.com/file/steempeak/theinkwell/X4DfQH87-TheInkWell20Section20Seperator.png)

## Short Story Writing Prompt of the Week

This week's prompt is: \

Whenever we meet people in life, we are subject to their opinions. Perhaps they make instant assumptions, based on our clothing, our skin color, how we travel about town, and other clues. But people do not really know us until they *take the time* to get to know us, do they?

With this prompt, you have the opportunity to explore this idea. What is the first impression a stranger has when they meet you — or your story character? Are they badly mistaken because of some initial impression, a way of dressing, or limited information?

If you want to write a *creative nonfiction story*, tell us about a time when you came to understand that a stranger's first impression was inaccurate, and did not represent who you really are.

If you want to write a *fictional story*, think about characters and situations where a person is judged by a stranger for their appearance, their tattoos, their station in life, or other factors that can *contribute* to who a person is, but do not necessarily *define* them.

As always, you do not need to actually use the prompt word(s). They are here to inspire your creativity!

We look forward to reading the product of your imagination or your personal experience! 

Good luck! And of course, you are welcome to use AI to generate ideas and images, but the writing must be *your own*! We do not accept stories that are AI-generated or heavily edited by AI. Only use tools like Grammarly to fix spelling and grammar issues.

Remember, as always, we are looking for the elements of *story*. These include: 

* Great first lines
* Good settings
* Well-developed characters
* Integration of action, dialogue and narrative
* A conflict that intrigues the reader
* A \

which results in the resolution of the conflict and brings the story to a satisfying conclusion
* And of course, we are looking for well-edited stories that are not littered with typos or grammatical errors — please use the free Grammarly tool for grammar and spelling checks (and not AI writing or rephrasing tools for revising)

You can find more on all of these topics in the [catalog of storytelling tips](https://peakd.com/hive-170798/@theinkwell/catalog-of-fiction-writing-tips-from-the-ink-well).

If you don't feel inspired by this prompt or the featured image, feel free to peruse any of our past prompts or our collection of idea-generators:

title.title: The end - El final
title.body:
> The end That afternoon, as the sun sank behind the hills of his small plot, he finished fitting the last beam of his cabin. There were no locks on the doors; in fact, there were no internal doors that could close against him. He sat at the table and gazed at the plate of vegetables he had grown himself, feeling the weight of the earth under his fingernails like a badge of honor. He remembered, as if they belonged to a stranger's life, the clang of metal against wood and the stifling silence of a coldly served dinner. But there, in his refuge of adobe and silence, the only sound was the wind through the furrows. For the first time in decades, he didn't have to ask permission to exist, nor give more than his own breath dictated. He ate slowly, in a solitude that didn't feel like emptiness, but like the finished house that finally inhabited his spirit.
El final Aquella tarde, mientras el sol se hundía tras las colinas de su pequeña parcela, él terminó de ajustar la última viga de su cabaña. No había cerraduras en las puertas; de hecho, no había puertas internas que pudieran cerrarse contra él. Se sentó a la mesa y observó el plato de hortalizas que él mismo había cultivado, sintiendo el peso de la tierra bajo sus uñas como una medalla de honor. Recordó, como si pertenecieran a la vida de un extraño, el estrépito del metal contra la madera y el silencio asfixiante de una cena servida con frialdad. Pero allí, en su refugio de adobe y silencio, el único ruido era el viento entre los surcos. Por primera vez en décadas, no tenía que pedir permiso para existir, ni dar más de lo que su propio aliento le dictaba. Comió despacio, en una soledad que no se sentía como un vacío, sino como la casa terminada que finalmente habitaba su espíritu.

(Kochi Meetha, Madre de Maya) Volandito ando con mis alpargatas de charol y mi son, de visita por esa linda comunidad #Music para traerles mis buenas vibras y una chispa que ilumine sus corazones. >

Believe it or not, I saw my first telenovela when I was studying at the agricultural school. One of my classmates had a small television and a tiny radio that only tuned into Radio Maturin. At home, we didn't watch telenovelas. My mother would give everyone a book, and our entertainment consisted of analyzing and discussing the book she gave us. We all love to read; it was instilled in us.

During a vacation, my mother enjoyed a telenovela called \
starring Amanda Gutiérrez and Daniel Alvarado, which aired on Venezolana de Televisión in 1984. In 1985, Venevisión broadcast \

(Channel of the Stars). From then on, we enjoyed and discussed telenovelas at home, especially Brazilian ones, as they were my mother's favorites. However, Venezuelan and Colombian telenovelas have also generated a lot of buzz.

For me, Brazilian telenovelas also set the standard, with current themes that are completely different from the traditional ones. I've seen several, but my favorites are: Pantanal, Isaura the Slave, The Clone, Terra Nostra, Xica da Silva, Doña Bella, Chocolate com Pimenta, and Camino de Indias, among others.

Of these telenovelas, I chose \

one of the most impactful because it portrays a culture quite different from Western society. However, it demonstrates that despite the customs, love and forgiveness always prevail. It also showcases the role of Western women, who can make their own decisions even when they make mistakes. \

was written by Gloria Pérez and directed by Marcos Schechtman.\n\nPremiering in Brazil in 2009, this telenovela tells the story of Maya, the protagonist, a woman deeply attached to tradition, gentle, and hardworking. Her parents want the best for her. Maya falls in love with Bahuan at first sight, but they belong to different castes. Later, she marries Raj and finds true love. It's a very good story. I'm sharing three songs from the soundtrack of the telenovela \
to participate in #Three Tune Tuesday with my friend @ablaze.

>

>![Spanish]
>
> Aunque no lo crean, vi mi primera telenovela cuando estudiaba en la escuela de agronomía, una de mis compañeras tenia una televisión pequeña y una radio equeña que solo sintonizaba Radio Maturin. En mi hogar no se veía telenovelas, a todos mami les ponía un libro en la mano y las horas de diversión era el análisis y opinión del libro que ella nos entregaba. A todos nosotros nos fascina leer, pues nos fue inculcado.
En unas vacaciones mami disfrutaba de una telenovela conocida como ”La Dueña”, con Amanda Gutiérrez y Daniel Alvarado, trasmitida por Venezolana de Televisión, en el año 1984. En año 1085 Venevisión trasmite “Tu o Nadie”, un éxito del “Canal de las estrellas”. A partir de allí, en casa disfrutábamos y comentábamos de telenovelas. Sobre todo de las brasileñas, pues eran las preferidas de mi madre. Sin embargo, las venezolanas y Colombianas han dado mucho que hablar. 
Para mi también las brasileñas marcan las pautas, con temas actuales y totalmente diferentes a las tradicionales. He visto varias pero mis preferidas: Pantanal, La esclava Isaura, El Clon, Terra Nostra, Xica Da Silva, Doña Bella, Chocolate con Pimenta, Camino de Indias, entre otras. 
De estas telenovelas seleccione a “Camino de Indias”, una de las que más me han impactado porque en ella se plasman una cultura opuesta a la sociedad occidental. Sin embargo, se  pone de manifiesto que a pesar de las costumbre;  el amor y el perdón siempre predominan por encima de todo. También muestra el papel de las mujeres occidentales, pues pueden tomar sus propias decisiones aun cuando cometan errores. “Camino de Indias” fue escrita por Glória Pérez y dirigida por Marcos Schechtman. 
Estrenada en Brasil en el año 2009. Vemos a Maya, la protagonista apegada a las costumbres, de carácter apacible y trabajadora. Con unos padres que desean lo mejor para ella. Maya se enamora de Bahuan a primera vista, pero pertenecen a castas diferentes.  Luego se casa con Raj y con el encuentra el amor verdadero. Es una trama muy buena. Les dejo tres canciones de la banda sonora de la telenovela “Camino de Indias” para participar en #Three tune Tuesday con el amigo @ablaze.

title.body:
**“Otoño”** está bien elegido y además lo aterrizas con una frase útil: **“Las hojas se vuelven rojas en otoño.”** Eso enseña vocabulario y contexto a la vez, que siempre vale más que una palabra suelta. La imagen también ayuda mucho porque fija la estación en la cabeza sin vueltas.

Un detalle fino: en inglés **“autumn”** y **“fall”** son correctos; **“autumn”** suena más estándar/internacional y **“fall”** más común en EE. UU. En español, **“otoño”** es directo y limpio, sin discusión. La idea de asociarlo con hojas rojas y amarillas encaja perfecto con usos comunes del término en materiales de aprendizaje como [Soy Guiri](https://blog.soyguiri.com/autumn-in-spanish) y [The Language Garage](https://thelanguagegarage.com/spanish-autumn-vocabulary/).

También me gusta que mantengas la serie diaria; **380 palabras ya no es una racha, es un sistema**. Eso tiene mucho más valor educativo que hacer posts “bonitos” sin continuidad.

Como contexto de tu propia línea de contenido, tu blog reciente sigue muy enfocado en aprendizaje y observación cotidiana, como este otro post de [@aljif7](https://inleo.io/@aljif7/when-pupils-speak-mental-math-memory-and-...); esa consistencia suma bastante.
